69.1
–– Diagnostics: Intense laboratory monitoring is 
the pillar of supportive care in HCT. Access to 
reliable round-the-clock laboratory services 
for blood counts, hemostasis tests, and com­
mon biochemical assessments are indispens­
able for establishing a successful HCT 
program (Aljurf et  al. 2019). A range of 
microbiological assessments including bacte­
rial and fungal cultures and antibiotic sensitiv­
ity assays are also essential. Viral infection 
monitoring, particularly for CMV in the con­
text of GVHD, is needed. Specialized radio­
logical evaluation is also frequently needed 
through experienced radiologists for ultra­
sound, CT scan, and MRI-based assessments.
–– Consultation services: In any ongoing HCT 
program, multisystem complications resulting 
from regimen-related toxicities, infections, or 
graft versus host disease are not uncommon. 
These require suitable consultation services to 
be available on call. Most commonly used ser­
vices are gastroenterology for endoscopies, 
nephrology for renal insufficiency, infectious 
diseases, and dermatology.
69.8	
Graft Versus Host Disease 
(GVHD) Management
–– Acute: This is one area where compromises 
are best avoided and standard protocols are 
followed depending on the type of donor and 
graft. Fortunately, most of the commonly used 
prophylactic drugs are widely available and 
not too expensive. Access to second-line drugs 
for steroid-resistant GVHD can be a challenge 
in some RCS and specific plans, and protocols 
should be in place to address these situations 
(Penack et  al. 2020). The success of haplo-­
identical HCTs with posttransplant cyclo­
phosphamide has made this an increasingly 
used option. This may also be useful in other 
donor HCTs and could make GVHD prophy­
laxis more cost-effective (Rimando et  al. 
2023).
–– Chronic: Extensive chronic GVHD can be one 
of the most difficult complications to manage 
in RCS because of the need for prolonged 
expensive immunosuppressive therapy and 
other associated complications (Saleem et al. 
2019). In the absence of adequate resources to 
support such care, this is a major cause of 
major morbidity and mortality. There are no 
specific low-cost protocols, and general prin­
ciples of the management of chronic GVHD 
also need to apply in RCS.

69.9	
Long-term Follow-Up
All HCT centers must aspire to have full long-­
term follow-up on all patients. An important 
aspect of achieving this goal is to provide ade­
quate information and counseling to the patient 
and their families regarding the importance and 
significance of such follow-up visits (Hashmi 
et al. 2018). Streamlining the assessments, a car­
ing attitude of the team toward the individual 
patient and offering relevant advice during such 
visits enhances compliance. However, given the 
paucity of HCT centers in RCS, patients often 
travel very long distances to have the HCT done 
and going back frequently for follow-up can be 
challenging. A hub and spoke model should be 
considered in those situations by establishing 
partnership with patients and local physicians for 
a shared care plan.
69.10	 Socioeconomic Issues
The major challenge that restricts access to HCT 
in RCS is the cost of HCT (Aljurf et al. 2019). 
What contributes heavily to costs are the drugs 
and disposables. These costs are variable 
­depending on where they are manufactured. It is 
important therefore that a facilitatory regulatory 
environment be created for such life-saving drugs 
and disposables to be made available and locally 
relevant prices. Human resource costs are often 
modest and usually in a structure that the health­
care system has learnt to accommodate. The low 
density of HCT services in most RCS around the 
world are related to two major reasons—cost and 
lack of adequately trained personnel who know 
how to innovate and establish such services 
within the local context. Both these need to be 
addressed (Aljurf et al. 2019).
69.11	 Conclusion
Creating greater awareness among healthcare 
professionals, comprehensive training programs 
and establishing appropriate infrastructure along 
with access to the required drugs and disposable 
combined with modifications and innovations in 
management protocols which are practical in 
those conditions are all needed to make HCT 
more widely available and accessible all over the 
world.

points: 建立移植計畫需配合當地疾病負擔、醫療網絡、人力與資源，分階段發展。
先確保細胞採集／處理、血品、微生物、藥品、急重症與訓練等基本能力。
可由較可行的 auto-HCT／相合同胞計畫逐步擴展至更複雜替代供者平台。
品質管理、資料登錄及結果回饋在資源有限處仍是核心，不能因預算而省略。
可近性、費用與病人長期支持需納入規劃，並結合國際合作。
question: 為何不能只添購設備就直接開展高複雜度移植？
answer: 安全執行仍依賴受訓人力、支援服務、標準流程與併發症救援能力，需逐步建立。
trap: 降低成本應改善流程，而非刪除基本安全能力。

69 資源受限環境下進行造血細胞移植之可行性與經驗 — Alok Srivastava、Fernando Barroso Duarte、Lawrence Faulkner
69.1 導論
儘管造血細胞移植（HCT）作為許多血液疾病的治癒性療法已盛行超過六十年，且在世界各地均呈上升趨勢（圖 69.1），但在中低收入國家（LMICs）的資源受限環境（RCSs）中，HCT 服務的密度仍然偏低，且取得現有服務仍是未被滿足的需求（Niederwieser et al. 2022）。不過，一線希望在於，在這些限制之下，已有數個國家運作著高品質 HCT 服務的諸多實例，其中部分中心更獲得完整的國家／國際認證，顯示即使在這些情況下，這也是可行的（Damodar et al. 2021）。本章的目標在於探討如何在資源受限環境（RCSs）中建立並維持良好的 HCT 服務（Pasquini et al. 2019; Faulkner et al. 2021）。
作者單位與聯絡資訊：

F. B. Duarte：巴西福塔雷薩塞阿拉聯邦大學／Hemoce 沃爾特．坎蒂迪奧大學醫院（Hospital Universitário Walter Cantídio, Universidade Federal do Ceara/Hemoce）；電子郵件：nutriquimio@uol.com.br。

【圖 69 各子圖、座標軸與圖例內容】
子圖 a — APBMT（1986–2016 年）：
• 子圖 A：
  – 縱軸（N，例數）：0、1,000、2,000、3,000、4,000、5,000、6,000

• 子圖 B：
  – 縱軸（N，例數）：0、100、200、300、400、500、600、700、800

  – 疾病類別圖例：實體腫瘤（Solid tumors）｜血紅素病變（Hemoglobinopathy）｜慢性骨髓性白血病（CML）

表 69.1 造血細胞移植（HCT）計畫的發展階段

欄位：［項目］｜第一階段（Stage I）｜第二階段（Stage II）｜第三階段（Stage III）

第 1 列 — 執行的移植類型（Types of transplantation performed）：
• 第一階段（Stage I）：
  – 自體移植（Autologous）
  – HLA 相合手足供者（HLA-matched sib donors）
• 第二階段（Stage II）：
  – 第一階段（Stage I）+
  – 所有相合手足供者（MSD）移植，包含不相合手足供者（MMSD）
  – 使用冷凍保存產品之自體移植（Autologous with cryopreserved products）
• 第三階段（Stage III）：
  – 第二階段（Stage II）+
  – 半相合移植（Haploidentical）
  – 及／或相合非親屬供者（MUD）、不相合非親屬供者（MMUD）
  – 及／或臍帶血（UCB）
  – 及／或去除 T 細胞（T-cell depleted）

第 2 列 — 造血細胞移植例數（Number of HCT）：
• 第一階段（Stage I）：
  – 每年 5 例自體 HCT（5 Auto-HCT/year）
  – 每年 3–5 例異體 HCT（3–5Allo-HCT/year）
• 第二階段（Stage II）：
  – 每年 10 例自體 HCT（10 Auto-HCT/year）
  – 每年 5–10 例異體 HCT（5–10 Allo-HCT/year）
• 第三階段（Stage III）：
  – 每年 >10 例自體 HCT（>10 Auto-HCT/year）
  – 每年 >10 例異體 HCT（>10 Allo-HCT/year）

腳註：
MMSD 表不相合手足供者（mismatched sibling donor），MSD 表相合手足供者（matched sibling donor），MMUD 表不相合非親屬供者（mismatched unrelated donor），MUD 表相合非親屬供者（matched unrelated donor），UCB 表臍帶血（umbilical cord blood），auto-HCT 表自體造血細胞移植（autologous hematopoietic cell transplant），allo-HCT 表異體造血細胞移植（allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant）。
出處：Transplantation and Cellular Therapy. 2021 Mar;27(3):267 e1–5。
69.2 建立 HCT 中心：人員／基礎設施／HCT 類型
所有 HCT 中心，即使在資源受限環境（RCS）內，最終都必須根據所服務患者的適應症，為兒科與成人患者提供全方位的 HCT 服務。然而，決定任何新設 HCT 服務重心與方向最關鍵的問題，在於主責移植醫師的訓練與經驗，以及能否取得各項支援基礎設施，近期來自孟加拉與尼泊爾的報告即為例證（Mahfuz et al. 2021; Poudyal et al. 2022）。雖然在政府資助的公立醫院提供 HCT 服務較為理想，但這在許多 RCS 並非成功的模式；正如同拉丁美洲的報告指出，當私立醫院提供服務時，HCT 的執行率反而矛盾地較高（Jaimovich et al. 2021）。在惡性腫瘤方面，自體 HCT 常是起步點，特別是在具備冷凍保存設施的情況下；惟多發性骨髓瘤除外，因其極短的調理療程不需要冷凍保存。然而，從異體 HCT 起步（特別是針對非惡性疾病，例如骨髓衰竭症候群、重度血紅素病變及免疫缺陷疾病）亦不罕見，且在兒童患者中預期可獲得極佳的成果，尤其是使用相合親屬供者（MRDs），但使用替代供者的比例亦日益增加。對於啟動 HCT 服務的這個層面，目前並無明確建議，唯一原則是主責醫師與團隊應針對其欲開展的服務接受充分訓練。表 69.1 列出一項建議做法。當然，這類醫師向其他發展更成熟中心之有經驗醫師尋求即時「會診諮詢」協助，是非常普遍的做法。
69.3 患者選擇與 HCT 適應症
對於在資源受限環境（RCS）中剛啟動計畫的中心而言，為 HCT 篩選患者可能面臨挑戰。一方面是罹患可藉由 HCT 治癒之疾病的個別患者（成人或兒童）的需求，另一方面則是可能希望優先處理特定適應症之 HCT 中心的能力與量能。最終的選擇取決於該中心的移植醫師與團隊、他們的經驗與訓練，以及機構的優先順序。建議從具有相合親屬供者的標準風險年輕患者開始——實際適應症將取決於所在的世界地區以及該中心的執業型態。鑑於 RCS 中 HCT 服務的匱乏，應認知到許多中心同時為成人與兒科患者提供服務（Chandy 2008; Benakli et al. 2020）。在這些 HCT 中心受訓的醫師，往往有能力處理廣泛患者族群與適應症的 HCT。當然，只要條件允許，移植團隊中必須有受過訓練的小兒科醫師。同樣重要的是，移植醫師必須了解不斷演進的 HCT 適應症，以及使用不同供者可能帶來的結果。在每一種情況下的預期結果，對於向患者及其家屬進行諮詢，以及規劃 HCT 所需資源均至關重要（Snowden et al. 2022）。
69.4 供者選擇：替代供者—移植物處理
在世界許多地區，難以取得當地可靠的 HLA 分型服務一直是阻礙異體移植開展的挑戰。隨著分子生物學 HLA 分型方法的普及，可取得的服務日益增加，進而能進行適當的供者選擇。一旦具備此項服務，相合親屬供者（MRDs）便成為啟動移植服務的首選。在近親通婚率高或種族血緣相近的地區，可能仍需要高解析度分型（Agarwal et al. 2017），且這也能啟動非親屬供者的配對搜尋。隨著經驗與資源的進步，以及移植物國際運輸物流的改善，相合非親屬供者（MUDs）的使用也日益增加。然而，隨著全球對半相合供者（HID）HCT 經驗的累積，視相關醫師與團隊的訓練和經驗，以及診斷與會診服務的可近性而定，這類供者移植可在 HCT 服務發展早期即提供（Niederwieser et al. 2022）。任何異體 HCT 服務的一個重要層面，是當遇到血型不相合供者而有需要時，至少有能力執行基本的移植物處理以去除紅血球。若無自動化儀器平台可用於此操作，則需熟悉手動離心或基於沉澱法的技術（Sawa et al. 2023）。
69.5 移植物採集：CD34+ 造血幹細胞劑量計算與冷凍保存問題
隨著周邊血幹細胞（PBSCs）用於異體移植物的比例日益增加，在大多數 HCT 中心，利用數種分離術（apheresis）平台之一來收集此類移植物相當容易建立。然而，使用 PBSC 移植物可能與移植物抗宿主疾病（GVHD）風險增加相關（特別是慢性 GVHD），因此移植醫師熟悉骨髓採集術非常重要。由於骨髓採集需要全身麻醉並使用手術室設施，這些層面也必須納入考量。移植物品質的評估（即便是 CD34+ 細胞計數）在許多中心都可能是一項限制；對此，通常可安排將此項評估外包。另一項常遇到的限制，則涉及移植物冷凍保存（主要用於自體 HCTs）的能力與量能。儘管有報告指出移植物在 4–8°C 下儲存長達 6 天後仍可使用（Bekadja et al. 2021），但為達到最佳的移植物儲存與移植結果，配備適當的程式降溫冷凍設備仍是較理想的做法。
69.6 調理方案
調理（conditioning）是任何 HCT 治療方案的關鍵環節，在骨髓清除性（myeloablative）與減低強度（reduced intensity）選項之間有多種可能性，可搭配各種具骨髓毒性與免疫抑制作用的藥物，並合併或不合併全身或較小範圍的放射線照射（Ma et al. 2020）。移植醫師必須熟悉這些可能性，並理解使用這些選項的原則，這一點非常重要。最終的選擇取決於當地可取得哪些藥物、是否具備放射治療設施，以及相關醫師的個人經驗。好消息是，幾乎對於所有 HCT 適應症，皆可採用各種以化學治療為基礎的調理方案並取得良好結果（Rehman et al. 2023）。調理方案相關毒性（regimen-related toxicities）可能是 HCT 發生併發症與死亡的主要原因，在選擇調理方案時應銘記這一點。
69.7 支持性照護
雖然疾病相關與患者個別相關變數是決定 HCT 結果的主要因素，但接下來對結果影響最大的，便是 HCT 期間所提供的支持性照護。這有兩個重要層面——第一是能否取得適當的治療藥品與血品（表 69.2），其次則是整個團隊運用這些產品的知識與訓練。將 HCT 各個層面的處置方案標準化，對於改善治療結果大有助益（Snowden et al. 2020）。在任何 HCT 計畫中，投入再多努力來強化護理、會診服務及相關診斷檢查方面的支持性照護，都不為過。
– 血品支持：能取得全方位的血庫產品（例如濃縮紅血球、血小板濃厚液及新鮮冷凍血漿），對於運作移植計畫而言絕對是不可或缺的（Warner et al. 2019）。免疫抑制患者所需的血品必須經過放射線照射，以避免輸血相關移植物抗宿主疾病（transfusion-associated GVHD）。當無專用血品照射儀時，亦可使用臨床鈷六十（Co60）遠距治療儀來照射紅血球與血小板血品（Goes et al. 2006）。若缺乏可隨時充足供應血品的大型血庫，在機構內的輸血服務部門設置分離術（apheresis）單位，並動員經篩檢的患者親屬及其他志願捐血者，是處理這項關鍵需求（特別是血小板輸注）的務實做法。

改編自：Transplantation and Cellular Therapy. 2021 Mar;27(3):267 e1–5。
– 免疫抑制劑：能取得相關的免疫抑制藥物，對於任何 HCT 計畫而言絕對是必要的（Penack et al. 2020）。常用藥物如鈣調磷酸酶抑制劑（calcineurin inhibitors，即 cyclosporin A 與 tacrolimus）、mycophenolate mofetil 及 sirolimus，加上 methylprednisolone，在大多數時候構成了處理 HCT 免疫併發症的基礎。移植後 cyclophosphamide（PTCy）是一項低成本的良好選擇，不僅適用於半相合供者（HID）移植，對於相合親屬供者（MRD）移植亦可能有益（Sawa et al. 2023）。在少數患者中，可能還需要用到包括生物製劑在內的廣泛其他藥物。測量藥物濃度對於確保療效至關重要（表 69.1）。
– 抗生素：鑑於抗微生物藥物抗藥性的廣泛程度（特別是在 RCS 中），能供應並取得多樣化的廣效性抗生素，對於啟動 HCT 服務而言絕對是不可或缺的。治療藥物監測（TDM）雖屬理想，但在大多數情況下並非絕對必要。然而，了解當地的抗微生物藥物抗藥性型態，對於制定抗生素治療方案非常重要（表 69.1）。
– 診斷檢查：密集的實驗室監測是 HCT 支持性照護的支柱。能取得全天候可靠運作的血球計數、止血功能檢測及常見生化評估實驗室服務，是建立成功 HCT 計畫不可或缺的條件（Aljurf et al. 2019）。一系列微生物學評估（包括細菌與黴菌培養以及抗生素敏感性試驗）同樣至關重要。此外，還需要進行病毒感染監測，特別是在 GVHD 情況下對巨細胞病毒（CMV）的監測。亦經常需要透過有經驗的放射科醫師進行超音波、電腦斷層掃描（CT）及磁振造影（MRI）等專業放射影像學評估。
– 會診服務：在任何運作中的 HCT 計畫裡，因調理方案相關毒性、感染或移植物抗宿主疾病所導致的多系統併發症並不少見。這需要有適當的專科會診服務隨時待命（on call）。最常使用的會診科別包括負責內視鏡檢查的胃腸肝膽科、負責腎功能不全的腎臟科，以及感染科與皮膚科。
69.8 移植物抗宿主疾病（GVHD）之處置
– 急性 GVHD：這是一個最應避免妥協的領域，應根據供者與移植物類型遵循標準治療方案。幸運的是，大多數常用的預防性藥物皆廣泛可得且價格不致過於昂貴。在某些 RCS 中，取得治療類固醇難治型（steroid-resistant）GVHD 的第二線藥物可能是一項挑戰，因此應預先制定具體計畫與方案來應對這些情況（Penack et al. 2020）。半相合 HCTs 搭配移植後 cyclophosphamide 的成功，使其成為日益普及的選擇；這在其他供者類型的 HCTs 中也可能有所助益，並可望使 GVHD 預防更具成本效益（Rimando et al. 2023）。
– 慢性 GVHD：廣泛性慢性 GVHD 可能是 RCS 中最難處理的併發症之一，因為患者需要長期且昂貴的免疫抑制治療，並伴隨其他相關併發症（Saleem et al. 2019）。在缺乏足夠資源支持此類照護的情況下，這是造成嚴重併發症與死亡的主要原因。目前並無特定的低成本治療方案，慢性 GVHD 處置的一般原則同樣必須應用於 RCS 中。
69.9 長期追蹤
所有 HCT 中心都必須以對所有患者進行完整長期追蹤為目標。達成此目標的一個重要層面，是向患者及其家屬提供充分的資訊與衛教諮詢，使其了解此類回診追蹤的重要性與意義（Hashmi et al. 2018）。精簡評估流程、團隊對個別患者展現關懷態度，並在回診期間提供切合需求的建議，皆有助於提升配合度（compliance）。然而，鑑於 RCS 中 HCT 中心稀少，患者往往需要長途跋涉才能接受 HCT，要頻繁返回中心追蹤可能相當困難。在這些情況下，應考慮採用「軸輻模式」（hub and spoke model），透過與患者及當地醫師建立夥伴關係，共同執行共享照護計畫（shared care plan）。
69.10 社會經濟問題
在資源受限環境（RCS）中，限制 HCT 可近性的主要挑戰是 HCT 的費用（Aljurf et al. 2019）。在費用中占極大比重的是藥品與一次性耗材，這些成本會因其製造地而異。因此，建立有利的法規環境，使這類救命藥品與耗材能以符合當地負擔能力的價格取得，至關重要。人力資源成本通常較為溫和，且往往已納入當地醫療照護體系所適應的結構中。全球大多數 RCS 的 HCT 服務密度偏低，主要與兩個原因有關——費用，以及缺乏受過充分訓練、懂得如何在當地脈絡下創新並建立此類服務的人員。這兩項問題都必須加以解決（Aljurf et al. 2019）。
69.11 結論
提升醫療專業人員的認知、建立全面的訓練計畫與適當的基礎設施、確保所需藥品與耗材的可近性，並結合在當地條件下切實可行的處置方案改良與創新，這些都是讓 HCT 在世界各地更廣泛普及且易於取得所不可或缺的要素。

AML in CR1
Jurjen Versluis and Jan J. Cornelissen
70.1.1	 Definition, Subtypes
AML is a malignancy of hematopoietic immature 
precursors (myeloblasts) that accumulate in the 
BM at the expense of their normal counterparts. 
AML is increasingly being recognized as a heter­
ogenous malignancy based on distinct disease 
biology and underlying cytogenetic and molecu­
lar profiles. Although a blast count of ≥20% in 
the BM or PB is still considered to diagnose 
AML, the 2022 World Health Organization

(WHO) 
classification 
and 
International 
Consensus Classification (ICC) considered a 
lower threshold to allow for disease-defining 
genetic abnormalities and to acknowledge the 
biologic continuum between MDS and AML 
(Khoury et al. 2022; Arber et al. 2022). A less 
strict definition of blast cutoff in the updated 
WHO classification and ICC emphasizes a com­
prehensive assessment of morphology, cytoge­
netic, and molecular genetic analyses to classify 
MDS and/or AML.
The ELN recommendations have also been 
updated in 2022, which stratified patients into 
three risk groups, including favorable risk, inter­
mediate risk, and adverse risk, based on pretreat­
ment cytogenetic abnormalities and gene 
mutations (Dohner et al. 2022). The ELN 2022 
further recognizes the underlying disease biology 
in its risk classification by adding a secondary 
type, MDS-associated mutations to the adverse-­
risk category (Dohner et al. 2022).
70.1.2	 Clinical Presentation
The median age at diagnosis is approximately 
70 years, and the annual age-standardized inci­
dence rate varies between 3 and 4 cases per 
100,000. Patients with AML typically present 
with symptoms such as fatigue, bruising, or 
infections, whereas lymphadenopathy and/or 
hepatosplenomegaly may be found by physical 
examination. Analysis of blood work often 
617

reveals thrombocytopenia, anemia, and/or neu­
tropenia. In some patients, a serious bleeding dia­
thesis can occur, particularly in the early phase of 
treatment, because the leukemic blasts are able to 
activate the coagulation cascade and cause 
hyperfibrinolysis.
70.1.3	 First-Line Treatment
Achieving and maintaining a first CR is crucial in 
AML patients, but treatment may largely fail 
because of relapse from CR rather than primary 
induction failure or treatment-related mortality 
(TRM). The standard intensive AML induction 
treatment has consisted of 7–10 days of the anti­
metabolite cytosine arabinoside (Ara-C) and 
3 days of an anthracycline (i.e., daunorubicin or 
idarubicin) since the 1980s. CR rates with stan­
dard induction estimate between 70 and 90%. 
Favorable-risk patients have relatively good out­
comes with overall survival rates of approxi­
mately 60–70%, whereas outcomes for patients 
with intermediate-risk and particularly adverse-­
risk AML remain unsatisfactory.
Targeted therapies have been introduced in 
AML, of which the kinase inhibitor midostaurin 
added to intensive induction and consolidation 
chemotherapy has been approved for first-line 
treatment of AML patients with mutated FLT3 
based on the survival benefit observed in the 
RATIFY trial (Stone et al. 2017). Other promis­
ing targeted therapies against FLT3 (e.g., gilteri­
tinib and quizartinib) or IDH1/2 mutations (e.g., 
ivosidenib and enasidenib) are currently being 
investigated in first-line intensive induction treat­
ment of which results are awaited. Alternative 
induction strategies might consist of gemtuzumab-­
ozogamicin, a humanized anti-CD33 antibody–
drug conjugate or CPX-351, a liposomal 
formulation of cytarabine and daunorubicin, for 
specific subgroups of patients. CPX-351 has been 
shown to improve overall outcome compared 
with standard intensive induction chemotherapy 
in patients aged 60–75 years with therapy-related 
or secondary-type AML, including MDS-related 
cytogenetic abnormalities (Lancet et al. 2018).
Treatment options have increased consider­
ably for AML patients deemed not eligible for 
intensive 
treatment 
to 
induce 
the 
first 
CR. Hypomethylating agents, including azacyti­
dine and decitabine, may be a treatment option in 
mono or combination therapy. Venetoclax, a 
BCL2 inhibitor, combined with azacitidine 
increased response rates, which were rapid and 
durable, and improved survival and quality of life 
compared with azacitidine alone (DiNardo et al. 
2020). As a result, azacitidine and venetoclax 
treatment has been established as the new stan­
dard of care for first-line treatment of older or 
unfit AML patients. Alternatively, for patients 
with mutated IDH1, ivosidenib combined with 
azacitidine was associated with higher response 
rates and superior survival compared with azacit­
idine alone in a randomized phase III trial 
(Montesinos et al. 2022). These targeted thera­
pies have different toxicity profiles compared 
with conventional chemotherapy and need spe­
cific monitoring of drug–drug interactions and 
adverse events such as cardiac QTc assessment, 
differentiation 
syndrome, 
and 
prolonged 
cytopenias.
Once a remission is being obtained, post-­
remission treatment decisions are directed by the 
ability of pretreatment features such as those 
incorporated in the ELN risk classification to pre­
dict outcome. However, probably more prognos­
tically important than the pretreatment features is 
response to treatment and especially the pres­
ence, in hematological remission, of measurable 
residual disease (MRD) as assessed by flow 
cytometry or targeted quantitative PCR for spe­
cific markers.
70.1.4	 HCT and AML Risk Categories

Similar to the previous risk classification, the 
ELN 2022 AML risk classification is advocated 
to be used for risk-stratifying AML and to a risk-­
adapted treatment approach for patients with 
AML.  Such a risk-adapted treatment approach 
for patients with AML depends not only on the 
risk of relapse of the underlying AML but also on 
the risk of TRM associated with the applied post-­
remission treatment. The application of MRD, 
detected by either multiparametric flow cytome­
try or quantitative PCR for specific molecular 
markers may further improve AML risk classifi­
cations. MRD may be detected at time points

Consequently, MRD negativity has been intro­
duced as an end point in patients with a hemato­
logical CR (Dohner et al. 2017).
70.1.4.2	
Transplantion Risk 
Categories
The risk-adapted approach of patients with AML 
in the first CR should also include the assessment 
of TRM for each individual patient. TRM may be 
attributed to GVHD, infectious complications, 
organ toxicity, and other causes (Penack et  al. 
2020). A number of parameters may relate to 
allo-HCT-related mortality, including the proce­
dure (e.g., conditioning regimen and application 
of TCD), donor characteristics (e.g., HLA-­
matching), and recipient features (e.g., age and 
comorbidity). The risk of mortality may be quan­
tified by composite risk scores, which have been 
established to predict TRM and overall outcome.
Two generally approved transplant risks were 
developed and validated, including the EBMT 
risk score (Gratwohl et al. 1998) and the hema­
topoietic cell transplantation-comorbidity index 
(HCT-CI) (Sorror et al. 2005). The EBMT risk 
score is based on patient and transplantation 
characteristics, which was developed in CML 
patients and subsequently validated in other 
patient groups including AML (Gratwohl et al. 
2009). The HCT-CI consists of 17 comorbidities 
that contribute to a cumulative score, which has 
been extensively validated and continuously 
being refined, including age, disease status, or 
biomarkers (Sorror et  al. 2007, 2014). A 
machine-based learning model was developed 
by the EBMT-acute leukemia working party 
(ALWP) based on 10 variables, which was 
highly predictive of mortality at 100 days and 
2 years (Shouval et al. 2015). Other groups have 
also developed predictive models for TRM 
modifying the weights of the EBMT risk score 
and the HCT-CI (Barba et  al. 2010), whereas 
others combined transplant-related parameters 
and patient characteristics or used biomarkers 
(Parimon et  al. 2006; Barba et  al. 2014; Luft 
et al. 2017).
Developments 
in 
allo-HCT 
care 
have 
improved outcomes over the last decades, attrib­
utable to for example the introduction of reduced 
intensity conditioning, improved supportive care 
and infectious prophylaxis, and better GVHD 
prophylaxis or GVHD treatment. Consequently, 
TRM has been strongly reduced and the use of 
allo-HCT as post-remission treatment for older 
or less fit patients with comorbidities has 
increased (Snowden et al. 2022). Several groups 
have reported less predictive power of the estab­
lished TRM risk models in the current era of allo-­
HCT. The EBMT-ALWP has developed updated 
scoring systems applicable to the setting of RIC 
in older patients with AML and PTCY as GVHD 
prophylaxis which both had increased predictive 
power (Versluis et al. 2015; Hermans et al. 2023). 
Similar to updating AML risk classifications, the 
prediction of TRM also needs ­continued refine­
ment and reassessment in specific patient groups 
and novel treatments.
70.1.5	 HCT in First-Line AML 
Treatment: A Risk-Adapted 
Approach

et  al. 2012b; Cornelissen and Blaise 2016). 
Table 70.1 summarizes a risk-­adapted approach 
based on the ELN 2022 AML risk classification, 
MRD status, and the risk for TRM. The risk for 
TRM should be preferably assessed with dedi­
cated scores for specific subgroups of patients.
Allo-HCT is generally not indicated in 
patients with a favorable AML risk profile; for 
those patients auto-HCT or continued chemo­
therapy may be preferred (Cornelissen et  al. 
2012b; Cornelissen and Blaise 2016; Dohner 
et  al. 2022). However, favorable-risk patients 
with MRD are considered high risk for relapse 
and preferably receive an allo-HCT in the first 
CR, unless excessive TRM is predicted even 
with RIC.
Results of allo-HCT compared with non-allo-­
HCT post-remission therapies have yielded con­
tradicting results in intermediate-risk patients, 
especially taking molecular markers into account 
(Koreth et al. 2009; Stelljes et al. 2014; Versluis 
et  al. 2017b). A risk-adapted AML trial which 
allocated patients with MRD negative, intermedi­
ate-risk AML to auto-HCT, whereas intermedi­
ate-risk patients with MRD positivity received 
allo-HCT, showed similar outcomes for auto-
HCT and allo-HCT (Venditti et  al. 2019). 
Consequently, assessment of MRD status is 
strongly advocated for post-­remission treatment 
decisions in patients with an intermediate-risk 
AML. Allo-HCT may be applied in patients with 
intermediate-risk AML with MRD after induc­
tion chemotherapy, except for patients with a 
high risk for TRM. Allo-HCT might also be con­
sidered for patients with intermediate risk, MRD 
negative AML, but auto-HCT and chemotherapy 
are alternative treatment options, particularly 
when the predicted risk for TRM is high.
Adverse-risk patients with MRD should be 
transplanted with an allograft as soon as a 
hematological CR is obtained. Adverse-risk 
patients without MRD still have a significant 
risk of relapse and are also candidates for allo-
HCT, although patients with a very high risk 
for TRM may be considered for non-allo-HCT 
approaches.
70.2	
Allo-HCT in Advanced AML
Charles Craddock
70.2.1	 Introduction
Allo-HCT plays an increasingly important role in 
the management of AML in adults (Dohner et al. 
2022). The advent of RIC regimens coupled with 
increased donor availability has dramatically 
increased the number of patients in whom allo-
HCT can be contemplated. At the same molecu­
lar characterization at diagnosis coupled with 
MRD, quantitation after induction chemotherapy 
has considerably improved our ability to predict 
relapse risk in patients treated with intensive che­
motherapy alone refining our ability to identify 
patients with the potential to benefit from alloge­
neic 
transplantation 
(Loke 
et 
al. 
2020). 
Consequently, allo-HCT is now a pivotally 
important personalized component of the treat­
ment algorithm in adults with AML in CR1. At 
the same time, there is an emerging recognition 
of the curative potential of allografting in patients 
with advanced-phase AML, particularly patients 
with primary refractory (PREF) AML (Dohner 
et al. 2022). It is therefore extremely important 
that all fit adults with newly diagnosed AML are 
tissue typed at presentation and, unless there are 
compelling reasons to believe allo-HCT will not 
be included in the patients’ treatment algorithm, 
a donor search is commenced in a timely manner. 
Encouraging results have been achieved using 
both matched sibling and volunteer unrelated 
donors and more recently transplantation using 
haploidentical donors (in conjunction with post-­
transplant cyclophosphamide GVHD prophy­
laxis) and cord blood units with a high nucleated 
cell dose. To date, there is no compelling data 
concerning whether there is an optimal stem cell 
source and prospective studies are required to 
address this important point. In both patients 
transplanted in CR1 and those with advanced 
phase disease, there has been a substantial reduc­
tion in transplant-related mortality (TRM) over 
the decades, but the risk of disease relapse post­

transplant remains stubbornly high and now 
­represents the major cause of treatment failure in 
patients allografted for AML.  There remains, 
therefore, an urgent requirement to develop novel 
strategies with the potential to reduce the risk of 
disease recurrence in all patients allografted for 
AML.
70.2.2	 The Role of Allo-HCT 
in the Management 
of Primary Refractory AML
Ten to forty percent of adults with newly diag­
nosed AML have PREF AML defined as a fail­
ure to achieve a morphological CR after two 
courses of intensive induction chemotherapy, 
including at least one cycle of intermediate dose 
cytarabine (Ferguson et al. 2016). Factors deter­
mining refractoriness to induction chemother­
apy include adverse disease biology and patient 
age. Patients with PREF AML have genuinely 
chemo-­refractory disease with long-term sur­
vival rates <10% if treated with further chemo­
therapy, and allo-HCT represents the only 
treatment modality with the potential to deliver 
long-term disease-­free survival. Evidence that 
allo-HCT can deliver long-term survival in a 
significant proportion of patients with PREF 
AML has been accumulating over the last 
decade and represents an important advance in 
the management of this sizeable patient popula­
tion for whom no other effective therapy exists 
(Craddock et  al. 2011; Todisco et  al. 2017; 
Brissot et  al. 2017; Boyiadzis et  al. 2023). 
Nonetheless, outcomes in patients allografted 
for PREF AML remain unsatisfactory, and both 
TRM and disease relapse continue to represent 
significant barriers to long-term survival. There 
is also a lack of clarity concerning which 
patients with PREF AML are the most likely to 
benefit from transplantation. Outcome is supe­
rior in patients who proceed swiftly to trans­
plant after no more than two courses of intensive 
chemotherapy, and relapse appears to be lower 
in those with a lower burden of disease at the 
time of transplantation. It is therefore important 
to consider transplant as a potentially curative 
treatment modality in fit patients with PREF 
AML, providing a suitable donor can be identi­
fied rapidly and the predicted TRM is accept­
able. However, further studies both on the 
impact of disease biology and evidence of 
chemo-­responsiveness on outcome after allo-
HCT are required if we are to be able to identify 
with greater clarity both which patients with 
PREF AML are likely to benefit from allo-HCT 
and equally for whom this further intensification 
in treatment is unlikely to deliver long-term sur­
vival. At present, accumulating data identifies 
very poor outcomes for patients with high-risk 
molecular features such as the presence of a 
TP53 mutation or inv(3)(q21.3q26.2) and on the 
basis of current knowledge it is probably rea­
sonable to reserve allogeneic transplantation in 
this patient group for patients who have achieved 
a morphological CR (Loke et  al. 2022; Daver 
et al. 2022; Badar et al. 2023).
The optimal conditioning regimen in patients 
with PREF AML remains a matter of conjecture, 
but it is recommended that a myeloablative regi­
men is utilized in patients under the age of 
50 years unless there are compelling reasons to 
the contrary. In older adults, there is no evidence 
that any particular RIC regimen is to be favored. 
Although encouraging results using a FLAMSA 
sequential regimen were reported in patients with 
PREF AML, it is relevant to note that a recent 
randomized trial failed to demonstrate any bene­
fit of such a regimen compared with the standard 
RIC regimen FB2 in adults with AML in CR1 or 
CR2, although insufficient patients with PREF 
AML were randomized to address whether this 
regimen has particular activity in this clinical set­
ting (Craddock et al. 2021). As with all patients 
allografted for high-risk AML, it is important to 
assess response to transplant by performing 
MRD studies on a bone marrow aspirate 
30–45 days posttransplant, since this may guide 
the implementation of an early immunosuppres­
sion taper or use of prophylactic/pre-emptive 
donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) (Loke et  al. 
2023).

70.3	
Practical Issues for Allo-HCT 
in AML
Arnon Nagler
AML is the most frequent indication in Europe 
for allogeneic HCT. As per the latest publication 
by Passweg et al., 7123 allo-HCT has been per­
formed in Europe in 2021 for AML (4266 for de 
novo AML in the first CR, 1775 for de novo AML 
not in CR, and 1082 for AML-therapy-related or 
myelodysplasia-related changes) accounting for 
38% of the allogeneic transplant activity in 
Europe (Passweg et al. 2021). In sharp contrast to 
the lymphatic malignancies, the allogeneic activ­
ity in AML has not been decreased as CAR-T cell 
treatment for AML is still in its infancy (Passweg 
et al. 2021). As in many of the AML patients with 
an indication for allo-HCT, transplant is currently 
the only curative procedure and in those achieving 
CR after first induction results are better. It is 
therefore recommended to perform HLA typing 
of the patient and the potential family donors 
upfront once the AML is diagnosed and to start a 
search (Carreras et al. 2019). In recent years, con­
tinuous novel developments in the field of allo-
HCT and mainly the reduced intensity/reduced 
toxicity conditioning and haploidentical donor 
allo-HCT with post-transplant cyclophosphamide 
(PTCY) have significantly reduced transplant-
related toxicities and mortality combined with the 
improved supportive care (Slavin et  al. 1998; 
Kasamon et  al. 2015; Shimoni et  al. 2005). 
Consequently, the median age of the AML patients 
that are undergoing transplantations is increasing 
with many of the transplanted patients being over 
60 years or even 65 years of age. Many of these 
patients are receiving the allo-­HCT following 
upfront induction with low-­intensity Venetoclax-
based protocols which further reduced toxicities 
(Dohner et al. 2022; Keith et al. 2022). Achieving 
measurable residual disease (MRD) negativity, 
pre-allo-HCT correlates with outcomes and 
becomes a major goal in the treatment paradigm 
for acute leukemias and other hematological 
malignancies as well (Keith et al. 2022; Abhishek 
et al. 2021; Bazinet et al. 2023). Most of the allo-
HCTs that are being performed nowadays are 
from unrelated including mismatched unrelated 
and haploidentical donors and with mobilized 
PBSC (Nagler and Mohty 2022; Arslan and Al 
Malki 2022; Anasetti et al. 2012; Raghunandan 
2022). Patients with a high risk of relapse post-
allo-HCT including those with high-risk AML, 
secondary poor prognostic mutations, or second­
ary AML should be considered for maintenance 
or preemptive therapy post-allo-HCT in an 
attempt to reduce the relapse rates (Eshrak et al. 
2023). Finally, PTCY-­based regimens are becom­
ing the preferred mode of GVHD prophylaxis 
including for patients with AML undergoing 
HLA-matched related, unrelated, and haploiden­
tical allo-HCT, and it may change other aspects of 
allo-HCT including the intensity of the condition­
ing as well as the risk of relapse post-transplanta­
tion (Bolanos-Meade et al. 2023).
70.4	
Acute Promyelocytic 
Leukemia
Miguel Á. Sanz
70.4.1	 Concept and Incidence
APL is a subtype of AML with peculiar clinical 
and morphological characteristics, which pres­
ents a specific genetic alteration, the t (15; 17), 
with its corresponding molecular counterpart, the 
rearrangement PML-RARA, which confer a par­
ticular sensitivity to all-trans retinoic acid 
(ATRA) and arsenic trioxide (ATO). It also high­
lights the presence of a hemorrhagic diathesis 
associated with a peculiar coagulopathy, which 
causes a high incidence of hemorrhagic compli­
cations at presentation and early during the 
induction treatment.
APL accounts for 5–15% of AML, with a 
median age of around 40 years and similar distri­
bution by sex. About 10% occur after the use of 
cytotoxic drugs (especially topoisomerase II 
inhibitors) or radiation.

70.4.3	 First-Line Treatment
The ELN recommendations in 2009 acknowl­
edged the promising outcomes reported in sev­
eral non-randomized studies using ATRA plus 
ATO, with or without minimal use of chemother­
apy, but the standard of care remained the combi­
nation of ATRA plus anthracycline-based 
chemotherapy (Sanz et  al. 2009). However, 
recent findings have led to modify this recom­
mendation in the updated ELN guidelines (Sanz 
et al. 2019).
The long-term results of a non-randomized 
study (Abaza et  al. 2017) and two randomized 
clinical trials (Lo-Coco et al. 2013; Burnett et al. 
2015), comparing the efficacy and safety of 
ATRA plus ATO versus the standard ATRA plus 
chemotherapy approach, strongly support the 
former combination as the new standard of care 
for low-to-intermediate-risk APL patients with 
WBC counts lower than 10 × 109/L at presenta­
tion. Nevertheless, in countries where chemo­
therapy is more affordable than ATO, the classical 
combination of ATRA and chemotherapy remains 
an acceptable option. For high-risk patients, how­
ever, there are two valid options, either ATRA 
plus chemotherapy or ATRA plus ATO with a 
certain amount of cytoreductive chemotherapy, at 
least during the induction phase.
HCT is never indicated in patients in CR1, 
except for the small fraction of patients with per­
sistent RQ-PCR positivity of PML-RARA after 
consolidation (<1%), given the poor prognosis 
associated with this subset. HCT is also indicated 
in APL patients who relapse and achieve second 
or subsequent CR.
70.4.4	 Salvage Therapy
Apart from patients with MRD positivity at the 
end of consolidation (molecular persistence), 
there is a consensus that patients experiencing 
molecular or hematological relapse later on 
require immediate additional treatment, includ­
ing HCT.  The goal of salvage treatment is to 
achieve molecular remission as a bridge to 
HCT. In cases where ATRA plus chemotherapy 
was the frontline therapy, salvage treatment with 
ATRA plus ATO is recommended. Conversely, if 
frontline therapy involves ATRA plus ATO, 
ATRA plus chemotherapy is the preferred option.
The use of gemtuzumab ozogamicin may also 
be considered in both situations, but always as a 
bridge to HCT.  Various studies (Yanada et  al. 
2013; Holter Chakrabarty et al. 2014; Lengfelder 
et  al. 2015) suggest that auto-HCT should be 
considered the first choice for eligible patients 
achieving a second molecular remission. Patients 
who are unsuitable for HCT or have a very pro­
longed CR1 can be managed with some mainte­
nance 
therapy, 
which 
would 
be 
chosen 
considering previous treatments and clinical 
condition.
Allo-HCT should be reserved for patients with 
a high risk of relapse and low risk of TRM, but 
also as a second option for patients who relapse 
after an auto-HCT.

zh: 成人急性骨髓性白血病 AML
points: CR1 是否 allo-HCT，需平衡疾病復發風險與預估 TRM／NRM，並整合分子、細胞遺傳與 MRD。
有利風險且良好 MRD 反應者，與不利風險／MRD 持續者的策略不同。
Primary refractory AML 仍可能從 allo-HCT 獲得治癒機會，但須迅速取得供者並接受其毒性風險。
前處理強度與疾病負荷共同影響復發；移植後可依靶點評估維持或先發治療。
APL 的移植情境特殊：分子緩解後 CR2 常考慮 auto-HCT；持續分子陽性或自體移植後復發等情境才評估 allo-HCT。
question: 所有 AML 在 CR1 都應接受 allo-HCT 嗎？
answer: 不是。需依 ELN／分子風險、MRD、替代療法及 NRM 綜合決定。
trap: 移植適應症是復發風險與治療風險的平衡。
fullTranslationText:
70 成人急性骨髓性白血病（AML） — Jurjen Versluis、Jan J. Cornelissen、Charles Craddock、Miguel Á. Sanz、Arnon Nagler
70.1 第一完全緩解期（CR1）之急性骨髓性白血病（AML）
Jurjen Versluis 與 Jan J. Cornelissen

70.1.1 定義與亞型
急性骨髓性白血病（AML）是一種造血未成熟前驅細胞（骨髓母細胞，myeloblasts）的惡性腫瘤，這些細胞在骨髓（BM）中大量累積並排擠正常造血細胞。基於截然不同的疾病生物學特性以及潛在的細胞遺傳學與分子特徵，AML 日益被認為是一種高度異質性的惡性腫瘤。儘管骨髓（BM）或周邊血（PB）中母細胞（blast）比例 ≥20% 仍被視為診斷 AML 的標準，但 2022 年世界衛生組織（WHO）分類與國際共識分類（ICC）皆納入了較低的母細胞門檻，以涵蓋具疾病定義性的遺傳異常，並肯認骨髓化生不良症候群（MDS）與 AML 之間的生物學連續性（Khoury et al. 2022；Arber et al. 2022）。更新版 WHO 分類與 ICC 對母細胞切點採取較不僵化的定義，強調結合形態學、細胞遺傳學與分子遺傳學分析進行綜合評估，以對 MDS 及／或 AML 作出分類。
歐洲白血病網（ELN）建議亦於 2022 年更新，根據治療前的細胞遺傳學異常與基因突變，將患者分為三個風險群組：預後良好（favorable risk）、中度風險（intermediate risk）與預後不良（adverse risk）（Dohner et al. 2022）。2022 年版 ELN 風險分類進一步反映潛在的疾病生物學特性，將次發型（secondary-type）、MDS 相關基因突變納入預後不良（adverse-risk）類別（Dohner et al. 2022）。
70.1.2 臨床表現
診斷時的中位年齡約為 70 歲，每年年齡標準化發生率介於每 10 萬人 3 至 4 例之間。AML 患者典型表現包括疲倦、瘀斑或感染等症狀，理學檢查則可能發現淋巴結腫大及／或肝脾腫大。血液檢查分析常
作者單位：Jurjen Versluis（通訊作者）、Jan J. Cornelissen — 荷蘭鹿特丹伊拉斯姆斯醫學中心癌症研究所血液科；e-mail: j.versluis.1@erasmusmc.nl; j.cornelissen@erasmusmc.nl。Charles Craddock — 英國伯明罕大學醫院 NHS 信託及華威大學臨床血液學中心；e-mail: charles.craddock@uhb.nhs.uk。Miguel Á. Sanz — 西班牙瓦倫西亞大學拉費大學醫院血液科；e-mail: Miguel.Sanz@uv.es。Arnon Nagler — 以色列 Tel-Hashomer 希巴醫療中心（Chaim Sheba Medical Center）血液與骨髓移植科；e-mail: arnon.nagler@sheba.health.gov.il。
顯示血小板低下、貧血及／或嗜中性白血球低下。部分患者可能出現嚴重的出血傾向（特別是在治療初期），因為白血病母細胞能活化凝血連鎖反應並引起過度纖維蛋白溶解（hyperfibrinolysis）。
70.1.3 第一線治療
在 AML 患者中，達成並維持第一完全緩解（CR1）至關重要；然而治療失敗的主要原因往往是自完全緩解（CR）後復發，而非原發性誘導失敗或治療相關死亡率（TRM）。自 1980 年代以來，標準高強度 AML 誘導治療包含 7–10 天的抗代謝藥物 cytosine arabinoside（Ara-C，阿糖胞苷）加上 3 天的蔥環類藥物（anthracycline，即 daunorubicin 或 idarubicin）。標準誘導治療的 CR 率估計介於 70% 至 90% 之間。預後良好風險（favorable-risk）患者的預後相對較佳，整體存活率（OS）約為 60–70%；然而中度風險（intermediate-risk）與特別是預後不良風險（adverse-risk）AML 患者的治療結果仍不理想。
標靶治療已引進 AML 治療領域，其中激酶抑制劑 midostaurin 併用高強度誘導及鞏固化學治療，基於 RATIFY 試驗觀察到的存活效益，已獲核准作為帶有 FLT3 突變之 AML 患者的第一線治療（Stone et al. 2017）。其他針對 FLT3（例如 gilteritinib 與 quizartinib）或 IDH1/2 突變（例如 ivosidenib 與 enasidenib）的具潛力標靶藥物，目前正於第一線高強度誘導治療中進行研究，結果尚待揭曉。針對特定患者亞群的替代誘導策略，可能包括人源化抗 CD33 抗體藥物複合體 gemtuzumab-ozogamicin，或 cytarabine 與 daunorubicin 的脂質體製劑 CPX-351。研究已證實，在 60–75 歲患有治療相關或次發型 AML（包含帶有 MDS 相關細胞遺傳學異常）的患者中，CPX-351 相較於標準高強度誘導化療能改善整體預後（Lancet et al. 2018）。
對於經評估不適合接受高強度誘導治療以取得第一次 CR 的 AML 患者，治療選擇已大幅增加。去甲基化藥物（hypomethylating agents，包括 azacitidine 與 decitabine）可作為單一藥物或合併治療的選擇。BCL2 抑制劑 venetoclax 併用 azacitidine 相較於單用 azacitidine，不僅能提高反應率（且反應迅速而持久），亦改善了存活率與生活品質（DiNardo et al. 2020）。因此，azacitidine 併用 venetoclax 已確立為年長或不耐受強效化療（unfit）之 AML 患者第一線治療的新標準照護。此外，針對帶有 IDH1 突變的患者，在一項隨機分配第三期臨床試驗中，ivosidenib 併用 azacitidine 相較於單用 azacitidine 具有更高的反應率與更優異的存活率（Montesinos et al. 2022）。這些標靶治療具有與傳統化學治療不同的毒性表現，需要特別監測藥物交互作用與不良事件，例如心電圖 QTc 評估、分化症候群（differentiation syndrome）以及延遲性血球低下。
一旦取得緩解，緩解後治療決策取決於治療前特徵（例如納入 ELN 風險分類中的各項指標）預測預後的能力。然而，在預後判斷上可能比治療前特徵更為重要的，是對治療的反應，特別是在達到血液學緩解時，以流式細胞儀或針對特定標記之定量聚合酶連鎖反應（PCR）所評估的可測量殘存疾病（MRD）是否存在。
70.1.4 造血細胞移植（HCT）與 AML 風險分類
70.1.4.1 AML 風險分類
過去 2017 年版 ELN 的 AML 患者風險分類納入了傳統細胞遺傳學以及 NPM1、FLT3-ITD、CEBPA、RUNX1、ASXL1 與 TP53 等基因突變（Dohner et al. 2017）。目前的 2022 年版 ELN 風險分類則新增了 BCOR、
EZH2、SF3B1、SRSF2、STAG2、U2AF1 及／或 ZRSR2 基因突變，這些突變被認定為具不良預後的 MDS 相關突變（表 70.1）（Dohner et al. 2022）。其他重要變更包括：(1) 分類中不再考量 FLT3-ITD 等位基因比率（allelic ratio）；(2) 目前僅將 CEBPA 的 bZIP 區域內框內突變（in-frame mutations）視為預後良好風險，無論為單等位基因或雙等位基因突變；(3) 若同時存在預後不良的細胞遺傳學異常，NPM1 突變不再歸類為預後良好；(4) 復發性細胞遺傳學異常包括 t(3q26;v) 或 t(8;16)(p11.2;13.3) 被納入預後不良風險群組；(5) 超二倍體核型（hyperdiploid karyotypes）不被視為複雜核型；以及 (6) 僅變異等位基因分率（VAF）≥10% 的 TP53 突變被視為預後不良風險。
與先前的風險分類相同，臨床上倡議使用 2022 年版 ELN 之 AML 風險分類對 AML 進行風險分層，並據以採取依風險調整（risk-adapted）的 AML 治療策略。此種依風險調整的治療策略不僅取決於潛在 AML 的復發風險，亦取決於所採用緩解後治療伴隨的治療相關死亡率（TRM）風險。透過多參數流式細胞儀或針對特定分子標記之定量 PCR 檢測可測量殘存疾病（MRD），可望進一步完善 AML 風險分類。MRD 可在多個時間點進行檢測：
表 70.1 第一完全緩解期（CR1）AML 患者依風險調整之緩解後治療ª

• CEBPA 之 bZIP 區域框內突變（bZIP in-frame mutated CEBPA）
  - MRD 陰性（Negative）：化學治療／自體 HCT（auto-HCT）

• 野生型 NPM1 且無 FLT3-ITD（無預後不良遺傳病灶）

• 未歸類為預後良好或預後不良之細胞遺傳學及／或分子異常

70.1.4.2 移植風險分類
針對處於第一完全緩解期（CR1）的 AML 患者採取依風險調整策略時，亦應納入對個別患者治療相關死亡率（TRM）的評估。TRM 可能歸因於移植物抗宿主疾病（GVHD）、感染併發症、器官毒性及其他原因（Penack et al. 2020）。多項參數與異體 HCT 相關死亡率有關，包括移植程序（例如預處理方案與 T 細胞去除術［TCD］的應用）、捐贈者特徵（例如 HLA 相合度）以及受贈者特徵（例如年齡與共病症）。死亡風險可透過綜合風險評分加以量化，這些評分系統已被確立用於預測 TRM 與整體預後。
目前有兩種廣獲認可的移植風險評分系統已完成開發與驗證，包括 EBMT 風險評分（Gratwohl et al. 1998）與造血細胞移植共病指數（HCT-CI）（Sorror et al. 2005）。EBMT 風險評分係依據患者與移植特徵所建立，最初於慢性骨髓性白血病（CML）患者中開發，隨後在包括 AML 在內的其他患者群體中獲得驗證（Gratwohl et al. 2009）。HCT-CI 包含 17 項共病症並計算累積分數，已獲廣泛驗證且持續改良，後續亦整合了年齡、疾病狀態或生物標記（Sorror et al. 2007, 2014）。EBMT 急性白血病工作小組（ALWP）亦根據 10 項變數開發出機器學習模型，對移植後 100 天與 2 年死亡率具高度預測力（Shouval et al. 2015）。其他研究團隊也透過調整 EBMT 風險評分與 HCT-CI 的權重開發出預測 TRM 的模型（Barba et al. 2010），另有團隊則結合移植相關參數與患者特徵或採用生物標記進行預測（Parimon et al. 2006；Barba et al. 2014；Luft et al. 2017）。
過去數十年間，異體 HCT 照護的發展改善了治療結果，這可歸功於減低強度預處理（RIC）的引進、支持性照護與感染預防的進步，以及更完善的 GVHD 預防或治療。因此，TRM 已大幅降低，且將異體 HCT 作為年長或體能較差且具共病症患者之緩解後治療的應用也有所增加（Snowden et al. 2022）。數個研究團隊指出，在當今異體 HCT 時代，既有 TRM 風險模型的預測力有所下降。EBMT-ALWP 已開發出適用於年長 AML 患者接受 RIC 移植以及使用移植後 cyclophosphamide（PTCY）作為 GVHD 預防之情境的更新版評分系統，兩者皆提升了預測能力（Versluis et al. 2015；Hermans et al. 2023）。如同 AML 風險分類的更新，TRM 的預測亦需針對特定患者群體與新型療法持續加以精進與重新評估。
70.1.5 第一線 AML 治療中的造血細胞移植（HCT）：依風險調整之策略
AML 風險分類被用於為患者量身打造最佳的緩解後治療，選項包括異體 HCT、高劑量化學治療後接續自體 HCT，以及持續化學治療。由於異體 HCT 具有強大的移植物抗白血病（GVL）效應，且研究已證實無論潛在 AML 細胞遺傳學亞型與 MRD 狀態為何皆能發揮此效應，因此異體 HCT 是預防復發最理想的緩解後治療（Cornelissen et al. 2012a；Versluis et al. 2017a）。然而，復發發生率的絕對估計值仍有差異，反映了導致 AML 抗藥性的分子或細胞遺傳學差異。儘管異體 HCT 的 GVL 效應在 CR1 的 AML 患者中無庸置疑地存在，但伴隨的 TRM 會損及整體預後，特別是在復發率相對較低的 AML 患者中。因此，針對 CR1 之 AML 患者的依風險調整緩解後治療策略，除了評估白血
病特徵與 MRD 外，還應納入對 TRM 風險的評估（Cornelissen et al. 2012b；Cornelissen and Blaise 2016）。表 70.1 總結了根據 2022 年版 ELN 之 AML 風險分類、MRD 狀態與 TRM 風險所制定的依風險調整治療策略。TRM 風險宜優先採用針對特定患者亞群設計的專用評分系統進行評估。
對於具預後良好（favorable）AML 風險特徵的患者，通常不建議進行異體 HCT；此類患者可能優先選擇自體 HCT 或持續化學治療（Cornelissen et al. 2012b；Cornelissen and Blaise 2016；Dohner et al. 2022）。然而，預後良好風險但具 MRD 陽性的患者被視為高復發風險群，除非預測即使採用減低強度預處理（RIC）仍有過高的 TRM，否則建議優先在第一完全緩解期（CR1）接受異體 HCT。
在中度風險（intermediate-risk）患者中，比較異體 HCT 與非異體 HCT 緩解後治療的研究結果並不一致，特別是在納入分子標記考量時（Koreth et al. 2009；Stelljes et al. 2014；Versluis et al. 2017b）。一項依風險調整的 AML 臨床試驗將 MRD 陰性的中度風險 AML 患者分配至自體 HCT，而將 MRD 陽性的中度風險患者分配至異體 HCT，結果顯示自體 HCT 與異體 HCT 的預後相似（Venditti et al. 2019）。因此，強烈建議在中度風險 AML 患者的緩解後治療決策中評估 MRD 狀態。對於誘導化療後仍具 MRD 的中度風險 AML 患者，除高 TRM 風險者外，可施行異體 HCT。對於中度風險且 MRD 陰性的 AML 患者，亦可考慮異體 HCT，但自體 HCT 與化學治療均為替代治療選擇，特別是在預測 TRM 風險較高時。
具 MRD 的預後不良風險（adverse-risk）患者一旦取得血液學 CR，應儘速接受異體移植。無 MRD 的預後不良風險患者仍具有顯著的復發風險，同樣是異體 HCT 的候選對象；不過若患者具有極高的 TRM 風險，則可考慮非異體 HCT 的治療策略。
70.2 晚期 AML 之異體造血細胞移植（Allo-HCT）
Charles Craddock

70.2.1 前言
異體 HCT 在成人 AML 的治療處置中扮演日益重要的角色（Dohner et al. 2022）。減低強度預處理（RIC）方案的問世加上捐贈者來源的增加，已大幅增加了可考慮進行異體 HCT 的患者人數。與此同時，診斷時的分子特徵分析結合誘導化療後的 MRD 定量，大幅提升了我們預測單用高強度化療患者復發風險的能力，進而能更精準地篩選出可望受惠於異體移植的患者（Loke et al. 2020）。因此，異體 HCT 現已成為處於 CR1 之成人 AML 治療流程中至關重要的個人化核心環節。同時，醫界也日益認識到異體移植對於晚期（advanced-phase）AML 患者——特別是原發性難治型（primary refractory, PREF）AML 患者——具有治癒潛力（Dohner et al. 2022）。因此，所有新診斷且體能合適（fit）的成人 AML 患者在初診時即進行組織分型（HLA 分型）極為重要；而且除非有充分理由確信異體 HCT 不會納入該患者的治療流程，否則應及時啟動捐贈者搜尋。無論是使用相合手足捐贈者、志願非親屬捐贈者，或是近期使用半相合捐贈者（搭配移植後 cyclophosphamide 之 GVHD 預防）以及高有核細胞劑量的臍帶血單位，皆已取得令人鼓舞的成果。迄今尚無確切數據證實是否存在最佳的幹細胞來源，仍需前瞻性研究來解答此一重要問題。無論是在 CR1 接受移植的患者或晚期疾病患者，過去數十年間移植相關死亡率（TRM）已大幅下降，但移植後疾病復發的風險
依然居高不下，目前已成為 AML 異體移植患者治療失敗的主要原因。因此，臨床上仍迫切需要開發具潛力的新型策略，以降低所有接受異體移植之 AML 患者的疾病復發風險。
70.2.2 異體 HCT 在原發性難治型 AML（PREF AML）處置中的角色
新診斷的成人 AML 患者中有 10% 至 40% 為原發性難治型 AML（PREF AML），其定義為接受兩個療程的高強度誘導化學治療（包含至少一個療程的中劑量 cytarabine）後，仍未能達到形態學完全緩解（CR）（Ferguson et al. 2016）。決定對誘導化療具抗藥性的因素包括不良的疾病生物學特性與患者年齡。PREF AML 患者屬於真正對化療具抗藥性的疾病，若僅以進一步化療治療，長期存活率 <10%，而異體 HCT 是唯一具潛力帶來長期無病存活的治療方式。過去十年間，愈來愈多證據顯示異體 HCT 能讓相當比例的 PREF AML 患者獲得長期存活，這對於此一缺乏其他有效療法且人數可觀的患者群體而言，代表著臨床處置上的重大進展（Craddock et al. 2011；Todisco et al. 2017；Brissot et al. 2017；Boyiadzis et al. 2023）。儘管如此，PREF AML 患者接受異體移植的預後仍不盡理想，TRM 與疾病復發持續是阻礙長期存活的重大障礙。此外，對於哪些 PREF AML 患者最可能從移植中獲益，目前亦尚不完全明朗。在接受不超過兩個療程的高強度化療後即迅速進行移植的患者，其預後較佳；而在移植時疾病負荷較低者，復發率似乎也較低。因此，對於體能合適（fit）的 PREF AML 患者，只要能迅速找到合適捐贈者且預測的 TRM 在可接受範圍內，將移植視為具治癒潛力的治療方式相當重要。然而，若要更清楚地區分哪些 PREF AML 患者可能受惠於異體 HCT，以及同樣重要地，哪些患者即使接受此種進一步強化治療仍不太可能獲得長期存活，則仍需針對疾病生物學特性與化療反應證據對異體 HCT 後預後的影響進行更多研究。目前累積的數據顯示，帶有高風險分子特徵（例如存在 TP53 突變或 inv(3)(q21.3q26.2)）的患者預後極差；根據現有知識，在此患者群體中，將異體移植保留給已達到形態學 CR 的患者可能是合理的作法（Loke et al. 2022；Daver et al. 2022；Badar et al. 2023）。
PREF AML 患者的最佳預處理方案目前尚無定論，但除非有充分的反對理由，否則建議在 50 歲以下患者中使用骨髓清除性（myeloablative）方案。在年長成人中，並無證據顯示任何特定的減低強度預處理（RIC）方案更為優越。儘管曾有報告指出使用 FLAMSA 序貫方案在 PREF AML 患者中取得令人鼓舞的結果，但值得注意的是，近期一項隨機分配試驗在處於 CR1 或 CR2 的成人 AML 患者中，未能證實此方案相較於標準 RIC 方案 FB2 具有任何效益；不過該試驗中納入隨機分配的 PREF AML 患者人數不足，尚無法解答此方案在該臨床情境下是否具有特殊活性（Craddock et al. 2021）。如同所有因高風險 AML 接受異體移植的患者，在移植後 30–45 天抽取骨髓進行 MRD 檢測以評估對移植的反應至關重要，因為這能指引是否提早調降免疫抑制劑，或採用預防性／先發性（prophylactic/pre-emptive）捐贈者淋巴球輸注（DLI）（Loke et al. 2023）。
70.3 AML 異體造血細胞移植（Allo-HCT）之實務議題
Arnon Nagler

AML 是歐洲異體 HCT 最常見的適應症。根據 Passweg 等人最新發表的數據，2021 年歐洲共為 AML 施行了 7123 例異體 HCT（其中 4266 例為處於 CR1 的原發性［de novo］AML、1775 例為未達 CR 的原發性 AML，以及 1082 例為治療相關或具骨髓化生不良相關變化的 AML），占歐洲異體移植總量的 38%（Passweg et al. 2021）。與淋巴系統惡性腫瘤形成鮮明對比的是，由於針對 AML 的 CAR-T 細胞治療仍在起步階段，AML 的異體移植量並未減少（Passweg et al. 2021）。對許多具異體 HCT 適應症的 AML 患者而言，移植是目前唯一具治癒性的醫療程序，且在首次誘導治療後即達到 CR 者預後更佳。因此建議一旦診斷出 AML，即應預先為患者及潛在家族捐贈者進行 HLA 分型並啟動配對搜尋（Carreras et al. 2019）。近年來，異體 HCT 領域持續有新進展，主要是減低強度／減低毒性預處理（RIC/RTC）以及搭配移植後 cyclophosphamide（PTCY）的半相合捐贈者異體 HCT，結合支持性照護的改善，已顯著降低了移植相關毒性與死亡率（Slavin et al. 1998；Kasamon et al. 2015；Shimoni et al. 2005）。因此，接受移植的 AML 患者中位年齡不斷上升，許多受植患者年齡超過 60 歲甚至 65 歲。這些患者中有許多人在接受以 venetoclax 為基礎的低強度前導誘導治療（進一步減少了毒性）後，順利接續接受異體 HCT（Dohner et al. 2022；Keith et al. 2022）。在異體 HCT 前達到可測量殘存疾病（MRD）陰性與預後密切相關，並已成為急性白血病及其他血液惡性腫瘤治療典範中的主要目標（Keith et al. 2022；Abhishek et al. 2021；Bazinet et al. 2023）。現今施行的異體 HCT 大多來自非親屬捐贈者（包括部分相合非親屬捐贈者［MMUD］）與半相合捐贈者，並採用動員後周邊血幹細胞（mobilized PBSC）（Nagler and Mohty 2022；Arslan and Al Malki 2022；Anasetti et al. 2012；Raghunandan 2022）。異體 HCT 後具高復發風險的患者（包括高風險 AML、帶有次發性不良預後突變或次發性 AML 者），應考慮在異體 HCT 後進行維持治療或先發性（preemptive）治療，以期降低復發率（Eshrak et al. 2023）。最後，以 PTCY 為基礎的方案正成為 GVHD 預防的首選模式，包括接受 HLA 相合親屬、非親屬及半相合異體 HCT 的 AML 患者，而這也可能改變異體 HCT 的其他層面，包括預處理強度以及移植後的復發風險（Bolanos-Meade et al. 2023）。
70.4 急性前骨髓細胞白血病（Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia, APL）
Miguel Á. Sanz

70.4.1 概念與發生率
急性前骨髓細胞白血病（APL）是具有獨特臨床與形態學特徵的 AML 亞型，表現出特定的遺傳學改變——t(15;17) 轉位及其對應的分子基因重組 PML-RARA，此異常賦予其對全反式維生素 A 酸（all-trans retinoic acid, ATRA）與三氧化二砷（arsenic trioxide, ATO）的特殊敏感性。此疾病另一顯著特徵為伴隨特殊凝血病變（coagulopathy）的出血傾向，導致患者在初診時與誘導治療初期有極高發生率的出血併發症。
APL 占所有 AML 的 5–15%，中位發病年齡約 40 歲，男女分布相近。約 10% 的病例發生於使用細胞毒性藥物（特別是第二型拓撲異構酶抑制劑［topoisomerase II inhibitors］）或放射線治療之後。
70.4.2 診斷
70.4.2.1 形態學、免疫表現型與其他特徵
欄位：典型 M3（多顆粒型，hypergranular）75–80%｜變異型 M3（微顆粒型，microgranular）20–25%

【形態學（Morphology）】
• 典型 M3（多顆粒型）：
  - 細胞質具濃密顆粒。常見 Auer 氏小體（Auer rods）
  - 腎形或雙葉細胞核
• 變異型 M3（微顆粒型）：
  - 細胞質具細小顆粒或寡顆粒（hypogranular）。Auer 氏小體較少見
  - 腎形、雙葉或多葉細胞核

【免疫表現型（Immunophenotyping）】
• 典型 M3（多顆粒型）：HLA-DR−/CD34−/CD33+ª/CD13+ᵇ/CD15−/+
• 變異型 M3（微顆粒型）：HLA-DR±/CD34±/CD33+ª/CD9+/CD2±/CD13+ᵇ/CD56±

【其他相關特徵（Other associated features）】
• 典型 M3（多顆粒型）：
  - 最常表現為低白血球計數（low WBC counts）
  - BCR3 異構型（isoform）較少見
• 變異型 M3（微顆粒型）：
  - 最常表現為高白血球計數（high WBC counts）
  - 最常為 BCR3 異構型（isoform）

註腳：
ª強且均質表現（Intense and homogeneous expression）
ᵇ異質性表現（Heterogeneous expression）
70.4.2.2 遺傳學診斷
【傳統細胞遺傳學 t(15;17)(q22;q21)】
• 優點（Pros）：
  – 特異性極高
  – 可在 30% 病例中偵測到額外染色體異常（最常見為 +8）
• 缺點（Cons）：
  – 敏感度較低（80%）
  – 20% 病例因分裂中期細胞不足、品質不佳或呈現正常核型而出現偽陰性

【螢光原位雜交（FISH）PML-RARA】
• 優點（Pros）：
  – 特異性極高且快速
• 缺點（Cons）：
  – 敏感度不夠高，且無法提供異構型（isoform）資訊

【反轉錄聚合酶連鎖反應（RT-PCR）】
• 優點（Pros）：
  – 特異性極高、快速且具高敏感度
  – 可鑑定異構型（isoform），有助於後續 MRD 監測
• 缺點（Cons）：
  – 偶有人工偽影（artifacts）與汙染問題

【抗 PML 抗體（PG-M3）免疫染色】
• 優點（Pros）：
  – 特異性極高、快速且價格低廉
  – 間接免疫螢光下呈現特徵性微斑點型態（microspeckled pattern）
• 缺點（Cons）：
  – 無法提供異構型（isoform）資訊
70.4.2.3 第 17 號染色體上 RARA 基因之其他重組
欄位：染色體異常（Chromosomal abnormality）｜RARA 重組（RARA rearrangement）
• t(11;17) (q23;q21) → ZBTB16 (PLZF)/RARA（對 ATRA 具抗藥性）
• t(17;17) (q21;q21) → STAT5b/RARA（對 ATRA 具抗藥性）

• t(17;17)(q21;q24) → PRKAR1A/RARA（對 ATRA 敏感）
• t(X;17)(p11;q21) → BCOR/RARA（2 例對 ATRA 敏感）
• t(4;17) (q12;q21) → FIP1L1/RARA（對 ATRA 敏感性未知）

70.4.3 第一線治療
2009 年版 ELN 建議肯認了數項非隨機研究中使用 ATRA 併用 ATO（無論是否搭配極少量化學治療）所報告的良好結果，但當時的標準照護仍是 ATRA 併用蔥環類（anthracycline）基礎化學治療的組合（Sanz et al. 2009）。然而，近期的臨床研究結果促使更新版 ELN 指引修正了此項建議（Sanz et al. 2019）。
一項非隨機研究（Abaza et al. 2017）與兩項隨機臨床試驗（Lo-Coco et al. 2013；Burnett et al. 2015）比較了 ATRA 併用 ATO 與標準 ATRA 併用化學治療之療效與安全性，其長期結果強力支持將 ATRA 併用 ATO 確立為初診時白血球計數（WBC）低於 10 × 10⁹/L 之低至中度風險 APL 患者的新標準照護。儘管如此，在化學治療比 ATO 更易負擔的國家中，ATRA 併用化學治療的傳統組合仍是可接受的選擇。然而，對於高風險患者則有兩種有效選擇：ATRA 併用化學治療，或 ATRA 併用 ATO 並在至少誘導階段加上一定劑量的減積化學治療（cytoreductive chemotherapy）。
處於第一完全緩解期（CR1）的患者絕對無需進行 HCT，唯一例外是鞏固治療後 PML-RARA 之即時定量 PCR（RQ-PCR）持續呈陽性的極少數患者（<1%），因為此亞群的預後極差。此外，對於復發後達到第二次或後續 CR 的 APL 患者，亦有進行 HCT 的適應症。
70.4.4 救援治療（Salvage Therapy）
除了鞏固治療結束時仍呈 MRD 陽性（分子持續存在，molecular persistence）的患者外，目前的共識是日後發生分子復發或血液學復發的患者，必須立即接受包括 HCT 在內的額外治療。救援治療的目標是達成分子緩解，作為銜接至 HCT 的橋接治療（bridge to HCT）。若第一線治療採用 ATRA 併用化學治療，建議使用 ATRA 併用 ATO 作為救援治療；反之，若第一線治療已使用 ATRA 併用 ATO，則優先選擇 ATRA 併用化學治療。
在上述兩種情況下，亦可考慮使用 gemtuzumab ozogamicin，但一律作為銜接至 HCT 的橋接治療。多項研究（Yanada et al. 2013；Holter Chakrabarty et al. 2014；Lengfelder et al. 2015）顯示，對於達到第二次分子緩解且符合移植條件的患者，應將自體 HCT（auto-HCT）視為首選。不適合接受 HCT 或 CR1 持續時間極長的患者，則可採行某種維持治療，其藥物選擇需綜合考量先前的治療紀錄與臨床狀況。
異體 HCT 應保留給復發風險高且 TRM 風險低的患者，或作為自體 HCT 後再次復發患者的第二線移植選擇。
70.4.5 造血細胞移植（HCT）之適應症
處於 CR1 的患者絕對無需進行 HCT，唯一例外是鞏固治療結束時未能達到分子緩解者（<1%）。有關需要接受 HCT 之患者的完整適應症與其他建議總覽，請參閱表 70.2 及下圖所示之治療流程。
70.4.6 APL 造血細胞移植之主要文獻系列報告
目前尚無隨機分配臨床試驗評估不同 HCT 模式在難治型／復發型 APL 中的療效與安全性。現有數據主要來自比較登錄資料庫歷史世代的回顧性研究（表 70.3）。EBMT（Sanz et al. 2021）與 CIBMTR（Holter Chakrabarty et al. 2014）的登錄資料庫研究均顯示，儘管復發率無顯著差異，但自體 HCT 在整體存活率（OS）上優於異體 HCT。日本成人白血病研究群（JALSG）的其他非比較性研究近期亦報告，在 ATO 救援治療後進行自體 HCT 具有相當卓越的療效（Yanada et al. 2013, 2017）。
表 70.2 APL 患者進行 HCT 之適應症（治療決策流程圖）
【上半部：第一線治療（Front-line therapy）】
• 第一線治療 → 鞏固治療後 MRD 評估（MRD assessment after consolidation）：
  – 分子緩解（Molecular remission）→ 無 HCT 適應症（HCT not indicated）
  – 分子持續存在（Molecular persistence，<1%）→ 救援治療（Salvage therapy）→ 異體 HCT（Allogeneic HCT）

【下半部：救援治療（Salvage therapy）】
• 救援治療 → 鞏固治療後 MRD 評估（MRD assessment after consolidation）：
  – 分子緩解（Molecular remission）→ 風險評估（Risk assessment）：
    ▪ TRM 風險高（TRM high）→ 不進行 HCT（No HCT*）
    ▪ TRM 與復發風險皆低（TRM and relapse low）→ 自體 HCT（Autologous HCT）
    ▪ TRM 風險低且復發風險高（TRM low and relapse high）→ 異體 HCT（Allogeneic HCT）
  – 分子持續存在（Molecular persistence）→ 強化治療（Intensification therapy）→ 異體 HCT（Allogeneic HCT）
* 考慮維持治療（ATRA、ATO 及／或低劑量化學治療）
表 70.2（續）APL 患者進行 HCT 之適應症與建議總表
欄位：項目｜自體 HCT（Auto-HCT）｜異體 HCT（Allo-HCT）

• 無適應症（Not indicated）：
  – 自體 HCT：處於分子緩解之 CR1
  – 異體 HCT：處於分子緩解之 CR1
• 具適應症（Indicated）：
  – 自體 HCT：≥CR2，且處於分子緩解
  – 異體 HCT：
    ▪ ≥CR2 且救援治療後 PML-RARA 仍呈陽性（+）
    ▪ ≥CR2 且先前自體 HCT 失敗
    ▪ ≥CR2 且屬於高復發風險、低 TRM 風險之患者
• 銜接至 HCT 之橋接救援治療（Salvage therapy as a bridge to HCT）：
  – 自體 HCT：第一線接受 ATRA＋化療後復發者，嘗試以 ATRA＋ATO 達成分子緩解；第一線接受 ATRA＋ATO 後復發者，則選擇 ATRA＋化療
  – 異體 HCT：第一線接受 ATRA＋化療後復發者，嘗試以 ATRA＋ATO 達成分子緩解；第一線接受 ATRA＋ATO 後復發者，則選擇 ATRA＋化療
• 預處理方案（Conditioning regimen）：
  – 自體 HCT：任何適用於 AML 之方案，優先選擇含高劑量 Ara-C（HDAC）者（例如 BEA 方案［Gondo et al. 1997］：BU/VP/Ara-C）
  – 異體 HCT：任何適用於 AML 之方案
• 幹細胞來源（Cell source）：
  – 自體 HCT：動員後周邊血（Mobilized peripheral blood）
  – 異體 HCT：動員後周邊血（Mobilized peripheral blood）
• 中樞神經系統（CNS）預防之適應症（Indication of CNS prophylaxis）：
  – 自體 HCT：以 MTX、hydrocortisone 與 Ara-C 進行鞘內注射治療（ITT），特別是發生 CNS 復發者
  – 異體 HCT：以 MTX、hydrocortisone 與 Ara-C 進行鞘內注射治療（ITT），特別是發生 CNS 復發者
• 移植後維持治療（Maintenance therapy post-HCT）：
  – 自體 HCT：尚未證實，但理論上 ATO + ATRA 可能有效
  – 異體 HCT：尚未證實，但理論上 ATO + ATRA 可能有效
• 分子監測（Molecular monitoring）：
  – 自體 HCT：建議至少每 3 個月以 RQ-PCR 監測一次，持續 2–3 年
  – 異體 HCT：建議至少每 3 個月以 RQ-PCR 監測一次，持續 2–3 年

重點摘要（Key Points）
• 處於第一完全緩解期（CR1）之 AML 患者是否進行異體 HCT，應根據同時評估 TRM 風險與 AML 疾病風險的依風險調整策略而定。
• 對於體能合適（fit）的原發性難治型 AML（PREF AML）患者，只要能迅速找到合適捐贈者且預測的 TRM 可接受，異體 HCT 仍是具治癒潛力的治療方式。
• 急性前骨髓細胞白血病（APL）僅在特定情況下有異體 HCT 適應症（例如：≥CR2 但未達分子緩解，或先前自體 HCT 失敗後）。

Acute Myeloid Leukaemia 
in Children
Brenda E. S. Gibson, Martin G. Sauer, 
Subramaniam Ramanathan, and Persis J. Amrolia
71.1	
Introduction
Whilst the outcome of frontline AML (including 
PR) has improved, treatment of R/R AML 
remains a challenge. Despite the majority of chil­
dren (>90%) achieving CR, the relapse risk (RR) 
in CR1 remains high at 20–30%, albeit varying 
by risk group. Relapse remains the most common 
cause of death.
HCT reduces the RR in CR1 in all risk groups 
when compared to chemotherapy as consolida­
tion treatment. Historically, this reduction in RR 
has not always translated into an improvement in 
OS due to the treatment-related mortality (TRM). 
However in the current era of a relatively low 
TRM, the balance shifts in favour of HCT for

Haematology Department, Royal Hospital for

Transplantation, Medizinische Hochschule Hannover,

71
children at high risk of relapse. When consider­
ing the benefits of transplantation in children, it is 
important to acknowledge the potential for asso­
ciated late effects, particularly infertility. HCT 
offers children with R/R AML their only real 
chance of long-term survival, which may rely on 
augmenting the graft versus leukaemia (GVL) 
effect. Post-HCT strategies such as the employ­
ment of FLT3 inhibitors (sorafenib and midastau­
rin) 
for 
FLT3/ITD-mutated 
AML, 
donor 
lymphocyte infusion (DLI), adoptive T-cells, or 
NK-cell immunotherapy may reduce the risk of 
further relapse post-transplant. A number of CAR 
T-cells are in development and may offer hope 
for the future.
71.2	
Prognostic Factors 
and Indications
71.2.1	 First Complete Remission
Consolidation therapy with allogeneic HCT in 
CR1 of paediatric AML has been shown consis­
tently to reduce the RR through a GVL effect, 
which is stronger in AML than ALL. Recognising 
the importance of the GVL effect in preventing 
relapse has led to the adoption of techniques to 
augment the GVL effect such as the use of cord 
blood stem cells, omission of serotherapy and 
early withdrawal of immunosuppression.
Improvements in HLA typing and expansion 
of the donor pool through the use of cord blood 
633

stem cells and haploidentical donors have made 
HCT an option for the majority of patients. All 
patients with AML should be tissue-typed at pre­
sentation in order to optimise the chance of early 
transplant should this be indicated.
The criteria for transplanting patients has 
evolved from transplanting patients irrespective 
of the risk group, to transplanting all patients 
other than those with good-risk (GR) cytogenet­
ics (about 70–80% of all patients), to the current 
practice of restricting transplant to those with 
poor-risk (PR) cytogenetics (about 30% of all 
patients), who are at the highest risk of relapse 
and most likely to benefit from HCT in CR1 in an 
era of low TRM.
There is no international agreement on the 
definition of PR disease. Most groups define PR 
disease which may benefit from HCT in CR1 
through a combination of PR cytogenetics/
molecular abnormalities, which are currently 
considered to be the strongest indicator of out­
come, and the persistence of MRD after chemo­
therapy course 1 or 2. There is evolving consensus 
on which cytogenetics/molecular aberration con­
stitutes high-risk disease, although some national 
groups place more value on MRD.
There is consensus that failure to achieve CR 
carries a poor outcome. There is no advantage for 
HCT in CR1 for patients with GR disease, that is, 
those with t(8;21)(q22;q22)/RUNX1::RUNX1T1, 
inv.(16)(p13;q22)/CBFB::MYH11, NPM1 muta­
tion or biallelic CEBPA bZIP in-frame insertion/
deletion mutation. The benefit of HCT in CR1 for 
patients with intermediate-risk (IR) cytogenetics is 
less clear, and these may be the patients without 
PR cytogenetics but with a suboptimal early 
response to chemotherapy in whom MRD assess­
ment can identify those at high risk of relapse who 
may benefit from transplant. There is no role for 
HCT in CR1 of acute promyelocytic leukaemia 
(APL) or Down syndrome myeloid leukaemia 
(ML-DS). HCT for patients with Fanconi anaemia 
and MDS/AML and those with JMML are dis­
cussed elsewhere.
71.2.1.1	
Cytogenetics
Cytogenetic/molecular abnormalities are strong 
prognostic indicators of outcome in AML and are 
used to risk-stratify treatment. There is consensus 
that patients with GR cytogenetics have favour­
able outcomes with chemotherapy alone and, 
with the exception of rare cases with a subopti­
mal response to induction therapy, should not 
proceed to transplant. The approach to patients 
with IR cytogenetics is largely based on response 
to chemotherapy as assessed by MRD. HCT is 
generally recommended for patients with PR risk 
cytogenetic/molecular abnormalities. There is 
increasing consensus on which cytogenetic/
molecular abnormalities are PR and those most 
commonly considered indicative of being at high 
risk of relapse include:
•	 inv.(3)(q21q26)/t(3;3)(q21;q26)/abn(3q26) 
(MECOM rearrangements),
•	 −5/del(5q)
•	 −7
•	 t(6,9)(p23;q34)/DEK::NUP214,
•	 t(9;22)(q34;q11)/BCR::ABL1,
•	 12p abnormalities
•	 t(6,11)(q27;q23)/KMT2A::MLLT4,
•	 t(4;11)(q21;q23)/KMT2A::AFF1,
•	 t(10;11)(p11 ~ 14;q23)/KMT2A::MLLT10 and 
other KMT2A partners located on 10p (e.g., 
ABI1),
•	 All 
NUP98 
fusions, 
t(5;11)(q35;p15.5)/

NUP98::NSD1, NUP98::KDM5A.
•	 t(7;12)(q36;p13)/MNX1::ETV6,
•	 inv.(16)(p13.3;q24.3)/CBFA2T3::GLIS2,
•	 FLT3-ITD without NPM1 mutation or CEBPA 
in-frame bZIP mutation or CBF-AML (NB: 
CEBPA double mutation with FLT3-ITD is 
intermediate risk).
•	 Complex karyotype – no consensus.
It is difficult to risk-stratify rare fusions, but 
FUS::ERG and PICALM::MLLT10 have been 
reported in the literature as poor risk. Not all 
groups consider a complex karyotype (3 or more 
abnormalities) to be poor risk. The translocation 
t(11;19)(q23; p13.3)/KMT2A::MLLT1 is variably 
classified as intermediate or high risk. KMT2A 
(MLL) rearrangements with the exception of 
t(4;11)(q21;q23)/KMT2A::AFF1, 
t(6;11)
(q27;q23)/KMT2A::MLLT4 and t(10;11p11-p14;
q23)/KMT2A::MLLT10/KMT2A::ABI1 
are

­generally considered intermediate risk, but in 
rare incidences intermediate risk KMT2A abnor­
malities may co-occur with poor-risk features 
(e.g., FLT3-ITD, monosomy 7, 12p abnormali­
ties, etc.), which may alter the risk. FLT3-ITD is 
considered as poor risk but often co-occurs with 
other poor-risk cytogenetic abnormalities, when 
the risk may be augmented. The absence of GR 
cytogenetic abnormalities and the allelic ratio 
(>0.4) may influence the risk and approach to 
treatment. An increasing number of clinically rel­
evant fusions are becoming recognised, a number 
of which are cytogenetically cryptic and require 
more comprehensive diagnostic assessment. 
Currently, PR cytogenetics comprise about 
30–35% of all AML in children.
AML is a heterogeneous disease, and not all 
PR cytogenetic groups will benefit to the same 
degree from HCT in CR1. The European Society 
for Blood and Marrow Transplantation (EBMT)/ 
Paediatric Diseases Working Party (PDWP) 
recently reported a review of children ≤18 years 
of age at HCT reported to the European Society 
for Blood and Marrow Transplantation (EBMT) 
registry, who received their first allogeneic HCT 
for AML in CR1 between 2005 and 2020 and 
who had an evaluable diagnostic karyotype. The 
aim was to establish whether PR cytogenetic 
abnormalities at diagnosis remain predictive of 
OS after HCT. Patients were subgrouped as (a) 
monosomy 7/del(7q) or monosomy 5/del(5q) 
(24%), (b) 11q23 abnormalities excluding t(9;11)
(p12;q23)/KMT2A::MLLT3 (37%), (c) complex 
or monosomal karyotype (24%), or (d) “other” 
(15%). A complex karyotype was defined as three 
or more structural abnormalities, and a mono­
somal karyotype as a monosomy with one or 
more structural abnormalities, excluding WHO-
designated recurring translocations or inversions 
(2017 ELN recommendations). The “other” 
subgroup 
included 
t(6;9)(p23;q34)/DEK::

NUP214, 
t(3;5)(q25;q34)/NPM1::ML

F1,t(9;22)(q34;q11)/BCR::ABL1, 
t(8;16)
(p11;p13)/MYST3::CREBBP, 
inv.(3)(q21q26) 
or t(3;3)(q21;q26)/RPN1::MECOM, t(16;21)
(p11;q22)/FUS::ERG, 
abn(11)(p15) 
and 
del(12p)/abnormality of 12(p13). The review 
included 744 children (median age at HCT: 
8.6 years [0.3–18 years]). Median follow-up after 
HCT was 4.4 years. Eighty-six per cent of 346 
evaluable patients were MRD-negative pre-HCT 
and 97% of patients received myeloablative con­
ditioning (MAC). The OS and leukaemia-free 
survival (LFS) for the entire cohort were 76% 
and 70%, respectively, at 2  years. In a multi­
variate model, 11q23 (hazard ratio (HR) = 0.59, 
P  =  0.01) and “other” PR cytogenetic abnor­
malities (HR = 0.49, P < 0.01) were associated 
with significantly better OS compared to mono­
somy 7/del(7q) or 5/del(5q) (HR1). The “other” 
PR cytogenetic abnormalities category was also 
associated with a lower risk of disease relapse 
after HCT (HR = 0.4, P = 0.01). Receipt of an 
unrelated donor was associated with a lower 
relapse incidence (RI) (HR = 0.58, P = 0.03).
71.2.1.2	
Measurable Residual Disease 
Assessment (See Chap. 57)
Whilst genetic risk is the most important prog­
nostic factor in AML, MRD is an independent 
post-remission prognostic factor important for 
risk 
stratification 
and 
treatment 
decision 
(Schuurhuis et al. 2018). Detection can be done 
by multiparametric flow cytometry (MFC), 
reverse-transcription 
quantitative 
PCR 
(RT-qPCR), digital droplet PCR and next-­
generation sequencing (NGS), all of which have 
different sensitivities and specificities. The 
European Leukaemia Net (ELN)-MRD Working 
Party has produced guidelines for standardisation 
and harmonisation which includes recommenda­
tions for the use of MRD prognostically, selec­
tion of the methodology, appropriate time points 
for assessment, MRD thresholds and definition 
of response (Heuser et al. 2021).
MFC is most commonly employed in paediat­
ric AML either by measuring leukaemia aberrant 
immunophenotype (LAIP), a “different from nor­
mal” (DfN) phenotype or a combination of both 
methodologies. MRD positivity by MFC at early 
time points is strongly predictive of outcome. It is 
sensitive to a level of 0.1–0.01% and with an 
appropriate panel about 90% of children will 
have an informative LAIP by MFC.
Currently, the commonest threshold level for 
MFC is 0.1%, and the time point for post-course

is 1 or 2. However, the ability to define absolute 
risk remains limited with nearly a quarter of 
patients with flow MRD ≤ 0.1% post-course 1 
relapsing and a similar proportion of patients 
with flow MRD >0.1% remaining relapse-free 
(Sievers et al. 2003; Paietta 2018). More recently, 
a systematic review of the prognostic value of 
MRD in paediatric AML was reported. Thirteen 
studies were included and in all studies, MRD 
positivity during treatment was associated with 
worse clinical outcome. However, MRD negativ­
ity during treatment is associated with signifi­
cantly better clinical outcome but does not 
exclude the possibility of relapse, whilst positiv­
ity early during treatment does not exclude cure 
(Segerink et al. 2021).
Molecular MRD assessment by RT-qPCR 
generally has a sensitivity level of 0.1–0.001% 
and is applicable in approximately 80% of chil­
dren who have a target for RT-qPCR such as a 
fusion gene or NPM1 mutation. Not only can 
molecular MRD be used to guide treatment but 
can also be used sequentially for the early detec­
tion and pre-emptive treatment of relapse. Further 
work is required to define molecular MRD 
thresholds at early time points that are predictive 
of relapse in the paediatric setting, bearing in 
mind that these may vary by molecular subtype. 
However, serially rising transcript levels (i.e., 
MRD relapse) are strongly predictive of haema­
tological relapse, and some consider this an indi­
cation for pre-emptive therapy. Digital PCR and 
next-generation sequencing have some potential 
advantages for MRD monitoring over existing 
molecular techniques but currently remain in the 
research arena. Similarly, leukaemia stem cell 
monitoring may add prognostic information to 
current flow cytometry-based assays (Schuurhuis 
et al. 2018).
Preliminary data from adult studies and 
AAML 03P1 (Loken et al. 2012) suggest a lim­
ited discriminatory value for flow MRD in 
patients with PR cytogenetics. Observation from 
COG AAML03P1 and AIEOP 2002/01 that 
patients considered MRD negative at the end of 
treatment, but with previously documented MRD 
post-course 1, remain at high risk of relapse and 
poor outcome, suggesting that intervention 
beyond clearance of MRD with chemotherapy 
alone is required for improved outcome (Buldini 
et al. 2017; Loken et al. 2012).
In patients with GR cytogenetics, stable or 
falling transcript levels may be an indication for 
further chemotherapy rather than HCT. It is rec­
ognised that some patients with GR cytogenetics 
may have disease which is detectable molecu­
larly after course 1, but patients may still obtain a 
durable CR with chemotherapy alone. Karlsson 
et al. reported a small study of 15 children treated 
on NOPHO-AML 2004 which compared results 
by RT-qPCR and MFC.  Eight children had a 
RUNX1::RUNX1T1, one CBFB::MYH11 and six 
KMT2A::MLLT3. Ten of 22 samples were discor­
dant with a cutoff for positivity of ≥0.1%. The 
majority 
(9/10) 
were 
MRD-positive 
with 
RT-qPCR but MRD-negative with MFC.  This 
was shown to be due to the presence of fusion 
transcripts in mature cells as well as in CD34-­
expressing cells. Measurement of RT-qPCR sug­
gests slower response kinetics than indicated by 
MFC, and the authors suggest that the prognostic 
impact of early measurement with RT-qPCR 
remains to be determined (Karlsson et al. 2022).
In the NOPHO–AML 2004 trial, MRD 
detected by MFC was performed on day 15 and 
before consolidation and was evaluable in 101 
patients. Using a 0.1% MRD cutoff level, MRD-­
negative and MRD-postive patients at the start of 
consolidation therapy had a 5-year EFS of 
57 ± 7% and 11 ± 7%, respectively (P < 0.001) 
and an OS of 78 ± 6% and 28 ± 11% (P < 0.001). 
Patients who were MRD-positive before consoli­
dation had a cumulative incidence of relapse 
(CIR) of 82 ± 9.3% compared to 38.2 ± 6% in 
those who were MRD-negative at this time point. 
In multivariate analysis, only MRD correlated 
significantly with survival and MRD before con­
solidation therapy was the strongest independent 
prognostic factor for EFS and OS (Tierens et al. 
2016).
HCT has been shown to reduce the negative 
impact of a poor early treatment response. Thirty 
one of 267 (12%) children treated on NOPHO-­
AML 20024 were defined as poor responders 
(15% blasts morphologically after course 1 or 
5% blasts after course 2). These patients had

time-intensive chemotherapy followed by HCT 
in 25 of 31 with a donor. The 3-year probability 
of survival for these high-risk patients was 70%. 
Patients classified as intermediate risk (defined as 
5–14.9% blasts after course 1) had a significantly 
inferior EFS compared to high-risk patients. Both 
groups had time-intensive chemotherapy, but 
only high-risk patients proceeded to HCT 
(Wareham et al. 2013; Abrahamsson et al. 2011).
The St Jude’s group showed that flow MRD 
positivity >0.1% after course 1 was associated 
with a 3-year EFS of 43% compared to 74% in 
those who were MRD-negative (Rubnitz et  al. 
2010). Likewise on the COG AAML03P1 proto­
col, of 188 patients who achieved morphological 
CR after course 1 or 2, 46 (24%) had detectable 
flow MRD  >  0.1%. Those with and without 
MRD > 0.1% at the end of course 2 had a 3-year-
RR of 67% and 30% and a relapse-free survival 
(RFS) of 29% and 65%, respectively (Loken 
et al. 2012).
Compared to patients with PR cytogenetics, 
the benefit of HCT in CR1 for patients with IR 
cytogenetics is less clear.
A recent I-BFMSG study evaluated the benefit 
of HCT in CR 1  in a heterogenous cohort of 
patients with KMT2A-r (rearranged) AML 
including high- and intermediate-risk rearrange­
ments based on the fusion partner. Irrespective of 
risk group, MRD negativity post-course 2 was 
associated with superior EFS and a trend towards 
lower CIR.  However, within the intermediate-­
risk group, the CIR was similar for MRD-­
negative and MRD-positive patients post-course 
2. The authors recognised the limitations of a ret­
rospective study in which the transplant rate was 
low (21%) by today’s standards, the limitations 
of MFC MRD in the era studied, and that the 
study was not powered to assess the effect of 
HCT in CR1 (van Weelderen et al. 2023).
71.2.2	 Relapsed Disease
Patients with relapsed AML across all cytoge­
netic risk groups have a dismal prognosis with 
chemotherapy alone, and it is generally accepted 
that they should proceed to transplant in CR2. 
The first international I-BFM AML Relapsed 
Study reported the chance of achieving a second 
CR after relapse to be dependent on the length of 
CR1: CR1 < 1 year versus CR >1 year is 50% 
versus 75% with an overall CR rate of 60% and 
OS for CR1  <  1  year 26% versus 45% 
CR1 > 1 year, p < 0.001 (Kaspers et al. 2013). 
Cytogenetics are strong prognostic indicators in 
relapse as in de novo disease with patients with 
CBF leukaemias fairing the best: CBF leukae­
mias versus others—OS 67% versus 31%, 
p < 0.001. Other significant prognostic indicators 
were no HCT in CR1 and speed of response to 
reinduction.
A retrospective analysis of two large interna­
tional study groups (COG and BFM) has updated 
these outcomes. The OS at 5  years was 42% 
(BFM) and 35% (COG). Initial high-risk features 
and short time to relapse predicted poor out­
comes. OS for all patients who received a HCT 
was 54%  ±  4%. In the BFM cohort, 82% of 
patients proceeded to HCT which represented an 
increase compared to previous trials and an 
improvement in outcomes was observed (Rasche 
et al. 2021).
The AML-SCT BFM 0227 trial showed simi­
lar outcomes. Patients transplanted in CR2 had a 
4-year EFS of 46% with a RR of 27% (Sauer 
et al. 2020).
Outcomes in multiply relapsed AML are poor. 
An AML-BFM study group reported a 5-year 
probability of OS of 31  ±  9% following HCT 
(n = 25) in patients transplanted after a second 
relapse. Twenty-one of 25 (88%) had a previous 
HCT. Early second relapse was associated with a 
dismal outcome and dependent on a favourable 
response to further treatment. Although survival 
at the second relapse is poor, it is possible (Rasche 
et al. 2021). Novel therapies may have a role in 
multiple relapsed AML to achieve remission 
prior to HCT.
71.2.3	 Refractory Disease
Residual 
disease/MRD 
positivity 
pre-HCT 
increases the risk of relapse post-HCT, but the 
susceptibility of AML to GVL does not preclude

transplant. MRD status just prior to HCT is an 
important prognostic indicator. A small study 
reported a 5-year OS of 80.4% for children with 
<0.01% MRD (n  =  27), 66.7% for those with 
0.01–5% MRD (n = 9) and 58.3% for those with 
>5% MRD (Leung et al. 2012). In a retrospective 
study from the UK of 44 paediatric patients trans­
planted for refractory AML, 68% achieved CR 
following HCT with a 5-year LFS of 43% and 
RR of 32% (O'Hare et al. 2017)). Outcomes in 
patients with primary refractory disease (n = 23) 
were equivalent to those with R/R AML (n = 21). 
Blast percentage ⩽ 30% in the bone marrow 
(BM) pre-HCT, myeloablative conditioning and 
acute GVHD were favourable prognostic fea­
tures. Stratification according to age ≥ 10 years 
and > 30% blasts in BM pre-HCT enabled prog­
nostication, i.e., patients with neither or one of 
these risk factors had a LFS of 53% whereas 
those with both factors had a LFS of 10%. It 
should be noted, however, that these data were in 
patients who proceeded to HCT and there is thus 
significant selection bias. Recent data suggest 
particularly impressive outcomes with unrelated 
cord blood transplant in patients with refractory 
disease with a 61% EFS in patients with primary 
refractory disease (n = 29) and 45% in those with 
R/R disease (n = 23) (Horgan et al. 2023). Overall 
these data suggest that a significant subset of 
patients with refractory disease are curable by 
HCT.
71.3	
Conditioning Regimens
No advantage has been shown for total body irra­
diation (TBI) in AML, and chemotherapy-only 
regimens should be used to limit the burden of 
morbidity associated with endocrine dysfunction. 
Adult data from the CIBMTR demonstrated 
improved NRM, OS and DFS in patients with 
AML transplanted using IV BU with therapeutic 
drug monitoring (TDM) compared with TBI 
(Copelan et al. 2013). Myeloablative condition­
ing (MAC) regimens are most commonly used, 
but a number of reduced toxicity conditioning 
(RTC) regimens are being tested. There is no 
proven “best” chemotherapy conditioning regi­
men, though MAC regimens with BU and CY 
with TDM of BU levels are currently the standard 
of care.
However, the AUC to be targeted has been 
systemically evaluated for the combination of 
BU with CY only. When BU was combined with 
agents other than CY, relationships between BU 
exposure and clinical outcomes have been shown 
to be altered (McCune et al. 2000). For example, 
the use of BU TDM varied considerably with 
BU/FLU (Parmar et al. 2013; Ayala et al. 2015), 
Bu/clofarabine (Andersson et al. 2011; Kebriaei 
et al. 2012) and BU/CY/etoposide (Zhang et al. 
2012; Chen et al. 2015). A retrospective EBMT 
study of Bu, Cy and Melphalan (Mel) (enhanced 
MAC) in paediatric AML in CR1 suggested 
improved RR and LFS compared with Bu-Cy, but 
the majority of patients receiving Bu-Cy on this 
study did not undergo TDM (Lucchini et al. 
2017). The prospectively conducted and centrally 
monitored BFM trial AML SCT-BFM 2007 used 
BU/CY/MEL (enhanced MAC) for children with 
a matched family or unrelated donor. BU dosing 
was weight-adapted only. Four-year EFS and OS 
were 61% and 70%, respectively, for the com­
plete cohort. CIR was 22%. TRM was 15% and 
correlated with age reaching 9% (SE 3%) in chil­
dren younger than 12 years and 31% (SE 9%) in 
older children and adolescents. Of note, children 
under the age of 12 years, who were transplanted 
in CR1, achieved an exceptional OS of 94%, an 
EFS of 84% and a TRM of 6% at four years. Due 
to unacceptable TRM rates between 20 and 30%, 
the trial was halted for teenagers, and this regi­
men should be avoided or used with caution in 
this age group (Sauer et al. 2020). There is an 
increasing body of experience with BU/FLU-
based MAC, which is well tolerated, but no pub­
lished randomised comparisons are available to 
determine the relative anti-leukaemic activity of 
BU/FLU versus BU/CY (Harris et al. 2018). The 
recently completed MyeChild01 trial is expected 
to give answers to this unresolved question.
Replacing BU with Treosulfan (TREO) to 
reduce toxicity whilst maintaining efficacy is being 
tested and given in combination with CY (TREO/
CY) or with FLU and Thiotepa (FTT). The choice 
of conditioning regimen is a balance between effi­
cacy and toxicity. Comorbidity, pretreatment with 
drugs that may contribute to toxicity, i.e., gemtu­

zumab and VOD/SOS, age and HLA disparity may 
influence the choice of conditioning regimen. 
Comorbidity or heavy previous treatment may 
indicate a reduced intensity conditioning (RIC) 
regimen with BU/FLU or FLU/MEL. Targeted BU 
levels will differ between MAC, RTC and 
RIC. Patient toxicities may suggest avoidance of 
specific agents. Newer regimens which include 
clofarabine (CLO) are being tested. A prospec­
tively randomised study comparing CLO/FLU/BU 
and BU/CY/MEL is currently being conducted by 
the NOPHO-DBH consortium.
An important concept has been introduced by 
the FLAMSA-RIC approach (Schmid et al. 2006). 
It incorporates prophylactic DLI after a rapid 
CSA taper to compensate for the potentially 
decreased anti-leukaemic potency of RIC chemo­
therapy. The AML SCT BFM 2007 trial for chil­
dren with refractory disease reported an EFS and 
OS of 53% and 57%, respectively, at 4 years for 
children with primary refractory de novo AML 
(Sauer et al. 2020). The trial delivered sequential 
conditioning for R/R AML immediately followed 
by allo-HCT.  The prospectively randomised 
phase III ASAP trial has very recently substanti­
ated this concept in adults and produced compa­
rable LFS for conventional intensive induction 
treatment prior to transplant (Stelljes et al. 2022).
71.4	
Donor Selection Hierarchy 
and Stem Cell Source
71.4.1	 Allogeneic HCT
The choice of donor for allo-HCT is based on 
HLA compatibility and CMV status. Outcomes 
are similar for MSD and MUD. The degree of 
mismatch which is acceptable depends on the 
risk of relapse and CR status. MMUD or cords 
and haplo-HCT are generally reserved for HR 
disease or early relapses.
Patients and their siblings should be tissue-­
typed at diagnosis. In the absence of a HLA 
MFD, an UD and a CBU, a search should be initi­
ated as soon as possible after induction course 1 
for patients with IR or PR cytogenetics. Donors 
should be selected using the selection hierarchy 
of the national group. Medium-/high-resolution 
typing is required for adult URD (HLA A, B, C, 
HLA-DRB1, HLA-DQB1 and HLA-DPB1) and 
unrelated cords (HLA A, B, C and DR loci). The 
risk of relapse does not direct the need for trans­
plantation, but the HLA discrepancy which is 
acceptable. MFD or well-MUD should be identi­
fied for CR1 patients, whilst mismatched donors 
and cords or haplo-HCT should be reserved for 
high-risk disease, CR2, or refractory disease. For 
MFD/UD, BM is the preferred stem cell source, 
but the use of peripheral blood stem cell (PBSC) 
is permissible. The use of PBSC from mis­
matched donors should be avoided wherever 
possible.
