89 經典何杰金氏淋巴瘤 — Carmen Martínez、Ali Bazarbachi 和 Anna Sureda
作者單位：Carmen Martínez — HCT 科，血液學系，血液學和腫瘤學研究所，巴塞隆納醫院診所，巴塞隆納大學，巴塞隆納，西班牙 (cmarti@clinic.cat)。 Ali Bazarbachi — BMT 項目，貝魯特美國大學醫學中心內科系，黎巴嫩貝魯特 (bazarbac@aub.edu.lb)。 Anna Sureda — 西班牙加泰隆尼亞巴塞隆納加泰隆尼亞腫瘤醫院研究所血液科和幹細胞移植計畫 (asureda@iconologia.net)。
〔89.1 定義與流行病學〕HL 是源自生發中心或生發中心後 B 細胞的惡性腫瘤。癌細胞僅占腫瘤少數，周圍環繞由淋巴球、嗜酸性球、嗜中性球、組織球與漿細胞構成的反應性發炎微環境。惡性細胞可為具特徵性的多核巨細胞或大型單核細胞，合稱 Hodgkin 與 Reed–Sternberg（HRS）細胞。HL 約占新診斷淋巴瘤的 10%。歐洲每年發生率為每 100,000 人 2.2 例，死亡率為每 100,000 人 0.7 例。男性較女性常見；發生率在年輕成人及 60 歲以上族群達高峰，過去二十年大致未變。
89.2 診斷 應根據 WHO 分類，從足夠大的手術標本或切除淋巴結活檢中進行病理診斷，為新鮮冷凍和福馬林固定樣本提供足夠的材料（Eichenauer 等，2014）。
89.3 分類 HL 分為經典型（cHL，由 HRS 細胞的存在定義）或結節性淋巴球為主型 (NLPHL)。 cHL和NLPHL惡性細胞的免疫表型差異顯著，有助於診斷。 cHL 存在四種亞型（結節性硬化症、混合細胞性、富含淋巴細胞和淋巴細胞耗盡），它們在表現、受累部位、流行病學以及與 EBV 的關聯方面有所不同。然而，所有亞型的管理大致相似。 NLPHL 具有獨特的臨床病程，僅佔 HL 病例的不到 5%。雖然在最近的第五版世界衛生組織血淋巴腫瘤分類中，NLPHL 仍然是本質上的分類。
診斷實體不變，在 2022 年國際成熟淋巴腫瘤共識分類中，NLPHL 現更名為結節性淋巴細胞為主的 B 細胞淋巴瘤 (NLPBL)，以認識到明顯的病理、生物學和臨床差異（Alaggio 等人，2022 年；Campo 等人，2022 年）。
〔89.4 危險因子〕早期疾病（I–IIA 期）預後極佳，許多試驗的 OS 超過 90%；晚期疾病（IIB、III–IV 期）的 OS 為 75–90%。早期疾病的危險因子包括縱膈腫塊大小、年齡、紅血球沉降速率、淋巴結區數、B 症狀，以及混合細胞型或淋巴球耗竭型組織學。EORTC、GHSG、NCCN 與加拿大國家癌症研究所分別建立整合這些因子的風險分層系統，現均用於臨床。晚期疾病危險因子包括白蛋白 <4 g/dL、血紅素 <10.5 g/dL、男性、年齡 ≥45 歲、IV 期、白血球 ≥15 × 10^9/L，以及淋巴球減少（淋巴球低於白血球的 8%，及／或絕對淋巴球 <0.6 × 10^9/L）；國際預後評分每項 1 分（Eichenauer et al. 2014）。
89.5 第一線治療 cHL 患者的治療主要以疾病的臨床分期和預後因素為指導。早期疾病患者通常接受化療 (ABVD) 加 RTx 的合併治療。對於疾病預後良好和不良的患者，化療量和放療劑量有所不同。化療（ABVD、升級BEACOPP 或Stanford V）是晚期患者的主要治療方法，RTx 可用於某些患者作為鞏固治療（Eichenauer 等，2014）。 PET-CT 掃描適應療法越來越多地使用，允許治療降級以減少毒性或在腫瘤控制不足的情況下升級（Johnson 等人，2016 年；Casasnovas 等人，2019 年）。 Echelon-1 研究的數據表明，當用 brentuximab vedotin 取代 ABVD 中的博萊黴素時，晚期 HL 一線治療的總體生存率得到改善（Ansell 等人，2022）。
89.6 Auto-HCT 前的第二線治療 復發或難治性 cHL 的治療原則如表 89.1 所示（von Tresckow 和 Moskowitz 2016）。全部
表 89.1 復發或難治性 cHL 的處理原則 新活檢 – 如果在主要治療結束後 ≥12 個月內復發，則必須進行新活檢，以排除其他診斷。強烈建議疑似復發 <12 個月的患者 – 如果有明顯的原發性難治性疾病，只有在新的疾病部位懷疑有進展時，才建議對 HL 進行組織學確認。
對於治療期間原發部位有明顯放射學進展的患者，可能不需要進行活檢 放射學評估 – 建議進行全身 CT 掃描，注射對比染料和 PET 進行進一步比較 治療 – 搶救治療後進行大劑量化療和自體 HCT 目前被認為是復發性 cHL 患者的護理標準 – 沒有研究比較不同治療方案的有效性治療前應評估心臟和肺功能 – 如果有指徵，應在治療前提出生殖諮詢 – 挽救性化療的目標：產生反應（腫瘤仍對化學敏感），這對自體 HCT 後的結果有重大影響。 PET 陰性的實現定義了化療敏感性，並且應該是挽救性化療的目標
基於化療的挽救方案與血液學毒性有關。 10-24% 的病例報告有感染和嗜中性球減少性發燒。觀察到腎毒性、肝毒性、黏膜炎和胃腸道毒性的發生率<10%。所有方案的造血幹細胞動員似乎都足夠。不同救助方案的效果如表 89.2 所示。
89.7 自體 HCT 自體 HCT 目前被認為是復發/難治性 (R/R) cHL 患者的標準治療方法。兩項具有里程碑意義的隨機臨床試驗，即 1993 年的英國國家淋巴瘤調查 (BNLI) 和 2002 年的德國霍奇金研究組 (GHSG)/EBMT HD-R1 聯合試驗，比較了高劑量化療後進行的自體 HCT 與化療，結果表明，在 EFS 和 FFTF 方面，自體 HCT 優於傳統化療的優勢；然而，沒有顯著性提高作業系統。 HL 中自體 HCT 的 EBMT 目前適應症見
表 89.3（Snowden 等人，2022 年）。
89.7.1 幹細胞來源和調理方案 來自動員的 PB 的造血幹細胞是自體 HCT 的首選幹細胞來源。儘管準備方案的選擇各不相同並且通常基於機構經驗，但 BEAM 是首選。標準 BEAM 包括 BCNU（300 mg/m² × 1，第 -6 天）、VP（200 mg/m²，第 -5 至 -2 天）、Ara-C（200 mg/m² bid，第 -5 至 -2 天）和 MEL（140 mg/kg/天 × 1，第 -1 天）。 CY、BCNU 和 VP (CBV) 方案在北美也常用。不建議使用基於 TBI 的治療方案，因為發生繼發性惡性腫瘤的風險較高。
【表89.2 挽救治療方案】傳統化療：DHAP（ORR 89%，CR 21%）；ESHAP（ORR 67%，CR 50%）；ICE（ORR 88%，CR 67%）。含 gemcitabine 方案：IGEV（ORR 81%，CR 54%）；GVD（ORR 70%，CR 19%）；GDP（ORR 62%，CR 1%）；BeGEV（ORR 83%，CR 73%）。非化療策略：brentuximab vedotin（BV）用於至少兩線多藥化療失敗且不適合 auto-HCT 者（ORR 50%，CR 12%）；pembrolizumab 用於難治性 cHL 或至少三線治療後復發者（ORR 69%，CR 22%）。新藥合併化療（目前未核准此適應症；以下為 PET 陰性反應率）：序貫 BV→ICE 77%、nivolumab→ICE 86%；合併 BV+bendamustine 74%、BV+ESHAP 70%、BV+ICE 69%、BV+DHAP 90%、BV+nivolumab 62%、pembrolizumab+GVD 95%、pembrolizumab+ICE 86%。
【表89.3：EBMT 對 cHL 自體 HCT 的現行適應症；Snowden et al. 2022】首次完全緩解：通常不建議，證據等級 I。化療敏感性復發且未曾接受自體 HCT：標準治療，證據等級 I。化療敏感性復發且曾接受自體 HCT：臨床選項，證據等級 III。難治性疾病：臨床選項，證據等級 III。
BEAM的晚期毒性包括肺部併發症（慢性間質纖維化和肺部彌散能力下降，21%）、感染（30%）、代謝症候群（17%）、心血管併發症（12%）、繼發性腫瘤（20%）和其他毒性（20%）。 NRM 最常見的原因是隨後發生的惡性腫瘤（與一般人群相比，風險增加 12 倍）。
89.7.2 預後因素 許多報告試驗一致的自體 HCT 後結果的不良預後因素包括初次誘導失敗、初始緩解持續時間 <3 個月、誘導治療 12 個月內復發、結外疾病、B 症狀、復發晚期、對挽救性化療耐藥和移植時持續性疾病。
〔89.7.3 自體 HCT 結果〕自體 HCT 前疾病狀態／NRM／5 年 OS／5 年 PFS：化療敏感性疾病為 0–18%／75%／50%；原發難治性疾病為 0–18%／30–36%／15–38%。
89.7.4 自體 HCT 後的鞏固治療 Brentuximab vedotin (BV) 是目前唯一被批准用於有復發或進展風險的患者在自體 HCT 後鞏固治療的藥物。該批准是在 III 期 AETHERA 試驗結果出來後獲得的。在這項多中心隨機試驗中，329 名復發或難治性 HL 患者在自體 HCT 後被分配接受最多 16 個週期的 BV 鞏固治療或安慰劑。 BV 組患者的 PFS 顯著較長（中位 PFS 為 43 個月 vs. 24 個月，P = 0.0013）。當病人依照危險因子的數量進行分組時，危險因子的數量越多，鞏固組的益處就越顯著（Moskowitz et al. 2015）。
89.8 串聯自體 HCT 多個小組已經探索了串聯移植方法，以改善具有不良危險因子的患者的移植後結果。這些研究表明，串聯自體 HCT 是可行的，並且與 0-5% 的 NRM、54-84% 的 5 年 OS 和 49-55% 的 5 年 PFS 相關（Smith 等人，2018）。根據這些結果，風險適應串聯自體 HCT 可以被視為低風險患者的一種選擇，但將 PET 結果與 BV 和檢查點抑制劑等新藥相結合可能有助於完善第二次自體 HCT 的需求，並可能改善這些患者的預後。
〔89.9 自體 HCT 後疾病復發〕過去，自體 HCT 後復發患者的整體預後不佳。早期復發、IV 期、腫瘤體積大、體能狀態不佳及自體 HCT 失敗時年齡 ≥50 歲，均是不良結果的預測因子（Jethava et al. 2017；Kallam and Armitage 2018；Lapo and Blum 2016）。EBMT 最近一項納入 1781 名成人、涵蓋 12 年的大型回溯分析顯示，復發後 4 年 OS 顯著改善：2006–2008 年復發者為 32%，2015–2017 年復發者升至 63%（Bazarbachi et al. 2022）。存活隨自體 HCT 至復發間隔延長而提高；年齡較大、體能狀態差、bulky disease、結外疾病及復發時有 B 症狀則與較差 OS 相關。可採治療相當異質（表89.4）（Martínez et al. 2013；Hahn et al. 2013）。
【表89.4 自體 HCT 後復發的治療選項】brentuximab vedotin（Chen et al. 2016）：已核准用於自體 HCT 後復發 cHL，ORR 75%、CR 34%、PFS 5.6 個月。Nivolumab：已核准用於自體 HCT 與 BV 後復發，ORR 69%、CR 16%、1 年 OS 92%、中位 PFS 12–18 個月。Pembrolizumab：已核准用於自體 HCT 後復發，ORR 69%、CR 22%、6 個月 PFS 72%。含 gemcitabine 化療：ORR 69–86%、EFS 10%。Bendamustine：ORR 53–78%、CR 29–33%。Lenalidomide：ORR 19%。Histone deacetylase inhibitors：ORR 4–74%、CR 0–4%、1 年 OS 78%。Everolimus：ORR 47%。Tislelizumab：ORR 82%、CR 63%。CAR-T cells：ORR 39–100%、CR 50%。第二次自體 HCT：NRM 15%，5 年 OS 與 PFS 均 30%。異體移植：見 89.10 節。
89.10 同種異體 HCT 對於自體 HCT 後復發或進展的 cHL 患者，異體 HCT 仍被認為是一種治癒性治療策略（Peggs 等，2008）。我們對 allo-HCT 療效的了解依賴於多項回顧性分析的結果，其中一些是基於註冊的 II 期前瞻性臨床試驗（Sureda 等人，2012 年），其中包括少量患者，而回顧性分析在捐贈者與無捐贈者策略中表明，allo-HCT 在 PFS 和 OS 方面均具有顯著優勢。 cHL 中異基因 HCT 的 EBMT 目前適應症如表 89.5 所示。
89.10.1 幹細胞來源、供體類型和調理方案 來自動員 PB 的 HSC 是異體 HCT 的首選幹細胞來源。單倍體供體的使用增加了某些系列中 BM 的使用。後來的研究表明，在這種情況下使用 PB 的 GVHD 發生率沒有顯著差異。近年來，隨著 PT-CY 方法的引入，半相合供體的使用顯著增加。透過這種類型的移植觀察到的有趣結果已經減少了 EBMT 報告中心 MUD 和 MRD 的使用（Gayoso 等人，2016）。回顧性地，EBMT 和 CIBMTR 的註冊研究表明，基於 PT-CY 的單倍體 HCT 的結果與 MRD 和 MUD 的結果相似；單倍體相合方法的 GVHD 累積發生率似乎較低，並且在某些系列中轉化為更好的 PFS-cGVHD（Martínez 等人，2017）。超過 50% 接受異體 HCT 治療的 HL 患者接受 RIC 方案。 RIC 方案已被證明可以顯著降低移植後的 NRM，但也可以增加移植後的 RI（Sureda 等，2008）。
沒有正式的前瞻性臨床試驗證明給定調理方案相對於其他方案的優越性。回顧性分析表明，與不含 TBI 的方案相比，低劑量含 TBI 的方案與較高的 RI 和較低的存活率相關。 EBMT 登記處最近的一項回顧性分析表明，隨著現代移植實踐，與 HL 的 MAC 相關的 NRM 已大幅下降，導致與 RIC 移植相比，EFS 有更好的趨勢（Genadieva-Stavrik 等，2016）。因此，MAC 可能是根據具體情況考慮的選項。
【表89.5：EBMT 對 cHL 異體 HCT 的現行適應症；Snowden et al. 2022】首次緩解：MSD、MUD 與替代供者皆通常不建議（GNR），證據等級 III。化療敏感性復發、未曾自體 HCT：MSD 與 MUD 為發展中選項、證據等級 III；替代供者通常不建議、證據等級 III。化療敏感性復發、曾自體 HCT：MSD、MUD 與替代供者皆為標準，證據等級 II。難治性疾病：MSD 與 MUD 為發展中選項、證據等級 II；替代供者為發展中選項、證據等級 III。替代供者包括 MMUD、haploidentical donor 與 CB；GNR＝通常不建議。
89.10.2 預後因子 與allo-HCT 後長期結果相關的最重要的不良預後因素是移植前的疾病狀態。然而，手術前 PET 陰性 CR 的影響並不像自體 HCT 設定那樣直接。
89.10.3 新藥時代 Allo-HCT 的應用 隨著新藥的推出，allo-HCT 在患者自體 HCT 後復發/進展中的作用和定位不太清楚。在過去 2 年中，用於此適應症的異基因 HCT 數量似乎有所減少。 BV 已被用作異體 HCT 的橋樑。沒有證據表明在最後一次 BV 劑量和 HCT 第 0 天之間需要有一個清除期。 allo-HCT 之前給予的 BV 週期數通常在四到六次之間。移植前使用 BV 不會改變移植後相關毒性，並且可能透過改善異體 HCT 前的體能狀態和疾病狀態來改善結果。它也可能讓更多患者成功接受移植，並有可能降低慢性 GVHD 的發生率（Bazarbachi et al. 2018）。 allo-HCT 先前的檢查點抑制劑（nivolumab、pembrolizumab）似乎非常有效，具有良好的生存結果 (Dada 2018)。然而，追蹤時間仍然太短，有人認為它們的使用可能與移植相關毒性（急性 GVHD、SOS/VOD、移植後超急性發燒綜合症）的增加有關。
一般建議在allo-HCT前保留檢查點抑制劑至少6週，並使用PTCY預防GVHD。是否對自體 HCT 後復發的患者進行異體移植的最終決定可能取決於潛在疾病的風險狀況以及與移植相關的風險。
〔89.10.4 異體 HCT 結果〕異體 HCT 前疾病狀態／NRM／3 年 OS／3 年 PFS：化療敏感性疾病為 15–20%／60–70%／40–50%；化療難治性疾病為 20–30%／40–50%／20–30%。
89.10.5 Allo-HCT 後疾病復發 疾病復發的預後較差。治療方案多樣且異質（表 89.6），在某些情況下，安寧療護是唯一可行的治療方案。
89.11 作者推薦的治療演算法（由 Yethava 等人修改）
【表89.6 異體 HCT 後復發的治療選項】DLI 單獨治療：ORR 33–54%。DLI+brentuximab vedotin：ORR 69%（CR 54%、PR 15%），PFS 5.5 個月。DLI+bendamustine：ORR 55%（CR 16%、PR 39%），PFS 6 個月。Brentuximab vedotin（Gopal et al. 2012）：ORR 50–69%、CR 31–38%、PR 37%，中位 PFS 7–8 個月。Nivolumab（Herbaux et al. 2017）：ORR 77–95%、CR 42–55%、PR 40–52%，1 年 PFS 58%。【治療流程內容】原發難治性 cHL 或第一次復發 cHL，先以第二／第三線化療測試化療敏感性，之後進行自體 HCT；高復發風險者考慮 BV 鞏固。自體 HCT 後復發時，依既往 BV 使用或抗藥性、治療反應，選擇 BV、nivolumab／pembrolizumab、前瞻性臨床試驗（PCT）、觀察或異體 HCT；必要時採傳統挽救治療／PCT。對年輕、體能良好、疾病有反應且有適當供者者，可考慮異體 HCT；灰色箭頭所示兩方案須權衡患者不良預後因子、移植相關共病並與患者充分討論。
89.12 復發/難治性 cHL 患者中 Auto-HCT 和 Allo-HCT 的長期結果（EBMT 資料庫，經許可） 復發/難治性 cHL 中 auto-HCT 隨時間推移的 OS 復發/難治性 cHL 中 allo-HCT 隨時間推移的 OS
【重點】• 自體 HCT 仍是原發難治性／化療敏感性第一次復發患者的標準治療。未來藉由更精確的患者選擇、更有效的挽救策略，以及對自體 HCT 後高復發風險患者施行鞏固治療，結果可能進一步改善。• 對自體 HCT 後復發者，異體 HCT 是唯一具治癒潛力的治療選項；haploidentical donor 與標靶治療的引入，正改變此情境下異體 HCT 的使用方式。

Michael H. Albert, Arjan Lankester, 
Andrew Gennery, and Bénédicte Neven 
90.1	
Introduction 
Inborn errors of immunity (IEI) arise from 
genetic defects that lead to abnormalities in 
immune cell development or function with a 
wide spectrum in severity and clinical manifesta­
tions. These include infectious, autoimmune, 
autoinflammatory, hematological, and malignant 
presentations. Allo-HCT provides a life-saving 
and curative treatment modality in many but not 
all of these disorders by replacing the defective 
hematopoietic cell lineage(s) by those from 
healthy allogeneic donors. Other management

90.3	
SCID 
The overall frequency of SCID was for a long 
time estimated to be 1  in 50,000–100,000 live 
births. However, in recent years, newborn screen­
ing programs making use of the T-cell receptor 
excision circles (TREC) technology have demon­
strated that the frequency may actually be two- or 
more-fold higher with clear geographical and 
ethnic differences (Kwan et  al. 2014; Rechavi 
et al. 2017; Speckmann et al. 2023). 
90.2
­
­
In the absence of newborn screening pro­
grams or positive family history, most patients 
present within the first 3–6 months with severe, 
recurrent, or opportunistic, often life-threaten­
ing, infections, the most common being 
Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia. Other com­
mon symptoms include diarrhea, dermatitis, and 
failure to thrive. Survival in SCID patients 
depends on expeditious T-cell reconstitution, 
and in the absence of successful HCT, or autolo­
gous stem cell gene therapy, most children usu­
ally die during the first year of life. As many as 
50% of SCID patients are engrafted with mater­
nal T-cells but in most instances these cells do 
not 
initiate 
GvHD. 
Transfusion-associated 
GvHD, on the other hand, is frequently lethal in 
SCID, and any patient with a possible diagnosis 
of SCID must receive irradiated blood products.

Europe, the presentation of SCID patient is about 
to change to mostly healthy-appearing newborns 
without signs of active infection. However, not 
all peri- and early postnatal infections like, i.e., 
CMV will be avoidable in infants identified by 
NBS (Speckmann et  al. 2023; Thakar et  al. 
2023). 
90.3.1	 General Principles in Allo-HCT 
for SCID 
The Stem CEll Transplant for primary Immune 
Deficiencies in Europe (SCETIDE) registry has 
collected data on SCID transplants comprising 
50  years of HCT experience, and a number of

important publications have documented the out­
comes and important risk factors (Fischer et al. 
1990; Antoine et al. 2003; Gennery et al. 2010; 
Lankester et al. 2022). Recently, studies from the 
North American group have reported similar 
findings (Pai et  al. 2014; Heimall et  al. 2017, 
Thakar et al. 2023). The major factors positively 
influencing outcome reported in these studies 
include:
	1.	 Absence of infections at HCT
	2.	 Age at transplant <3.5  months or diagnosis 
via NBS
	3.	 Use of MFD and MUD
	4.	 Use of myeloablative conditioning
	5.	 Recovery of naive CD4 T lymphocytes 
>0.5 × 103/μL at +1 year after HCT 
90.3.2	 Donor, Graft Source, 
and Conditioning in HCT 
for SCID 
Overall survival for MD (related or unrelated) 
HCT in SCID has improved to over 90% 
(Lankester et  al. 2022; Thakar et  al. 2023). 
Virtually all infants have a haploidentical paren­
tal donor, and this is an alternative option, as the 
donor is readily available. HLA disparity neces­
sitates rigorous in vitro or in vivo TCD in order to 
reduce to risk of GvHD.  Most centers now 
employ 
either 
TCR 
alpha/beta 
depletion 
(Balashov et al. 2015; Shah et al. 2018) or PT-CY 
(Neven et al. 2019). Although promising survival 
rates have been reported, longer follow-up in a 
larger cohort of patients is required to determine 
the position of these approaches. CD34+ selec­
tion of the graft also remains an option in selected 
cases. CB can be a suitable alternative stem cell 
source (Fernandes et  al. 2012). Theoretical 
advantages for using CB stem cells include rapid 
availability, less risk of GvHD compared to adult 
URD, no medical risk to the donor, and a greater 
proliferative life span which might be particu­
larly important in such young recipients. There 
are some specific disadvantages including some­
times slower engraftment, lack of viral-specific 
cytotoxic T-cells, and lack of availability of the 
donor for a boost HCT. 
Although HLA-genoidentical sibling donor 
BM may be infused into SCID recipients without 
any conditioning or GvHD prophylaxis, usually 
only T-cells of donor origin will engraft, and 
myeloid and often B-cells will remain of recipient 
origin. Patients with insufficient myeloid engraft­
ment and/or poor or declining naïve T-cell com­
partments may experience severe complications 
that require a second, conditioned HCT (Riller 
et  al. 2023). Therefore, and if tolerable for the 
patient, conditioning is recommended for all SCID 
patients in order to achieve optimal clinical and 
immunological outcomes (Lankester et al. 2022). 
Individualized approaches making use of ther­
apeutic drug monitoring provide novel and less 
toxic options to improve HCT outcome in these 
vulnerable young infants, while antibody-based 
conditioning approaches that may limit systemic 
toxicity are currently being developed. 
90.3.3	 Omenn’s Syndrome 
Omenn’s syndrome (OS) is characterized by 
SCID typically associated with the triad of eryth­
roderma, 
hepatosplenomegaly, 
and 
­lymphadenopathy. There is a marked eosino­
philia and a variable number of autologous, acti­
vated, and oligoclonal T lymphocytes, which 
infiltrate target organs and are generally poorly 
responsive to mitogens. Whereas outcomes in 
HCT for OS were traditionally inferior compared 
to classical SCID, results have improved in recent 
years (Gennery et al. 2010; Heimall et al. 2017; 
Thakar et al. 2023). The overall mortality in these 
studies was lower than previously reported and 
was due to early recognition of OS and rapid ini­
tiation of treatment with topical/systemic immune 
suppression with steroids, cyclosporin A, and 
T-cell directed serotherapy to control immune 
dysreactivity before proceeding to HCT. 
90.4	
Non-SCID IEI 
The landscape of HCT in non-SCID IEI has 
dramatically changed over the last decade 
•	 New genetic causes of IEI are being described 
in accelerating frequency thanks to next-­

generation sequencing techniques (Bousfiha 
et  al. 2022). Functional consequences of 
genetic variants in the same gene can be broad, 
from complete or partial loss to gain of func­
tion resulting in different clinical phenotypes. 
Somatic variants may also occur, mimicking 
disease caused by germline variants. 
•	 The concept of “pure” immunodeficiencies 
with predisposition to infections has been 
abandoned with many newly described auto­
immune, auto-inflammatory conditions, or 
syndromal disorders with immunodeficiency. 
Many of these diseases can be cured by HCT, 
while in syndromal disorders only the hema­
topoietic portion of the disease can be cor­
rected, which may nevertheless be indicated 
and result in not just increased survival but 
also quality of life in selected patients. 
•	 HCT outcomes have further improved with 
around 90% OS and low GVHD rates after 
MSD or MUD HCT in many non-SCID IEI, 
like, i.e., CGD and WAS (Chiesa et al. 2020; 
Albert et al. 2022b). 
•	 In general, donor availability has become less 
of a factor in the decision-making process to 
go for HCT. Current outcomes of MFD and 
MUD are highly similar, while results with 
mismatched/haplo-identical HCT are gradu­
ally approaching those obtained with MD 
especially when performed in experienced 
centers (Shah et al. 2018; Neven et al. 2019; 
Kurzay et al. 2019). 
•	 The importance of DFS and GRFS as com­
pared to OS is increasingly appreciated and 
addressed in medium- to long-term outcome 
studies, also in comparison to non-HCT 
approaches (Speckmann et al. 2017; Barzaghi 
et al. 2018; Albert et al. 2022b). 
•	 More IEI patients are discovered with very 
mild or atypical phenotypes of well-known 
IEI, and these often hypomorphic genetic 
variants are especially challenging with 
respect to timely recognition and management 
(Notarangelo et al. 2016; Schuetz et al. 2023). 
Especially in these “milder” cases, often rec­
ognized in adolescence and adulthood, quality 
of life is increasingly a factor in HCT decision 
making (Cole et  al. 2013; Cheminant et  al. 
2023). 
•	 Adolescents and young adults with IEI are 
increasingly appreciated as candidates for 
HCT, and outcomes are encouragingly good 
(Albert et al. 2018; Fox et al. 2018), with sur­
vival determined by the underlying IEI entity, 
pre HCT comorbidities, and organ damage 
rather than age at HCT or donor type (Albert 
et al. 2022a). 
The consequence of these developments has 
been that many more patients with IEI are today 
considered for, referred for, and counselled about 
HCT. 
90.4.1	 Indication 
One of the most challenging aspects of transplant 
for non-SCID IEI is the question of whether a 
high-intensity, curative therapy with HCT is 
­indicated. For some IEI (like FHLH), the imme­
diate HCT indication is clear, while for many 
other IEI this will be less evident because of the 
high interindividual variability of the clinical 
phenotype. In diseases where long-term progno­
sis is known to be poor, even presymptomatic 
patients can be subjected to HCT (like i.e. 
X-CGD). A genetic diagnosis is increasingly 
made in IEI patients and may support the deci­
sion to proceed to HCT. Similarly, a positive fam­
ily history with severe disease manifestations or a 
known poor long-term prognosis of the disease 
may justify early preemptive HCT.  Still, given 
the highly variable and frequently unpredictable 
disease course in IEI, a genetic diagnosis alone 
without clinical manifestations is in many IEI an 
insufficient reason to perform HCT.  In all IEI 
patients, the decision to proceed with HCT 
should always include interdisciplinary discus­
sions with patients and their families, also 
addressing issues like fertility/family-planning, 
school/work, other psycosocial factors, and qual­
ity of life.


90.3
In IEI, it is the goal is to establish sufficient long-­
term donor chimerism in the affected cell lineage, 
while reducing short- and long-term toxicity to a 
minimum. The required degree of donor chime­
rism for effective and sustainable disease correc­
tion varies depending on the type of IEI and has 
not yet been established for all entities. 
Accordingly, the graft source, serotherapy, and 
type of conditioning regimen should be chosen 
depending on many factors, including IEI entity, 
age of patient, donor type, active infections, 
comorbidities, organ damage, and experience of 
the center. 
Conventional MAC preparation with BU-/ 
CY-based regimens has historically been associ­
ated with significant treatment-related toxicity 
and TRM.  The IEWP of EBMT had begun in 
2005 to publish detailed recommendations for 
conditioning of IEI as discussed above (Lankester 
et al. 2021). These recommendations include:
	1.	 Replacement of CY with FLU, as the combi­
nation of BU/FLU with pharmacokinetic tar­
geting of BU AUC appears to be better 
tolerated in these patients.
	2.	 The option to replace BU with a structural 
analogue, TREO, which is similarly immuno- 
and myelosuppressive but causes less hepatic 
SOS/VOD (Slatter et al. 2018).
	3.	 Addition of a submyeloablative dosing regi­
men for BU/FLU (Güngör et al. 2014).
	4.	 Establishing RIC to achieve stable engraft­
ment of immunocompetent donor cells with

reduced procedure-related morbidity and 
mortality (Veys 2010).
	5.	 An alkylator-low regimen for radiosensitive 
disorders (Slack et al. 2018). 
90.5	
HCT for Radiosensitive IEI 
Patients with radiosensitive IEI such as Nijmegen-­
breakage syndrome, DNA ligase 4 deficiency, 
Cernunnos deficiency, or DNA-PKcs deficiency 
including those with a SCID phenotype are 
increasingly being identified and considered for 
HCT. As many of the conditioning regimens are 
particularly damaging to DNA, less toxic regi­
mens are required to successfully treat these 
patients (Slack et al. 2018). No definitive studies 
are available, but low-dose FLU/CY regimens 
like the one suggested by the EBMT IEWP 
guidelines have been proven effective and safe 
(Lankester et al. 2021). 
90.6	
Alternative Therapies 
Alternative treatments to HCT have been devel­
oped for specific IEI over the last three decades. 
90.6.1	 Enzyme Replacement Therapy 
(ERT) for Adenosine 
Deaminase Deficiency 
(ADA-SCID) 
Enzyme replacement in ADA deficiency with 
PEG-ADA is administered weekly or twice 
weekly by IM injection and leads to rapid meta­
bolic correction which is followed by cellular and 
humoral immune reconstitution. The extent of 
immune recovery is variable, and a significant 
number (~50%) remain on Ig replacement. Over 
a longer time period, patients show a decline in 
T-cell numbers and remain lymphopenic. Long-­
term follow-up shows that patients may remain 
clinically well, but clinical problems can arise 
and a number of cases of EBV-related lymphoma 
have been reported (Chan et al. 2005). Given the

improved outcomes of HCT and GT in recent 
times, ERT is predominantly considered as a 
bridge to stem cell-based curative therapy. 
90.6.2	 Gene Therapy for Specific IEI 
Autologous stem cell gene therapy (GT) via 
vector-­mediated transfer of healthy copies of an 
affected gene into autologous CD34+ cells has 
progressed from a highly experimental therapy to 
the first licensed gene therapy for an IEI (ADA-­
SCID) within the last two decades. One of the 
major conceptual advantages of GT is the elimi­
nation of the inherent risk of GVHD associated 
with allogeneic HCT procedures. 
Clinical trials performed with gamma retrovi­
ral vectors for ADA-SCID, X-linked SCID 
(SCID-X1), chronic granulomatous disease 
(CGD), and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS) 
demonstrated that gene therapy can be an effec­
tive treatment option in patients lacking an HLA-­
identical donor (Hacein-Bey-Abina et al. 2002; 
Boztug et al. 2010; Stein et al. 2010; Aiuti et al. 
2009). However, a high rate of insertional muta­
genesis was observed in trials for SCID-X1, 
WAS, and CGD (Ott et  al. 2006; Hacein-Bey-­
Abina et al. 2003; Braun et al. 2014). This has 
prompted the development of safer vectors based 
on self-inactivating retroviral or lentiviral vec­
tors. Currently, a number of trials are ongoing or 
concluded for a number of IEI. All share the con­
cept of submyeloablative conditioning followed 
by the infusion of autologous stem/progenitor 
cells transduced with the wildtype gene. 
Promising results were published, especially for 
ADA-SCID (Kohn et  al. 2021; Cicalese et  al. 
2016), WAS (Ferrua et al. 2019) and SCID-X1 
(Mamcarz et al. 2019). It is expected that gene 
editing approaches as an alternative for gene 
addition technologies will be developed for stem 
cell based GT in the next few years and may 
potentially also be employed to correct mature 
cells in diseases like, i.e., CD40 ligand defi­
ciency, CTLA4, and IPEX. 
In theory, autologous stem cell gene therapy 
offers the appealing prospect of avoiding allo­
immune reactions such as GVHD or rejection 
and a lower conditioning-related toxicity com­
pared to allo-HCT.  But its exact role in treat­
ment algorithms still needs to be defined in the 
absence of comparative studies. Also, logistic, 
regulatory, and economic hurdles still have to be 
overcome before its widespread application in 
the treatment of IEI. Nevertheless, it has wid­
ened the therapeutic repertoire for patients with 
some IEI.  The rapid evolution of novel gene 
correction approaches has the potential to lead 
to even safer and more effective treatment 
options. 
90.6.3	 Targeted Therapies 
The unravelling of new genetic IEI entities, espe­
cially those caused by gain-of-function (GOF) 
variants and their pathophysiology, has for the 
first time opened the possibility to treat these dis­
eases with highly specific, often small molecule 
inhibitors, some of which are already approved 
for other indications. These include but are not 
limited to abatacept for CTLA4 haploinsuffi­
ciency, ruxolitinib and other JAK-inhibitors for 
STAT1 GOF, leniolisib for APDS, etanercept for 
ADA2 deficiency, and IL-1-targeted therapies 
(anakinra, rilonacept, and canakinumab) for 
auto-inflammatory recurrent fever syndromes 
(Ochs and Petroni 2018; Ombrello et al. 2019; 
Rao et al. 2023). We can expect that more sub­
stances (like, i.e., IL-18BP for XIAP) may be 
licensed or repurposed for the treatment of IEI in 
the future. At this point in time, the exact role of 
these agents in the treatment algorithm of IEI is 
unclear. Ideally, they could make HCT unneces­
sary for some patients. On the other hand, con­
cerns about long-term toxicity, infection risk, and 
lymphoma risk exist. In any case, in some patients 
with excessive autoimmunity and/or inflamma­
tion, these therapies can be viewed as an ideal 
bridge to HCT and considered as a remission 
induction strategy to control the underlying IEI, 
because they have the potential to bring the 
patient into the best possible clinical condition 
for HCT.

Key Points 
•	 IEI require a tailored approach to HCT 
management, and disease-specific trans­
plant protocols have been developed for 
these diseases, including stem cell-­
based GT. 
•	 Preceding 
comorbidity, 
particularly 
infectious complications at HCT and 
concurrent end-organ damage, adversely 
affects outcome. For many diseases, 
HCT at an early age is recommended. 
•	 Alternative therapies—often as a bridge 
to transplant—are increasingly avail­
able to improve patient outcomes.

zh: 先天免疫缺陷 IEI
points: IEI 需疾病特異性策略，不能把所有免疫缺陷視為相同移植適應症。
活動性感染與既有器官損傷會使移植風險上升，許多疾病宜早期診斷及治療。
是否需要 conditioning、所需 donor chimerism 與供者選擇，取決於受影響細胞與疾病機轉。
酵素替代、標靶免疫治療或基因治療可在特定疾病作替代或移植橋接。
長期需追蹤免疫功能、感染、疫苗及非造血表現。
question: IEI 是否都能使用同一套前處理？
answer: 不能。不同缺陷的毒性敏感度、植入需求與感染背景不同，需採疾病專屬方案。
trap: 年幼移植的利益須與感染及器官狀態一起評估。
fullTranslationText:
【第90章：先天免疫缺陷（IEI）】作者：Michael H. Albert、Arjan Lankester、Andrew Gennery、Bénédicte Neven。〔90.1 導論〕IEI 源於造成免疫細胞發育或功能異常的遺傳缺陷，疾病嚴重度及臨床表現範圍很廣，可表現為感染、自體免疫、自體發炎、血液異常或惡性疾病。對許多、但並非所有這類疾病，allo-HCT 可透過健康異體供者的細胞，取代有缺陷的造血細胞系，提供救命且具治癒性的治療。其他選擇包括酵素替代治療、將基因導入自體造血幹細胞，以及下述標靶治療；在特定 IEI 中，它們可作為 HCT 的替代或橋接治療。
〔90.2 疾病〕IEI 可概分為嚴重複合型免疫缺陷（SCID）與非 SCID。非 SCID 可再依國際免疫學會聯盟（IUIS）先天免疫缺陷委員會提出的表型分類細分；此分類涵蓋超過 500 種 IEI 遺傳病因（表90.1）。
【作者任職機構】M. H. Albert：德國 Munich，Ludwig-Maximilians Universität／Dr. von Hauner University Children’s Hospital，Pediatric SCT Program；michael.albert@med.uni-muenchen.de。A. Lankester：荷蘭 Leiden，Leiden University Medical Center／Willem-Alexander Children’s Hospital，Department of Pediatrics，Stem Cell Transplantation Program；a.lankester@lumc.nl。A. Gennery：英國 Newcastle upon Tyne，Newcastle University／Great North Children’s Hospital，Paediatric Immunology + HSCT；andrew.gennery@newcastle.ac.uk。B. Neven：法國 Paris，Necker Children Hospital／Paris City University，Pediatric Immune-Hematology and Rheumatology Unit；benedicte.neven@aphp.fr。
【表90.1：IUIS IEI 表型分類；Bousfiha 等，2022】① 影響細胞及體液免疫的免疫缺陷（CID）；② 合併其他或症候群特徵的 CID；③ 以抗體缺乏為主；④ 免疫調節失衡；⑤ 吞噬細胞數量及／或功能先天缺陷；⑥ intrinsic／innate immunity 缺陷；⑦ 自體發炎；⑧ 補體缺陷；⑨ 骨髓衰竭；⑩ IEI phenocopies（免疫缺陷擬表型）。
EBMT Inborn Errors Working Party（IEWP）於 2021 年發表更新的 IEI 移植指引及詳細方案（Lankester 等，2021），可於原文所列 EBMT 網址取得。指引依 IEI 類型、病人狀況及年齡，詳列六種不同強度前處理方案的使用建議。
〔90.3 SCID〕SCID 的整體發生率長期被估計為每 50,000–100,000 名活產嬰兒一例。然而，近年運用 T-cell receptor excision circles（TREC）技術的新生兒篩檢顯示，實際發生率可能高出兩倍或更多，而且存在明顯的地理與族群差異（Kwan 等，2014；Rechavi 等，2017；Speckmann 等，2023）。
表90.2列出 SCID 的免疫表型，代表 T、B、NK 細胞分化的單基因遺傳缺陷，導致相應成熟細胞缺失或無法正常作用。
若未實施新生兒篩檢，也沒有陽性家族史，多數患者在出生後 3–6 個月內，出現嚴重、反覆或伺機性感染，常危及生命，最常見者為 Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia。其他常見症狀包括腹瀉、皮膚炎與生長遲滯。SCID 的存活取決於能否迅速重建 T 細胞；若未成功接受 HCT 或自體幹細胞基因治療，多數兒童通常在一歲內死亡。多達 50% 患者有母體 T 細胞植入，但多數情況下不會因此引發 GVHD。相反地，輸血相關 GVHD 在 SCID 常具致命性；任何可能患有 SCID 的患者，都必須接受經照射的血品。
BCG 疫苗可能引發播散性 BCG 感染，rotavirus 疫苗則可能造成持續性腸炎。因此，只要懷疑嚴重 T 細胞缺陷、新生兒篩檢（NBS）陽性，或具有陽性家族史，就應避免所有活性疫苗。隨著歐洲持續導入 NBS，SCID 患者的初次就醫樣貌正轉變為外觀健康、沒有活動性感染的新生兒。但即使經 NBS 及早辨識，也無法避免所有周產期及出生後早期感染，例如 CMV（Speckmann 等，2023；Thakar 等，2023）。
〔90.3.1 SCID 異體 HCT 的一般原則〕歐洲原發性免疫缺陷幹細胞移植登錄庫 SCETIDE，累積了涵蓋 50 年 HCT 經驗的 SCID 移植資料。多篇重要研究描述其結果與風險因子（Fischer 等，1990；Antoine 等，2003；Gennery 等，2010；Lankester 等，2022），北美團隊近期亦有相近發現（Pai 等，2014；Heimall 等，2017；Thakar 等，2023）。與較佳結果相關的主要因素包括：① 移植時沒有感染；② 移植年齡小於 3.5 個月，或由 NBS 診斷；③ 使用相合親屬供者（MFD）或相合非親屬供者（MUD）；④ 使用骨髓消除性前處理；⑤ 移植後一年 naïve CD4 T 淋巴球恢復至 >0.5 × 10³/μL。
【表90.2：SCID 表型與基因；依原表逐欄配對】T−B+NK−：IL2RG（SCID-X1）、JAK3。T−B+NK+：IL7R、CD3D、CD3E、CD247（CD3ζ）、CORO1A、ITPKB、LAT、PTPRC（CD45缺陷）、SLP76；另有胸腺缺陷 FOXN1、PAX1、complete DiGeorge syndrome、CHARGE syndrome。T−B−NK−：ADA、AK2（reticular dysgenesis）、RAC2。T−B−NK+：LIG4、RAG1、RAG2、DCLRE1C（Artemis缺陷）、NHEJ1（Cernunnos XLF）、PRKDC（DNA-PKcs缺陷）。改編自 Bousfiha 等（2022）。星號註：胸腺缺陷可表現為 SCID 或由 NBS 偵測，但 HCT 可能有禁忌，或不是主要治療。
〔90.3.2 SCID 的供者、細胞來源與前處理〕SCID 接受相合親屬或非親屬供者 HCT 的整體存活率，已改善至超過 90%（Lankester 等，2022；Thakar 等，2023）。
幾乎所有嬰兒都有可立即取得的半相合父母供者，可作為替代選擇。HLA 不相合使得嚴格的體外或體內 T-cell depletion（TCD）成為降低 GVHD 風險的必要措施。多數中心現採 TCRαβ 去除或 PT-CY（Balashov 等，2015；Shah 等，2018；Neven 等，2019）；雖有令人鼓舞的存活率，仍需更大群體及更長追蹤來確立其定位。選定病例也可使用 CD34+ selection。臍帶血（CB）亦是合適替代來源（Fernandes 等，2012）。其理論優點包括取得迅速、相較成人非親屬供者較低的 GVHD 風險、供者無醫療風險，以及較長的增殖壽命——對這麼年幼的受者可能特別重要。缺點則包括有時較慢的植入、缺少病毒特異性細胞毒性 T 細胞，以及無法再次向同一供者取得追加移植物。
雖然 SCID 受者可在沒有前處理或 GVHD 預防下，接受 HLA 基因型相合同胞的骨髓，但通常只有供者 T 細胞植入，髓系及常見的 B 細胞仍來自受者。髓系植入不足、naïve T 細胞群不足或持續下降者，可能出現嚴重併發症，而需第二次、且有前處理的 HCT（Riller 等，2023）。因此，只要病人能耐受，建議所有 SCID 患者使用前處理，以取得最佳臨床與免疫學結果（Lankester 等，2022）。
結合 therapeutic drug monitoring 的個別化策略，為這些脆弱的小嬰兒提供較新的低毒性選擇，以改善移植結果；可能限制全身毒性的抗體型前處理，也正在開發中。
〔90.3.3 Omenn syndrome〕Omenn syndrome 是 SCID 的一種表現，典型三徵為紅皮症、肝脾腫大與淋巴結腫大。患者常有明顯嗜酸性球增加，以及數量不一、已活化且寡克隆性的自體 T 淋巴球；這些細胞浸潤標的器官，對 mitogens 的反應通常不佳。過去其移植結果較典型 SCID 差，但近年已改善（Gennery 等，2010；Heimall 等，2017；Thakar 等，2023）。這些研究的整體死亡率較早期報告低，歸因於及早辨識，以及在 HCT 前迅速以局部／全身性 steroids、cyclosporin A 及 T 細胞導向 serotherapy 控制異常免疫反應。
〔90.4 非 SCID 型 IEI〕過去十年，非 SCID IEI 的移植情勢有重大改變。① 隨著 NGS 技術發展，新 IEI 遺傳病因的發現速度加快（Bousfiha 等，2022）。同一基因不同變異可導致完全或部分功能喪失，乃至功能獲得（GOF），而產生不同臨床表型。
體細胞變異也可能造成與生殖系變異疾病相似的表現。
② 「純粹是容易感染的免疫缺陷」這個概念已被揚棄，因為越來越多疾病表現為自體免疫、自體發炎，或合併免疫缺陷的症候群。
許多這類疾病可由 HCT 治癒；若為症候群性疾病，HCT 只能校正造血相關部分，但對選定病人仍可能有適應症，且不只改善存活，也改善生活品質。
③ HCT 結果持續改善：許多非 SCID IEI，如 CGD 與 WAS，接受 MSD 或 MUD 移植後，整體存活率約 90%，GVHD 發生率也低（Chiesa 等，2020；Albert 等，2022b）。
④ 供者可得性在是否接受移植的決策中，影響已較以往小。MFD 與 MUD 的當代結果非常相近；不相合／半相合移植的結果也逐漸接近相合供者，尤其在有經驗的中心（Shah 等，2018；Neven 等，2019；Kurzay 等，2019）。
⑤ 相較於只看 OS，中長期研究越來越重視 DFS 與 GRFS，並將其與非移植策略比較（Speckmann 等，2017；Barzaghi 等，2018；Albert 等，2022b）。
⑥ 越來越多已知 IEI 被發現具有極輕微或非典型表型；這些常為 hypomorphic variants 的病例，在及早診斷與處理上特別困難（Notarangelo 等，2016；Schuetz 等，2023）。
尤其是青春期或成年後才辨識出的「較輕症」病例，生活品質已成為移植決策中越來越重要的考量（Cole 等，2013；Cheminant 等，2023）。
⑦ 青少年及年輕成人 IEI 患者逐漸被視為 HCT 候選人，結果亦令人鼓舞（Albert 等，2018；Fox 等，2018）。存活主要取決於 IEI 類型、移植前共病與器官損傷，而非移植年齡或供者類型（Albert 等，2022a）。
這些發展使更多 IEI 患者被考慮接受移植、被轉介，並接受 HCT 諮詢。
〔90.4.1 適應症〕非 SCID IEI 最困難的問題之一，是是否有必要接受高強度、具治癒性的 HCT。某些疾病如家族性 HLH，其立即移植適應症明確；其他疾病則因臨床表型個體差異很大而不易判斷。若已知長期預後差，例如 X-linked CGD，甚至可在症狀前移植。遺傳診斷越來越普遍，可支持移植決策；家族有嚴重表現，或疾病已知長期預後不佳，也可能合理化早期先發 HCT。但 IEI 病程高度多變且常難預測，許多疾病只有遺傳診斷而無症狀，仍不足以構成移植理由。所有 IEI 的移植決策，都應由跨專科團隊與患者、家屬討論，涵蓋生育／家庭計畫、學校／工作、心理社會因素與生活品質。
〔90.4.2 前處理；見表90.3〕IEI 移植的目標，是在受影響細胞系中建立足夠、長期的供者嵌合，同時將短長期毒性降至最低。要達成有效且持續的疾病校正，所需供者嵌合程度因 IEI 而異，並非所有疾病都已確立。
因此，細胞來源、serotherapy 與前處理方案，應綜合 IEI 類型、年齡、供者、活動性感染、共病、器官損傷及中心經驗選擇。
傳統 BU／CY 骨髓消除性前處理，有顯著治療相關毒性與死亡率。EBMT IEWP 自 2005 年起發表 IEI 前處理詳細建議（Lankester 等，2021），包括：① 用 FLU 取代 CY，因為 BU／FLU 加上以 BU AUC 為目標的藥動學調整，在此族群似乎耐受較佳。
② 可用 BU 的結構類似物 TREO 取代 BU；其免疫及骨髓抑制作用相近，但較少肝臟 SOS／VOD（Slatter 等，2018）。
③ 加入 BU／FLU 的 submyeloablative 劑量方案（Güngör 等，2014）。
④ 建立 RIC，讓具免疫能力的供者細胞穩定植入，同時降低程序相關罹病與死亡（Veys，2010）。
⑤ 對放射敏感疾病使用低 alkylator 劑量方案（Slack 等，2018）。
〔90.5 放射敏感型 IEI 的 HCT〕Nijmegen breakage syndrome、DNA ligase 4、Cernunnos 或 DNA-PKcs 缺陷等放射敏感 IEI，包括具 SCID 表型者，越來越常被辨識並評估 HCT。許多前處理對 DNA 具有強烈損傷作用，因此需較低毒性的方案（Slack 等，2018）。雖然缺乏決定性比較研究，EBMT IEWP 指引建議的低劑量 FLU／CY 等方案，已顯示有效性與安全性（Lankester 等，2021）。
〔90.6 替代治療〕過去三十年，已針對特定 IEI 開發 HCT 以外的治療。
〔90.6.1 ADA-SCID 的酵素替代治療〕ADA 缺陷可用 PEG-ADA，每週一次或兩次肌肉注射，迅速校正代謝異常，接著出現細胞及體液免疫重建。免疫恢復程度不一，仍有約 50% 需要 Ig 替代。時間拉長後，T 細胞數會下降，淋巴球低下持續存在。長期追蹤顯示，病人可維持臨床良好，但仍可能出現問題，且已有數例 EBV 相關淋巴瘤報告（Chan 等，2005）。由於近年 HCT 與基因治療結果改善，ERT 主要被視為通往幹細胞治癒性療法的橋接。
【表90.3：IEWP 建議前處理；Lankester 等，2021】A：BU AUC 85–95 mg·h/L＋FLU 160 mg/m²。B：TREO 30–42 g/m²＋FLU 150–160 mg/m²＋TT 8–10 mg/kg。C：BU AUC 60–70 mg·h/L＋FLU 160–180 mg/m²。D：TREO 30–42 g/m²＋FLU 150–160 mg/m²。E：FLU 150–160 mg/m²＋MEL 140 mg/m²。F：FLU 150 mg/m²＋CY 20–40 mg/kg。數值與組合依原表；療程給藥細節需查完整原指引。
〔90.6.2 特定 IEI 的基因治療〕以載體把正常基因副本導入自體 CD34+ 細胞的幹細胞基因治療，在過去二十年已從高度實驗性治療，發展為首個獲准用於 IEI（ADA-SCID）的基因療法。其重要概念優勢之一，是消除異體 HCT 固有的 GVHD 風險。
ADA-SCID、SCID-X1、CGD 與 WAS 的 γ-retroviral vector 試驗，證實對缺乏 HLA 相合供者者，基因治療可有效（Hacein-Bey-Abina 等，2002；Boztug 等，2010；Stein 等，2010；Aiuti 等，2009）。但 SCID-X1、WAS、CGD 試驗出現較高比例 insertional mutagenesis（Ott 等，2006；Hacein-Bey-Abina 等，2003；Braun 等，2014），促使研究者開發更安全的 self-inactivating retroviral 或 lentiviral vectors。目前多項 IEI 試驗進行中或已結束，共同概念是 submyeloablative 前處理後，回輸導入野生型基因的自體幹／祖細胞。
ADA-SCID（Kohn 等，2021；Cicalese 等，2016）、WAS（Ferrua 等，2019）與 SCID-X1（Mamcarz 等，2019）已有令人鼓舞的結果。作者預期未來幾年，基因編輯將成為 gene addition 的替代技術，用於幹細胞基因治療，也可能校正 CD40 ligand deficiency、CTLA4 或 IPEX 等疾病的成熟細胞。
理論上，自體幹細胞基因治療可避免 GVHD、排斥等異體免疫反應，前處理毒性也較 allo-HCT 低。但缺乏比較研究，使其在治療流程中的精確定位仍未定；廣泛應用前，也須克服物流、法規與經濟障礙。儘管如此，它已擴大某些 IEI 的治療選擇，快速發展的基因校正方法有望進一步提高安全性與有效性。
〔90.6.3 標靶治療〕新 IEI 遺傳病因，尤其 GOF 變異與病生理的解析，使疾病首次可能以高度專一、常為小分子抑制劑的藥物治療，其中部分已獲准用於其他適應症。例子包括：CTLA4 haploinsufficiency 的 abatacept、STAT1 GOF 的 ruxolitinib 或其他 JAK inhibitors、APDS 的 leniolisib、ADA2 deficiency 的 etanercept，以及自體發炎反覆發燒症候群的 IL-1 標靶藥 anakinra、rilonacept、canakinumab（Ochs 與 Petroni，2018；Ombrello 等，2019；Rao 等，2023）。未來可能有更多藥物獲准或轉用，如 XIAP 的 IL-18BP。目前其精確治療定位未明；理想情況可讓部分患者免於 HCT，但長期毒性、感染與淋巴瘤風險仍令人關切。對過度自體免疫／發炎者，這些藥可作為理想移植橋接或緩解誘導，控制 IEI，使病人以最佳臨床狀況接受 HCT。
【章末重點】① IEI 需要個別化移植策略，已有疾病專屬方案，包括幹細胞基因治療。② 既有共病，尤其移植時感染及終末器官損傷，會惡化結果；許多疾病建議較年幼時移植。③ 替代療法越來越多，常作為移植橋接，以改善病人結果。

and Osteopetrosis
Robert Wynn and Ansgar Schulz
91.1	
Inborn Errors of Metabolism
91.1.1	 Definition and Epidemiology
Inborn errors of metabolism (IEM) comprise a 
large group of inherited diseases. They are indi­
vidually rare. HCT is indicated only in a small 
number of diseases.
It can be curative in certain lysosomal disor­
ders, peroxisomal disorders or certain disorders 
of mitochondrial function. This review will be 
limited to the commoner indications reported in 
HCT registries and which together account for 
most of transplanted IEM.
91.1.2	 Diagnosis
Timely diagnosis is imperative in IEM since in 
all such diseases, HCT is better at preventing dis­
ease progression than reversing established dis­
ease manifestations. Indeed, HCT might be 
contraindicated in those patients presenting with 
more advanced disease.

91
This is true for all lysosomal storage diseases 
and for X-ALD.
Diagnosis is made in three ways
–– Through early clinical recognition of disease 
manifestations
–– Through screening of pre-symptomatic indi­
viduals within a known affected kindred
–– Population screening for disease, such as in 
the neonatal period, with new-born screening
In X-ALD, transplant is indicated for the pre­
vention of progression of cerebral inflammation, 
which manifests with a high interpersonal vari­
ability, even within an affected kindred. Progress 
of inflammation is detected with serial cerebral 
MRI scans (at 6 or 12 monthly intervals) in boys, 
that are genetically affected but currently well.
	 
91.1
91.1.4	 Risk Factors
Patient performance score at transplant predicts 
transplant outcome. Patients with an adverse per­
formance score at transplant also have an inferior 
long-term survival as the transplant fails in 
advanced disease to prevent disease progression.
819

Table 91.1  Classification of inborn errors of metabolism
IEM
Hurler syndrome, 
Hurler syndrome. This is the most severe phenotype of iduronidase deficiency, a lysosomal 
MPSIH
storage disorder (LSD), which results in the accumulation of glycosaminoglycans, heparan and 
dermatan sulfate. There is progressive multiorgan dysfunction including psychomotor retardation, 
severe skeletal disease, life-threatening cardiopulmonary complications, and premature death, 
HCT prevents early death and attenuates the multisystem disease manifestations as the deficient 
enzyme is donated by engrafted donor leucocytes to host tissues (“cross-correction”)
X-linked 
In this X-linked disorder, there is accumulation of very long-chain fatty acids in the brain 
adrenoleukodystrophy 
and adrenal glands arising from their defective metabolism by a peroxisomal, membrane 
(ALD)
protein encoded by the ABCD1 gene
Clinical manifestations in genetically affected boys are highly variable, even within a 
kindred. The principle role of HCT is to prevent progression of early cerebral ALD, an 
inflammatory demyelinating disease of childhood that is seen in about 40% of genetically 
affected individuals
HCT does not influence other illness such as adrenal insufficiency or the later 
myeloneuropathy of the spinal cord
Metachromatic 
This is an autosomal recessive LSD, and there is accumulation of sulfatides, a myelin 
leukodystrophy 
component, due to deficiency of the arylsulfatase A enzyme. There is demyelination in the 
(MLD)
central and peripheral nervous systems, and clinical manifestations are related to residual 
enzyme activity. In the late infantile disease, the commonest and most severe phenotype, 
there is progressive neurological dysfunction and early death usually by the age of 4 years
HCT is ineffective in preventing progression of early presenting disease, although it may 
have a greater impact on later, attenuated disease especially when applied early in the 
course of the illness. HSC GT is recently available for presymptomatic late infantile 
disease, and corrects disease by delivery of supra-physiological enzyme by leukocytes, 
derived from gene-modified stem cells
91.1.5	 Prognostic Index
Not available.
91.1.6	 First-Line Treatment (Summary)
Multimodality therapies are usual in IEM.
–– Residual disease manifestations will require 
management beyond the HCT episode. This 
will include orthopaedics, ENT, and speech 
therapy in lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs), 
as well as family and educational support.
–– Pharmacological enzyme replacement therapy 
(ERT) is used in MPSI but does not correct neu­
rological disease as it does not cross the blood–
brain barrier, and alloantibody formation might 
limit its use in somatic disease. It is used to 
improve pre-HCT performance, but it has not 
been shown to influence transplant outcomes.
91.1.7	 Second-Line Treatment 
(Summary)
See Sect. 91.1.6., above.
91.1.8	 Autologous HCT
Gene-modified auto-HCT approaches have been 
shown to improve outcomes in late infantile 
MLD as the graft delivers more enzyme than pos­
sible in a conventional HCT. This treatment has 
been recently licensed by the EMA for therapy in 
several European countries.
Similar approaches are under investigation for 
other lysosomal disorders including MPSIIIA, 
MPSII, Gaucher (particularly where there is neu­
rological involvement, GD3), and MPSIH. It is 
likely that this approach will greatly change the 
landscape of therapeutic approaches in metabolic 
disease in the coming years.
Similar approaches have been successful in 
X-ALD.  The mechanism of action is different, 
since there is no supraphysiological production 
of enzyme. Of course, autologous HCT is also 
safer. Consecutively, no immune suppression is 
needed with a lower risk of infections and no risk 
of GVHD.

Table 91.2  Main characteristics of allo-HCT for MPSIH (Hurler), MLD, and X-ALD
Indicated in
MPSIH (Hurler) is a standard indication for HCT
In MLD, HCT is usually reserved for later (attenuated) forms of the disease, namely, juvenile and adult forms (note 
HCT GT is licensed and standard of care in the more severe forms of disease, manifesting earlier)
In X-ALD, HCT is indicated in early cerebral inflammatory disease. Ordinarily, a genetically affected individual has 
serial (6 monthly or annual) MRI scans from early childhood, and HCT is carried out when there are early MRI 
changes of demyelination (the MRI changes are scored as a Loes score)
Contraindications
Where MPSIH is diagnosed late, the opportunity for HCT to meaningfully alter the natural history of the disease 
might be lost. No predetermined and simple rules can be applied. HCT is usually not offered to a child presenting 
beyond the age of 30 months, but careful multidisciplinary assessment is required. Not transplanting means the child 
will die of somatic disease manifestations, and the decision not to transplant is not easy to make
Late infantile MLD is not usually considered for allogeneic HCT. Note that such disease—if diagnosed in a timely 
fashion—has been shown to be markedly improved using an autologous, ex vivo HSC gene therapy approach
Advanced cerebral X-ALD is considered a contraindication for HCT. Disease will progress through transplant. The 
MRI scan-derived Loes score might predict those who will benefit most from HCT

91.2	
Osteopetrosis
91.2.1	 Definition and Epidemiology
Osteopetrosis (OP) is a generic name for a vari­
ety of rare monogenetic diseases characterized 
by sclerosis of the skeleton. At least nine variants 
are known with different modes of inheritance 
and severity, which cumulatively have an inci­
dence ~1:100,000. The disease originates from 
reduced or complete lack of osteoclast function 
and, as a consequence, impairment of bone 
resorption.
91.2.2	 Diagnosis
In addition to the obligate increased bone density 
of all bones (X-ray), a combination of symptoms 
can be found in classical infantile osteopetrosis 
after birth. These symptoms include characteris­
tic changes of the head (macrocephalus, frontal 
bossing, choanal stenosis), vision impairment 
(due to narrowed foramina), hematological insuf­
ficiency (thrombocytopenia, anemia, leukocyto­
sis), hepatosplenomegaly (due to extramedullar 
hematopoiesis), and hypocalcemia (with second­
ary hyperparathyroidism). Cave: OP is a geneti­
cal and phenotypical heterogenous disease with 
presentations 
(incomplete 
and/or 
atypical 
delayed onset of symptoms). In these cases, an 
intensive work-up including spine biopsy and 
cranial MRI is recommended.

91.2.4	 Risk Factors
There is an increased risk of pulmonary hyper­
tension (pre and post HCT) and SOS/VOD (post 
BMT). The risk of non-engraftment and rejection 
increases with severity of disease and age.
91.2.5	 Prognostic Index
Not available.
91.2.6	 First-Line Treatment 
(Summary)
Symptomatic, steroids may be beneficial to 
improve hematological symptoms.
91.2.7	 Second-Line Treatment 
(Summary)
Not available.

zh: 先天代謝疾病與骨硬化症
points: 只有部分 IEM 適合 HCT，例如特定 lysosomal／peroxisomal 疾病；需疾病與基因層級判斷。
HCT 通常較能預防進展，而非逆轉已形成的神經與器官損傷，因此早期診斷關鍵。
供者來源的造血／髓系細胞可提供缺失酵素或功能，但受疾病病理與進入組織速度限制。
Osteopetrosis 需確認是否為可由造血來源 osteoclast 校正的類型；神經原發缺陷可能無法改善。
嚴重晚期病變可能降低收益，需跨專科評估適應症。
question: 為何某些代謝疾病越早移植越重要？
answer: 因移植主要防止後續累積損傷，已建立的神經傷害往往難以逆轉。
trap: 不是所有同名臨床表型都有相同的 HCT 可治療機轉。
fullTranslationText:
【第91章：先天代謝疾病與骨硬化症】作者：Robert Wynn、Ansgar Schulz。〔91.1 先天代謝疾病；91.1.1 定義與流行病學〕先天代謝疾病（IEM）包含大量遺傳疾病，各病均罕見；只有少部分疾病具有 HCT 適應症。
HCT 可治癒某些溶小體、過氧化體或粒線體功能疾病。本章限於移植登錄庫中較常見、合計占多數 IEM 移植病例的適應症。
〔91.1.2 診斷〕IEM 必須及時診斷，因為對這些疾病，HCT 預防進展的效果，優於逆轉已形成的病變。疾病較晚期者，甚至可能有 HCT 禁忌症。
這適用於所有 lysosomal storage diseases（溶小體儲積症）及 X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy（X-ALD）。
診斷途徑有三種：① 早期辨識臨床表現；② 在已知受影響家系中篩檢尚無症狀者；③ 人口篩檢，例如新生兒篩檢。X-ALD 的移植目的，是防止腦部發炎持續進展；即使同一家族，其表現也有很大差異。因此，對基因已確認受影響、但目前仍健康的男孩，每 6 或 12 個月追蹤腦部 MRI，以偵測發炎進展。
〔91.1.3 分類〕見表91.1。〔91.1.4 風險因子〕移植時的 performance score 可預測結果。功能狀態較差者，長期存活亦較差，因為對晚期疾病，移植無法阻止病程繼續進展。
【作者任職機構】R. Wynn：英國 Manchester，University of Manchester／Royal Manchester Children’s Hospital，Blood and Marrow Transplant Unit；robert.wynn@mft.nhs.uk。A. Schulz：德國 Ulm，University Medical Center Ulm，Department of Pediatrics；ansgar.schulz@uniklinik-ulm.de。
【表91.1：IEM 分類】Hurler syndrome（MPSIH）是 iduronidase 缺乏最嚴重的表型，屬溶小體儲積症，因 glycosaminoglycans（heparan、dermatan sulfate）堆積，造成進行性多器官功能異常，包括精神動作發展遲滯、嚴重骨骼疾病、危及生命的心肺併發症及早逝。HCT 可防止早逝並減輕多系統表現，機轉為已植入的供者白血球將缺乏的酵素供應給宿主組織，即 cross-correction。X-linked ALD 則因 ABCD1 所編碼的過氧化體膜蛋白功能異常，使極長鏈脂肪酸在腦與腎上腺堆積。即使同一家族，受影響男孩的臨床表現仍高度多樣。HCT 主要防止早期 cerebral ALD 進展；這是兒童期發炎性脫髓鞘疾病，約見於 40% 基因受影響者。HCT 不會改善腎上腺功能不全或之後的脊髓 myeloneuropathy。
【表91.1續：Metachromatic leukodystrophy（MLD）】這是體染色體隱性溶小體儲積症，arylsulfatase A 缺乏使髓鞘成分 sulfatides 堆積，造成中樞與周邊神經脫髓鞘；表現與殘餘酵素活性相關。最常見且最嚴重的晚期嬰兒型，會出現進行性神經功能障礙，通常四歲前死亡。HCT 無法有效阻止早發病型進展，但對較晚發、較輕型疾病可能較有效，尤其病程早期介入。近來症狀前的晚期嬰兒型可使用 HSC 基因治療，藉基因修飾幹細胞產生的白血球，提供超生理量酵素以校正疾病。〔91.1.5 預後指標〕目前無可用指標。
〔91.1.6 第一線治療概述〕IEM 通常需多模式治療。
移植之外，殘餘病變仍需照護。例如溶小體儲積症需骨科、耳鼻喉及語言治療，以及家庭和教育支持。
MPSI 可使用酵素替代治療（ERT），但因藥物無法穿越血腦障壁，不能校正神經病變；異體抗體形成也可能限制其對全身性病變的效益。ERT 可改善移植前功能狀態，但尚未證實會影響移植結果。
〔91.1.7 第二線治療概述〕見上方第91.1.6節。
〔91.1.8 自體 HCT〕基因修飾自體 HCT 可比傳統移植提供更多酵素，已顯示能改善晚期嬰兒型 MLD 的結果。按本書撰寫時資訊，這項治療近期已經 EMA 核准，於數個歐洲國家使用。
MPSIIIA、MPSII、Gaucher disease（尤其神經受累的 GD3）及 MPSIH 等其他溶小體疾病，也在研究相似策略。作者預期，未來數年這會大幅改變代謝疾病的治療。
X-ALD 也已有相似策略成功，但機轉不同，並非透過超生理酵素產生。自體 HCT 在這方面亦較安全：後續不需免疫抑制，因此感染風險較低，且沒有 GVHD 風險。
〔91.1.9 MPSIH、MLD 與 X-ALD 的異體 HCT；表91.2〕【適應症】MPSIH 是標準移植適應症。MLD 的 allo-HCT 通常保留於較晚發、較輕的青少年型及成人型；較早發的嚴重病型，目前已有獲准且屬標準照護的幹細胞基因治療。X-ALD 則在早期腦部發炎時移植：通常從幼年起，每半年或一年以 MRI 追蹤，出現早期脫髓鞘變化即安排 HCT；MRI 變化可用 Loes score 評分。【禁忌／限制】MPSIH 若太晚診斷，可能已錯失改變自然病程的機會。沒有能一概適用的簡單規則；通常不對超過 30 個月才就醫者提供 HCT，但須仔細跨專科評估。未移植可能因身體病變而死亡，因此不移植的決定並不容易。晚期嬰兒型 MLD 通常不採 allo-HCT，但及時診斷者使用自體、體外 HSC 基因治療，可明顯改善病情。
【表91.2續】晚期 cerebral X-ALD 被視為 HCT 禁忌，因疾病可能在移植過程仍持續進展；Loes score 有助辨識最可能獲益者。【供者】溶小體儲積症（LSD）：非帶因 MFD > MUD > 帶因 MFD。LSD 常偏好臍帶血而非骨髓，因嵌合較高、轉介至移植時間可能最短，但初次排斥可能較多。PB 很少作為來源。X-ALD：MFD > MUD。IEM 很少使用 haplo-HCT。【標準前處理】IEM 植入較困難；一般 RIC 與體外 TCD 與較高移植物流失相關。MSD／MFD 及 MUD：IV BU（劑量達 MAC AUC）＋FLU 160 mg/m²。自體基因治療：IV BU（MAC AUC），不需免疫抑制。【減毒前處理】偶爾可用於 Wolman 或較輕型 MPS 等全身性 IEM：TREO 42 g/m²＋FLU 160 mg/m²＋TT 10 mg/kg。【細胞來源】LSD 常偏好 UCB，因較高嵌合可帶來較佳酵素供應；MUD 偏好 BM 而非 PB。
【表91.2續】不使用體外 TCD，因其會增加移植物流失。【GVHD 預防】MSD／MFD：ATG／Campath、CSA＋MMF；MUD：ATG／Campath、CSA＋MMF；非親屬 CB：ATG 於第 −9 至 −6 天，搭配 CSA＋MMF 或 CSA＋PRD。CB 前處理常另加 rituximab，以降低移植後自體免疫性血球低下及初次移植物排斥。【MPSIH 的結果】TRM：MSD <5%，MUD <10%；成功植入且存活比例 >80%，整體存活率約 90%。縮寫：MAC AUC＝調整劑量以達骨髓消除性 AUC；MSD＝相合同胞供者；MFD＝相合家庭供者；MUD＝相合非親屬供者；LSD＝溶小體儲積症；IEM＝先天代謝疾病。
〔91.2 骨硬化症；91.2.1 定義與流行病學〕Osteopetrosis（OP）是多種以骨骼硬化為特徵的罕見單基因疾病總稱。已知至少九種變異類型，遺傳方式及嚴重度不同，合計發生率約 1／100,000。疾病源於破骨細胞功能下降或完全缺失，因而無法正常骨吸收。
〔91.2.2 診斷〕除 X 光必然可見全身骨密度增加外，典型嬰兒型 OP 出生後可合併頭部特徵（大頭、前額突出、後鼻孔狹窄）、因孔道變窄造成視力障礙、造血不足（血小板低下、貧血、白血球增加）、因髓外造血造成肝脾腫大，以及低血鈣伴續發性副甲狀腺機能亢進。須注意，OP 在遺傳及表型上高度異質，可能有症狀不完整或較晚出現的非典型表現；這些病例建議深入檢查，包括原文所述 spine biopsy 與顱部 MRI。
〔91.2.3 分類〕【嬰兒型「惡性」體染色體隱性 OP（ARO）】嬰兒期發病，未 HCT 通常十歲前死亡；可有 TCIRG1、CLCN7、SNX10、TNFRSF11A／RANK、FERMT3／KINDLIN-3 的雙等位基因變異。排除「神經退化型 OP」（所有 OSTM1，以及約半數 CLCN7 病例）與「破骨細胞外在缺陷」（TNFSF11／RANKL）後，可評估 HCT。【中間型 OP】十歲內出現症狀；若有造血不足及已出現或迫近的視力損害，可個別評估移植。特殊的 CA2 缺乏會造成腎小管酸中毒與腦鈣化；若造血不足、視力受威脅，且神經及腎臟問題已控制，可考慮 HCT。【良性體染色體顯性 OP（ADO）】Albers–Schönberg disease，為 CLCN7 單等位基因變異，通常不需 HCT；極嚴重者仍可個別評估。〔91.2.4 風險因子〕患者在 HCT 前後的肺高壓，以及移植後 SOS／VOD 風險較高；疾病越嚴重、年齡越大，未植入與排斥風險越高。
〔91.2.5 預後指標〕目前無可用指標。
〔91.2.6 第一線治療概述〕以症狀治療為主；steroids 可能改善血液學症狀。
〔91.2.7 第二線治療概述〕目前無可用治療。
〔91.2.8 自體 HCT〕本書撰寫時，針對 TCIRG1 缺陷的基因修飾自體 HCT 臨床試驗正在準備中。
〔91.2.9 異體 HCT〕詳見表91.3。其後為延伸閱讀書目，保留英文。
【表91.3：OP 異體 HCT 主要特徵】適應症：有臨床症狀的嬰兒型 OP，須排除神經退化與破骨細胞外在缺陷。禁忌：具非低血鈣性癲癇／原文所稱 EEC 變化、嚴重進行性發展遲緩，及／或 OSTM1、CLCN7 雙等位基因變異的神經退化型 OP；但僅約半數 CLCN7 變異造成神經退化。TNFSF11／RANKL 病變並非破骨細胞分化／功能的內在缺陷，也不適合此療法。供者：MFD > MUD > haplo，不建議 CB。標準前處理：MSD／MFD、MUD、haplo 皆為 IV BU（MAC AUC）＋FLU 160 mg/m²。減毒前處理：MSD／MFD 或 MUD 可用 TREO／FLU 150 mg/m²／TT 8–10 mg/kg。MMUD 或 haplo 應採調整過的 PT-CY 方案（見 ESID 指引，Lankester 等，2021）。細胞來源：相合供者、PT-CY 平台偏好 T-replete BM > PB。GVHD 預防：MSD／MFD 用 CSA＋MMF，MFD 可考慮 ATG 或 Campath；MUD 用 CSA＋MMF＋ATG（或 Campath）；T-replete haplo 用 Campath、PT-CY、TAC（或 CSA）＋MMF。TRM：MSD／MUD 10–20%。
【表91.3續】Haplo 的 TRM 約 20–30%。整體存活率：MSD 約 90%，MUD 約 80%，haplo／MMUD 約 70%。MAC AUC 為調整劑量以達骨髓消除性 AUC；MSD 為相合同胞、MFD 為相合家庭、MUD 為相合非親屬、MMUD 為不相合非親屬供者。

92.1	
Introduction
Autoimmune diseases (ADs) are a heterogeneous 
group of diseases affecting 8–10% of the Western 
population, which constitute a heavy burden to 
society and are often debilitating and disabling 
for affected individuals. ADs are defined as an 
impairment of the immune system resulting in 
the loss of immune tolerance against self-tissues, 
by the existence of autoreactive T and B cells and 
by a complex mechanism of multifactorial aetiol­

B. Sharrack

Sheffield, UK

M. Rovira

and Oncology, Hospital Clínic, 

Barcelona, Spain

ogy, across genetics and environmental factors 
(Alexander and Greco 2022). Autoimmunity is 
also linked to autoinflammation, having common 
features as the activation against self, with subse­
quent systemic inflammation (Chap. 93).
Current therapeutic strategies for AD are 
based on systemic immunosuppression (IS) or 
targeted biologic disease-modifying therapies 
(DMTs), which ameliorate symptoms and halt 
progression in the vast majority of patients but 
usually require continuous administration and

J. A. Snowden

Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, Royal Hallamshire 
Hospital, and University of Sheffield, Sheffield, UK

825

may be associated with long-term side effects 
and substantial costs. Although biologic DMT 
has improved specificity and efficacy in the treat­
ment landscape, cure remains elusive, and many 
patients still suffer from progressive disability 
with shortened life expectancy and comorbidity.
Initially supported by preclinical animal mod­
els and ‘serendipitous’ case reports, auto-HCT 
has grown as a promising and feasible treatment 
option for severe treatment-resistant patients, 
especially in diseases for which effective thera­
pies are lacking. The annual number of patients 
treated with autologous HCT is constantly 
increasing (Alexander and Greco 2022), and AD 
are among the fastest growing disease category 
reported to the EBMT for autologous HCT 
(Passweg et al. 2021). Allo-HCT has also been 
undertaken, although caution related to its intrin­
sic risks has precluded widespread application.
The EBMT Autoimmune Diseases Working 
Party (ADWP) was established in 1997 by Alois 
Gratwohl, Alberto Marmont, Alan Tyndall and 
Athanasios Fassas, who developed the registry 
covering AD indications and produced early 
guidelines based on consensus opinion (Tyndall 
and Gratwohl 1997).
Subsequently, the ADWP built productively 
on these initial achievements, generating studies 
from the growing registry and developing rela­
tionships with other specialist societies, culmi­
nating with successful publication of three 
randomised controlled trials (van Laar et  al. 
2014; Hawkey et al. 2015; Mancardi et al. 2015), 
along with updated guidelines for clinical prac­
tice (Snowden et al. 2012), immune monitoring 
and biobanking (Alexander et al. 2015; Cencioni 
et al. 2022).
With increasing evidence, the guidelines have 
become more disease specific. A successful inter­
national collaboration involving also non-­
European experts resulted in the EBMT 
guidelines for auto-HCT in systemic sclerosis 
(Farge et  al. 2017b). A further collaborative 
review with the European Crohn’s and Colitis 
Organisation (ECCO) has included recommenda­
tions for patient selection, transplant technique 
and follow-up of HCT in patients with Crohn’s 
disease (Snowden et al. 2018). EBMT guidelines 
for MS and other neurological diseases were 
published in 2020 (Sharrack et  al. 2020). 
Guidelines for best practices were also provided 
during the COVID-19 pandemic (Greco et  al. 
2021, 2023).
92.1
92.2

will cover the main neurological, rheumatologi­
cal and gastroenterological indications for auto-­
HCT, along with reference to the rare AD 
indications and allogeneic HCT.  More detailed 
literature can be sourced from recently published 
reviews (Achini‐Gutzwiller et al. 2022; Alexander 
and Greco 2022; Snowden et al. 2017).

92.2	
Mechanisms of Action
HCT represented an opportunity to gain insights 
into the aetiology and pathogenesis of AD, char­
acterised by aberrant activation of the immune 
system with failure of the immune regulation to 
maintain adapted tolerance. HCT exerts its thera­
peutic effect through various mechanisms, 
including the immunosuppressive conditioning 
regimen able to eradicate the autoreactive immu­
nologic memory, and the regeneration and 
renewal of the immune system, leading to the re-­
induction of immune tolerance to rewire aberrant 
immune response toward self-antigens (Cencioni 
et al. 2022; Lima-Junior et al. 2021). The effect 
of HCT on immunologic renewal has been the 
focus of many mechanistic studies. They collec­
tively demonstrated that many of the age- or 
autoimmune-mediated 
immune 
disturbances 
may improve or even resolve. For example, 
immune reconstitution studies indicated a pre­
dominant repopulation of CD27-IgD+ naïve B 
cells (Alexander et al. 2009; Arruda et al. 2018), 
a stable output of recent thymic emigrants (RTE) 
(Farge et al. 2017a; Muraro et al. 2005), leading 
to a re-diversification of the receptor repertoire,

and recurrence of both regulatory B and T cells in 
various disease settings (Alexander et al. 2013; 
Lima-Junior et al. 2021). Allo-HCT has been less 
well explored, although there is an element of 
immune replacement and evidence for a ‘graft-­
versus-­autoimmune effect’ (Greco et  al. 2019). 
Further, areas for exploration include the impact 
of the microbiome on autoimmunity and the 
impact of HCT (Alexander et al. 2021).
92.3	
HCT for Multiple 
Sclerosis (MS)
1997

92.2

Tolf et al. 2019). The bulk of the data has been 
provided by observational cohort studies in 
which patients failing to respond to standard 
DMT were treated with an auto-HCT.  Burman 
et  al. identified the four most rigorously con­
ducted cohort studies in which a total of 188 
relapsing MS patients received auto-HCT 
(Burman et al. 2018). In these studies, PFS was 
observed in 70–91% of patients at 5 years (where 
progression is defined as a deterioration of at 
least 0.5–1 points from baseline in the Expanded 
Disability Status Scale (EDSS). Furthermore, no 
evidence of disease activity (NEDA), defined as 
the absence of clinical relapses, disability pro­
gression and MRI disease activity, was observed 
in 70–92% of patients at 2  years post-­
transplantation (Boffa et al. 2021; Muraro et al. 
2017a). Such results were compared with DMT 
efficacy data reported in registration studies 
(Muraro et  al. 2017a). Higher rates of NEDA 
were achieved with auto-HCT than with any 
other DMT, including those that are considered 
to have high efficacy, although these studies 
included different patient populations. Only two 
randomised trials of auto-HCT have been 
reported in the literature. The first was a phase II 
trial which showed auto-HCT to be more effec­
tive than mitoxantrone on MRI disease activity 
(Mancardi et al. 2015). The second was a phase 
III randomised controlled trial which showed that 
auto-HCT resulted in prolonged time to disability 
progression compared to DMTs. Improvement in 
the EDSS score (3.4–2.4 vs 3.31–3.98), reduction 
in relapse rate (1 vs 39) and reduced disability 
progression (6% vs 60%) were seen in the aHCT 
group vs controls, respectively. There were no 
significant side effects and no treatment related 
mortality in the aHCT arm (Burt et  al. 2019). 
Three phase III randomised controlled trials, 
aimed to compare auto-HCT to DMTs are cur­
rently 
recruiting 
(BEAT-MS: 
Identifier: 
NCT04047628, 
RAM-MS 
Identifier: 
NCT03477500, STAR-MS: EudraCT Identifier: 
2019-001549-42) and others are expected to be 
started (Sharrack et al. 2022). The conditioning 
regimens used in MS vary between treatment 
centres. The balance of efficacy and acceptable 
safety profile of ‘intermediate intensity’ regi­
mens, i.e. either the specific ‘BEAM + ATG’ 
regimen or the more generic regimen of CY 
200 mg/kg combined with ATG, led to their rec­
ommended use in the current EBMT ADWP 
guidelines (Sharrack et al. 2020). Single-centre 
data suggest that ‘high-intensity’ regimens, 
incorporating Busulfan and ex-vivo T-cell deple­
tion, have higher rates of PFS but potentially 
greater toxicity, including TRM (Atkins et  al. 
2016). Retrospective registry data suggest that 
graft purging has no added benefit to the trans­
plant outcome (Sharrack et al. 2020).
Currently, auto-HCT is recommended as a 
standard of care for patients with active relapsing 
MS failing DMTs and as a treatment option for 
patients with progressive MS with evidence of 
disease activity or patients with aggressive MS as 
a first-line treatment. The best results are seen in 
patients who are not older than 45  years, have 
had the illness for less than 10 years, are not very 
disabled (EDSS ≤6) and have active disease with 
evidence of enhancement on their MRI.  The 
ADWP has recently provided guidelines for the 
management of HCT in MS and other immune-­
mediated neurological ADs (Sharrack et  al. 
2020), and current clinical trials are summarised 
in a recent review (Sharrack et al. 2022). Updated 
interspecialty guidelines have been finalised fol­
lowing a joint EBMT-ECTRIMS workshop 
(Muraro et al. unpublished).
92.4	
HCT for Systemic Sclerosis 
(SSc)
Over the past 25  years, results from large 
European prospective observational studies and 
analysis of the European Scleroderma Trials and 
Research Group (EUSTAR) registry data base 
(Elhai et  al. 2017) confirmed that SSc patients 
benefit only marginally from standard immuno­
suppressive drugs, including CY, with a progres­
sive 
increase 
in 
SSc-specific 
mortality, 
predominantly related to cardiac (31%) and pul­
monary causes (18%). Since three successive 
randomised trials, namely, ASSIST [American 
Scleroderma 
Stem 
cell 
versus 
Immune 
Suppression Trial, (Burt et  al. 2011)], ASTIS

[Autologous 
Stem 
cell 
Transplantation 
International Scleroderma trial, (van Laar et al. 
2014)] 
and 
SCOT 
[Scleroderma: 
Cyclophosphamide Or Transplantation, (Sullivan 
et al. 2018)], have now demonstrated that auto-­
HCT is superior to CY for early rapidly progres­
sive SSc in terms of long-term survival as well as 
improvement of lung function and skin fibrosis, 
AHCT for early severe dcSSc patients is now rec­
ommended with a grade I level of evidence by the 
EBMT (Snowden et  al. 2022), and by the 
American Rheumatism Association (ACR) and 
The European League Against Rheumatism 
(Kowal-Bielecka et al. 2017) and the American 
Society for Transplantation and Cellular Therapy 
(Majhail et al. 2015), with increased transplant 
activity reported to the EBMT registry and world­
wide over the last decade.
Of note, ASSIST and ASTIS utilised a non-­
myeloablative regimen of cyclophosphamide 
(200 mg/kg total dose) and rabbit antithymocyte 
globulin (rATG), and the main difference between 
the two studies was that ASSIST mobilised stem 
cells with 2 g/m2 CY and infused unmanipulated 
peripheral blood stem cells (PBSC), while ASTIS 
mobilised stem cells with 4 g/m2 CY and infused 
CD34+ selected PBSC. The SCOT trial used no 
CY with only G-CSF for mobilisation and a 
lower dose of CY (120 mg/kg total dose) for con­
ditioning plus TBI (800  cGy/4 fractions over 
2 days/200 cGy to lungs and kidneys with shield­
ing), which induces myeloablation.
In addition, patient selection was shown to 
directly affect transplant outcomes (Henes et al. 
2021) with specific concern for cardiac involve­
ment, undetected by echocardiography alone, 
becoming clinically overt during the transplant 
procedure, under the stress of fluid overload, CY 
and ATG administration and sepsis. Current 
guidelines recommend auto-HCT for SSc 
patients, according to the 2013 ACR/EULAR 
classification criteria (van den Hoogen et  al. 
2013), aged 18–65 years (certain paediatric indi­
cations may be considered on a case-by-case 
basis), with disease duration less than 2 years and 
a clinical phenotype of diffuse SSc, a modified 
Rodnan score (mRSS) greater than 20, a sedi­
mentation rate >25 mm or an elevated C-reactive 
protein >5 mg/L or a haemoglobin level less than 
11 g/dL not explained by causes other than the 
evolvability of SSc; or less than 5 years SSc with 
a) a modified Rodnan skin score ≥15 plus severe 
organ involvement in respiratory, cardiovascular 
or renal systems or b) a mRSS <14 (limited skin 
involvement), in case of coexisting severe pro­
gressive lung involvement (alteration of FVC 
and/or TLC ≥10% and/or DLCO ≥15% com­
pared to an initial value obtained 12 ± 6 months 
previously). Treatment should be performed in 
JACIE-accredited 
centres 
where 
combined 
expertise from SSc disease specialists and dedi­
cated transplant teams can assess and follow 
patients before, during and after the procedure 
according to Good Clinical Practices (Snowden 
et  al. 2017). Since toxicity and efficacy arise 
from individual patient selection and the condi­
tioning regimen, different chemotherapies may 
account for subtle differences in results, and fur­
ther studies are warranted to analyse the use of 
attenuated conditioning regimens according to 
cardiac function and risk for renal crises (Burt 
et al. 2021).
92.5	
HCT for Systemic Lupus 
Erythematosus (SLE)
Despite the era of DMTs, a considerable number 
of patients with SLE do not achieve clinical 
remission, with an accumulating risk of organ 
failure and increased mortality. For these patients, 
autologous HCT has been applied since 1996 
with more than 300 cases reported worldwide 
(Alexander and Greco 2022). The two largest 
experiences on auto-HCT for SLE come from the 
EBMT data registry (n  =  53; mean follow-up, 
25  months) and from a single-centre trial per­
formed at the Northwestern University (n = 50; 
mean follow-up, 29 months), both demonstrating 
a probability of 5-year DFS of 50% despite dis­
continuation of chronic immunosuppression. 
Subsequently, a follow-up study from the EBMT 
registry reported the outcome of auto-HCT in 
SLE with various regimens between 2001 and 
2008 (n  =  28; median follow-up, 38  months; 
range, 1–110  months) (Alchi et  al. 2013).

Although PFS in this study was only 29% at 
5 years, TRM had gradually improved. In addi­
tion, this study indicated that CD34-selection 
was associated with a significantly reduced risk 
for relapse. More recently, Richard Burt reported 
a remission rate of 92% at 1 year, 81% at 2 years, 
71% at 3 years, and 62% at 4 and 5 years post-­
HCT, respectively, for 26 patients receiving a 
CYC/ATG/RTX conditioning (Burt et al. 2018). 
Long-term outcomes (Burt et al. 2021) are avail­
able from two independent Chinese reports, both 
with 10-year follow-up, demonstrating remark­
able clinical responses with PFS of 86% and 
68%, respectively, while TRM across both stud­
ies was only 2%.
Summarising the results from the most rele­
vant 15 studies in the field covering 339 patients 
with a median follow-up of 5 years, the median 
remission rate achieved was 65% with a median 
mortality of 8%, with a gradual decline of TRM 
from 12% in the first EBMT registry survey in 
2004 to <5% in most recent reports between 2017 
and 2019 (Burt et al. 2021). Overall, responding 
patients are usually free of clinical symptoms and 
may regain seronegativity for antinuclear anti­
bodies, which is rarely seen under conventional 
therapies. Early use of HCT also has the potential 
to protect against organ failure and toxicity-­
related morbidity and improve quality of life 
(Burt et al. 2018). The relapse rate is higher in 
patients receiving unmanipulated stem cell grafts 
and conditioning regimens without serotherapy 
(Alchi et al. 2013). Current evidence and expert 
consensus suggest HCT in SLE as ‘clinical 
option’ in patients with active disease (BILAG 
category A), state despite chronic immunosup­
pression with or without B-cell-targeted thera­
pies (Illei et al. 2011; Snowden et al. 2012, 2022).
92.6	
HCT for Crohn’s Disease (CD)
Despite the major recent progress in the treat­
ment of CD, based around corticosteroids, IS 
(thiopurines, MTX) and DMTs (Ab targeting 
TNFα, α4β7 integrin or IL-12/IL-23), some 
patients fail all available therapies. In many 
cases, surgery may be an option but may lead to 
short bowel syndrome or to a permanent stoma, 
which may be unacceptable to patients. With this 
background, in the past few years, auto-HCT has 
emerged as a promising therapy in a subset of 
patients in whom the disease is refractory to all 
available therapies, with progressive tissue dam­
age and potentially reduced life expectancy.
Auto-HCT has been investigated in several 
studies with encouraging responses, some pro­
longed, although a progressive incidence of 
relapse with long-term follow-up is recognised 
(Burt et  al. 2010; Lopez-Garcia et  al. 2017). 
Furthermore, patients regain response to anti-­
TNF therapy, although they had been refractory 
to this drug class prior to HCT.
In Europe, the EBMT-sponsored ASTIC trial 
in patients with refractory CD produced appar­
ently negative results as few patients after auto-­
HCT met the stringent primary composite 
endpoint of clinical remission for 3  months 
(Hawkey et al. 2015). However, it should not be 
assumed that this single trial provides the defini­
tive answer to the benefit of auto-HCT in CD, as 
the number of patients included was limited and 
encouraging long-term follow-up of ASTIC trial 
patients has since been reported (Lindsay et al. 
2017). Encouraging results have also been 
reported by an EBMT retrospective analysis of 
82 treatment-resistant patients who were not in 
the ASTIC trial. In this difficult-to-treat group of 
patients, around a quarter maintained remission 
without further medical therapy, and long-term 
disease control was maintained with the reintro­
duction of salvage therapies in the majority of 
patients who relapsed. TRM occurred in one 
patient (Brierley et al. 2018).
The EBMT ADWP and ECCO (European 
Crohn’s and Colitis Organisation) have published 
a joint position paper of auto-HCT in CD, which 
recommends auto-HCT ideally in the context of a 
multicentre clinical trial but on an individual 
basis may currently be considered for patients 
with active CD refractory to IS and biological 
treatments or unacceptable risks of surgical man­
agement (Snowden et  al. 2018). These recom­
mendations include conditioning regimens using

CY/ATG, which has been used in the majority of 
HCT for CD with an acceptable and predictable 
balance between safety and efficacy in these 
challenging CD cases. A cautionary note should 
be taken from a recent randomised controlled 
trial using FLU, CY and ATG-based conditioning 
regimens, which was stopped early due to unex­
pected severe toxicity, including thrombotic 
microangiopathy (Lindsay 2021).
The next steps in this field focus on minimis­
ing the risk of infectious complications in this 
setting. In this sense, CY-free mobilisation seems 
to be safe and effective (Giordano et  al. 2022) 
and other modifications will be key to further 
development and deliverability of autologous 
HCT in patients with severe CD refractory to 
modern DMTs.
92.7	
Allogeneic HCT 
for Autoimmune Diseases
Autoimmune diseases have also been treated 
with allo-HCT from MRD, URD and CB sources. 
In the last 25 years, the EBMT registry has col­
lated 286 cases. Because of the higher procedural 
risks and potential long-term impact on quality of 
life from late effects, allo-HCT has been largely 
restricted to life-threatening AD in paediatric 
practice with the most common indications in 
immune cytopenia followed by arthritis. In a 
recent summary of cases from the registry (Greco 
et al. 2019), 128 patients undergoing allo-HCT 
were treated between 1997 and 2014. The median 
age was 12.7 years (range 0.2–62.2). The inci­
dence of grades II–IV aGvHD was 20.8% at 
100 days. The cumulative incidence of cGvHD 
was 27.8% at 5 years. Non-relapse mortality 
(NRM) was 12.7% at 100 days. OS and PFS were 
70.2 and 59.4% at 5 years, respectively. By mul­
tivariate analysis, age <18 years, males and more 
recent year of transplant were found to be signifi­
cantly associated with improved PFS.  Reduced 
conditioning intensity was associated with a 
lower NRM. In a subgroup of 64 patients with 
detailed information, a complete clinical response 
was obtained in 67% of patients at 1 year.
Moreover, allo-HCT may represent a potential 
treatment option for the novel entity called 
VEXAS (Vacuoles, E1 enzyme, X-linked, 
Autoinflammatory, Somatic) (Bruno et al. 2023).
In summary, experience in allo-HCT is lim­
ited, but long-term data are supportive of basic 
biological differences in the responses of AD to 
allo- and auto-HCT in terms of curability. 
However, due to related NRM risks, the applica­
tion of allo-HCT remained limited and develop­
mental in AD. With time, allo-HCT in AD has 
become safer and activity continues, particularly 
in the paediatric field. Moreover, improved 
patient selection, reduced toxicity conditioning 
regimens and new strategies for GvHD prophy­
laxis (i.e. PT-CY) are currently under investiga­
tion, generating interest in extending the 
application to non-malignant disorders. In addi­
tion, there has been increasing recognition that 
the nature of the genetic component of some AD 
means that allo-HCT is the only realistic approach 
for long-term disease control. Thus, there is 
renewed interest in this area, particularly where 
there is overlap with autoinflammatory and 
immunodeficiency diseases, particularly in the 
paediatric setting as summarised in a recent 
EBMT review (Achini‐Gutzwiller et al. 2022).

Conclusions and Future 
Directions
With accumulating evidence and improved out­
comes, along with the recognition that modern 
biological and other therapies are not universally 
effective, ADs have become the fastest-growing 
indication for HCT (Alexander and Greco 2022; 
Passweg et al. 2021). Initially applied as salvage 
therapy in patients with poor prognosis, HCT has 
emerged as a promising treatment option for AD 
patients earlier in the treatment algorithm. This is 
the result of successful large phase II and ran­
domised controlled phase III trials and updated 
guidelines for patient selection and transplant 
techniques in SSc, MS and CD, respectively 
(Farge et al. 2017b; Sharrack et al. 2020; Snowden 
et al. 2012).
In 2023, the major indications for HCT in AD 
are MS, SSc and CD (Alexander and Greco 2022) 
for which significant subsets of patients still 
show an unsatisfactory response to both conven­
tional and targeted biologic therapies.
Moving forward, further efforts are needed to 
drive HCT into routine clinical care. It is recom­
mended that patients should be treated in experi­
enced and JACIE-accredited transplant centres in 
a multidisciplinary setting. A future goal is to 
optimise the conditioning regimens according to 
disease-specific requirements and to outbalance 
the intensity to maintain outcomes while mini­
mising toxicity and TRM risk. Moreover, posi­
tive preliminary experiences have been recently 
reported with chimeric antigen receptors (CAR) 
T cells, paving the way for the use of innovative 
cell therapy approaches in AD field (Chap. 93).
In addition, comprehensive data reporting, 
harmonisation and exploitation of existing bio­
banking infrastructure (Alexander et  al. 2015), 
education at individual centre and network level, 
including ADWP educational activities (Burt 
et  al. 2021) and health economic evaluations 
along with evidence-based recommendations 
will establish the future place of HCT in the treat­
ment algorithms for various autoimmune and 
inflammatory diseases.
Key Points
•	 With accumulating evidence, including 
randomised controlled trials, AD has 
become one of the fastest-growing indi­
cation for autologous HCT.
•	 Major indications for HCT in AD 
include multiple sclerosis (MS) and sys­
temic sclerosis (SSc), where auto-HCT 
is 
now 
featuring 
in 
treatment 
algorithms.
•	 Although HCT for ADs is predomi­
nantly autologous, there is renewed 
interest in allo-HCT, particularly in ADs 
with autoinflammatory and immunode­
ficiency components.
•	 It is recommended that all patients 
should be treated in experienced and 
JACIE-accredited 
transplant 
centres 
with close multidisciplinary collabora­
tion and reporting of data to the EBMT 
registry.
•	 Immune reconstitution studies are pro­
viding insights into the mechanisms of 
immune reset following HCT and dis­
ease processes underlying various AD.
