zh: 自體免疫疾病的 HCT
points: Auto-HCT 透過免疫清除與重建，嘗試重置失衡免疫，而非提供 GVL。
MS 與 systemic sclerosis 是本章主要適應疾病，已有隨機試驗支持特定族群。
病人選擇需看活動性、病程、既有不可逆器官損傷及替代治療。
Systemic sclerosis 尤其需嚴格心肺評估，避免高風險前處理毒性。
應在有經驗、具品質認證及跨專科合作的中心治療並登錄結果。
question: Auto-HCT 對所有晚期、固定失能的 MS 都同樣有效嗎？
answer: 不能如此推論。活動性發炎與可逆程度影響收益，固定神經損傷不一定隨免疫重置而恢復。
trap: 免疫重置與修復不可逆器官損傷是不同目標。
fullTranslationText:
【第92章：自體免疫疾病】作者：Tobias Alexander、Basil Sharrack、Montserrat Rovira、Riccardo Saccardi、Dominique Farge、John A. Snowden、Raffaella Greco。〔92.1 導論〕自體免疫疾病（AD）是一組異質疾病，影響西方人口約 8–10%，造成沉重社會負擔，病人常衰弱並失能。其定義是免疫系統受損，對自身組織的耐受喪失，存在自體反應性 T、B 細胞；病因是遺傳及環境多因子交互作用的複雜結果（Alexander 與 Greco，2022）。自體免疫與自體發炎相互關聯，共同特徵是對自身活化，繼而引起全身發炎（第93章）。
現行 AD 治療以全身性免疫抑制或標靶生物性疾病修飾治療（DMT）為主，多數病人可改善症狀並阻止進展，但通常需持續用藥，可能伴隨長期副作用與高昂費用。生物性 DMT 雖提高專一性與療效，仍難達治癒；許多病人持續失能進展、壽命縮短並累積共病。
【作者任職機構；機構及聯絡人專名保留英文】T. Alexander：Charité-University Medicine Berlin，Department of Rheumatology and Clinical Immunology；tobias.alexander@charite.de。B. Sharrack：University of Sheffield／Sheffield Teaching Hospitals，Academic Department of Neuroscience、Sheffield NIHR Translational Neuroscience BRC；Basil.Sharrack@sth.nhs.uk。M. Rovira：Hospital Clínic、August Pi i Sunyer Biomedical Research Institute、Institute Josep Carreras，Barcelona；mrovira@clinic.cat。R. Saccardi：Careggi University Hospital，Department of Haematology，Florence；riccardo.saccardi@unifi.it。D. Farge：CRMR MATHEC、Hôpital St-Louis AP-HP、Université de Paris-Cité／IRSL URP3518 MATHEC-EUROCORD，Paris；dominique.farge-bancel@sls.ap-hop-paris.fr。J. A. Snowden：Royal Hallamshire Hospital、Sheffield Teaching Hospitals／University of Sheffield；john.snowden@sth.nhs.uk。R. Greco（通訊作者）：IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital／Vita-Salute San Raffaele University，Unit of Hematology and Bone Marrow Transplantation，Milan；greco.raffaella@hsr.it。
最初由動物模型及偶然發現的病例報告支持，自體 HCT 已成為嚴重、治療抗性患者具希望且可行的選擇，尤其是缺少有效藥物的疾病。接受 auto-HCT 的年度人數持續增加（Alexander 與 Greco，2022）；AD 是 EBMT 登錄中自體移植成長最快的疾病類別之一（Passweg 等，2021）。異體 HCT 也曾使用，但其固有風險限制了廣泛應用。
EBMT Autoimmune Diseases Working Party（ADWP）於 1997 年由 Alois Gratwohl、Alberto Marmont、Alan Tyndall、Athanasios Fassas 成立，建立涵蓋 AD 適應症的登錄庫，並提出早期共識指引（Tyndall 與 Gratwohl，1997）。
此後 ADWP 以成長中的登錄資料進行研究，與其他專科學會建立合作，成果包括三項隨機對照試驗（van Laar 等，2014；Hawkey 等，2015；Mancardi 等，2015），以及臨床實務（Snowden 等，2012）、免疫監測與生物資料庫的更新指引（Alexander 等，2015；Cencioni 等，2022）。
隨證據增加，指引越來越具疾病專一性。包括非歐洲專家的國際合作，產出 systemic sclerosis 的 EBMT auto-HCT 指引（Farge 等，2017b）；與 ECCO 的合作綜述，提出 Crohn disease 的病人選擇、移植技術與追蹤建議（Snowden 等，2018）。MS 及其他神經疾病指引則於 2020 年發表（Sharrack 等，2020）。
COVID-19 疫情期間亦提出最佳實務建議（Greco 等，2021、2023）。
表92.1與92.2概述 EBMT 的 AD 資料。截至本章撰寫時，這個全球最大的國際資料庫已登錄超過 4,000 名因 AD 接受 HCT 的病人；其他登錄庫的資料使全球總量更高。
本章依據這些治療活動，介紹 auto-HCT 主要的神經、風濕及腸胃道適應症，也涉及罕見 AD 與 allo-HCT。詳盡文獻可見近期綜述（Achini-Gutzwiller 等，2022；Alexander 與 Greco，2022；Snowden 等，2017）。
【表92.1：EBMT 資料庫概況，2023年3月】病人 4,055 名；移植程序 4,140 次；323 個中心、44 國。自體／異體移植分別 3,854 次（93%）／286 次（7%）。自體移植中位年齡 38 歲（3–76），異體 11 歲（<1–64）；男性／女性 40%／60%。
【表92.2：診斷分布，2023年3月】MS 2,132。結締組織疾病 1,028：SSc 835、SLE 126、原文 Polymalgia／dermatomyositis 18、Sjögren syndrome 6、抗磷脂症候群 6、其他 37。關節炎 209：RA 82、全身型 JIA 74、其他 JIA 19、關節型 JIA 22、乾癬性關節炎 3、其他 9。IBD 283：Crohn disease 233、coeliac disease 18、其他 32。血液疾病 161：ITP 42、溶血性貧血 36、Evans syndrome 24、其他 60。血管炎 67：GPA 12、Behçet disease 18、Takayasu arteritis 3、PAN 4、EGPA 2、其他 28。其他神經疾病 146：CIDP 65、neuromyelitis optica 29、重症肌無力 11、其他 41。胰島素依賴型糖尿病 20；其他疾病 94。〔92.2 作用機轉〕HCT 提供機會，研究 AD 的病因與病生理；這些疾病以異常免疫活化，以及無法維持適當耐受的免疫調節失靈為特徵。HCT 經多種機轉發揮治療作用。
這些機轉包括前處理的免疫抑制，清除自體反應性免疫記憶，以及免疫系統再生與更新，重新誘導耐受，重整對自體抗原的異常反應（Cencioni 等，2022；Lima-Junior 等，2021）。多項機轉研究共同顯示，年齡或自體免疫所致的免疫失衡，可改善甚至消失。例如 CD27−IgD+ naïve B 細胞主導重建（Alexander 等，2009；Arruda 等，2018）、recent thymic emigrants 穩定輸出（Farge 等，2017a；Muraro 等，2005），帶來受體庫重新多樣化，以及各疾病中 regulatory B、T 細胞的恢復（Alexander 等，2013；Lima-Junior 等，2021）。Allo-HCT 研究較少，但包含免疫替換，且已有 graft-versus-autoimmune effect 的證據（Greco 等，2019）。
其他待研究領域包括 microbiome 對自體免疫的影響，以及 HCT 對此的作用（Alexander 等，2021）。
〔92.3 多發性硬化症（MS）的 HCT〕自 1995 年首例使用 auto-HCT 治療 MS 的病例報告以來（Fassas 等，1997），EBMT 已累積超過 2,000 人。早期將它用於晚期進行性疾病的救援，療效有限；近年對活動性復發型 MS，則有持久臨床及 MRI 反應，部分失能改善程度，是 DMT 少見的（Muraro 等，2017b；Tolf 等，2019）。
多數資料來自標準 DMT 無效後接受 auto-HCT 的觀察性群體。Burman 等（2018）選出四項最嚴謹的群體研究，合計 188 名復發型 MS：五年 PFS 為 70–91%；進展定義為 EDSS 自基線惡化至少 0.5–1 分。移植後兩年，70–92% 無疾病活動證據（NEDA），亦即無臨床復發、失能進展或 MRI 活動（Boffa 等，2021；Muraro 等，2017a）。與藥物註冊研究比較，auto-HCT 的 NEDA 高於包括高效 DMT 在內的療法，但研究族群不同，不能忽略此限制。文獻僅有兩項隨機試驗：第一項第二期試驗顯示，auto-HCT 抑制 MRI 活動優於 mitoxantrone（Mancardi 等，2015）。
第二項第三期試驗顯示，auto-HCT 較 DMT 延長失能進展時間。移植組／對照組 EDSS 變化分別為 3.4→2.4／3.31→3.98；復發事件為 1 對 39，失能進展為 6% 對 60%。移植組無重大副作用或治療相關死亡（Burt 等，2019）。
本書撰寫時，三項比較 auto-HCT 與 DMT 的第三期試驗正在收案：BEAT-MS（NCT04047628）、RAM-MS（NCT03477500）、STAR-MS（EudraCT 2019-001549-42），並預期有其他試驗開始（Sharrack 等，2022）。各中心前處理不同；因療效與可接受安全性平衡，EBMT ADWP 建議中等強度方案，即 BEAM＋ATG 或 CY 總量 200 mg/kg＋ATG（Sharrack 等，2020）。單中心資料顯示，含 busulfan 及體外 TCD 的高強度方案可能 PFS 較高，但毒性及 TRM 也可能較高（Atkins 等，2016）。回顧性登錄資料顯示 graft purging 沒有額外益處（Sharrack 等，2020）。
依本章指引，對 DMT 失敗的活動性復發型 MS，auto-HCT 為標準照護；對有疾病活動證據的進行型 MS，或侵襲性 MS 的第一線治療，也可作為選項。結果最好者通常不超過 45 歲、病程少於十年、失能不重（EDSS ≤6），且 MRI 有增強病灶等活動證據。ADWP 已發表 MS 與其他免疫介導神經 AD 的指引（Sharrack 等，2020），近期綜述也整理試驗（Sharrack 等，2022）；EBMT–ECTRIMS 工作坊後完成的跨專科更新，於原書中列為 Muraro 等「未發表」。
〔92.4 全身性硬化症（SSc）的 HCT〕過去 25 年，歐洲大型前瞻性觀察研究與 EUSTAR 登錄分析證實，包含 CY 的標準免疫抑制藥對 SSc 效益有限；SSc 特異死亡持續增加，主因心臟（31%）與肺部（18%）（Elhai 等，2017）。三項隨機試驗 ASSIST（Burt 等，2011）、ASTIS（van Laar 等，2014）、SCOT（Sullivan 等，2018）則顯示，早期快速進展 SSc 的 auto-HCT，在長期存活、肺功能及皮膚纖維化改善上優於 CY。
因此，早期嚴重瀰漫型皮膚 SSc（dcSSc）的自體移植，已獲 EBMT 以第一級證據推薦（Snowden 等，2022），亦獲 ACR、EULAR（Kowal-Bielecka 等，2017）及 ASTCT（Majhail 等，2015）支持，過去十年 EBMT 及全球移植活動均增加。
ASSIST 與 ASTIS 都用 CY 總量 200 mg/kg＋rabbit ATG 的 NMA 方案。差別主要為 ASSIST 以 CY 2 g/m² 動員、輸注未處理 PBSC；ASTIS 則以 CY 4 g/m² 動員、使用 CD34+ selected PBSC。SCOT 動員不用 CY、僅 G-CSF；前處理 CY 較低（總量 120 mg/kg），但另加具骨髓消除效果的 TBI：兩天四次，共 800 cGy，肺與腎以遮蔽降至 200 cGy。
病人選擇直接影響結果（Henes 等，2021），尤其單靠心臟超音波未偵測到的心臟受累，可能在容量負荷、CY／ATG 或敗血症壓力下顯現。現行章內建議依 2013 ACR／EULAR 分類（van den Hoogen 等，2013），對 18–65 歲 SSc 評估 auto-HCT，兒童個案另議。條件包括：病程 <2 年、瀰漫型、mRSS >20，並有 ESR >25 mm、CRP >5 mg/L，或無其他原因可解釋的 Hb <11 g/dL；或病程 <5 年，符合 a）mRSS ≥15 且嚴重呼吸、心血管或腎臟受累，或 b）mRSS <14、皮膚受累較少，但嚴重肺部病變進展，相較 12±6 個月前基值，FVC 及／或 TLC 改變 ≥10%，及／或 DLCO ≥15%。治療應在 JACIE 認證中心，由 SSc 專家與移植團隊共同執行。
團隊需依 Good Clinical Practices 在移植前、中、後評估及追蹤（Snowden 等，2017）。毒性與療效取決於病人選擇及前處理；不同化療可能造成細微結果差異。仍需研究依心功能與腎危象風險調降強度的方案（Burt 等，2021）。
〔92.5 全身性紅斑性狼瘡（SLE）的 HCT〕即使有 DMT，仍有不少 SLE 患者無法臨床緩解，並累積器官衰竭與死亡風險。自 1996 年起已有 auto-HCT 應用，全球報告超過 300 例（Alexander 與 Greco，2022）。最大兩組經驗來自 EBMT（53人，平均追蹤25個月）及 Northwestern University 單中心試驗（50人，平均29個月）；即使停止長期免疫抑制，兩組五年 DFS 機率均約 50%。
後續 EBMT 研究追蹤 2001–2008 年以不同方案移植的 28 名 SLE 患者，中位追蹤 38 個月，範圍 1–110 個月（Alchi 等，2013）。
該研究五年 PFS 僅 29%，但 TRM 逐步改善；CD34 selection 與顯著較低復發風險相關。較近期 Burt 報告 26 名接受 CYC／ATG／RTX 者，移植後第1、2、3、4、5年緩解率依序為 92%、81%、71%、62%、62%（Burt 等，2018）。
兩項獨立中國研究有十年追蹤，臨床反應顯著，PFS 分別 86% 與 68%，兩研究的 TRM 僅 2%（Burt 等，2021）。
彙整最相關的 15 項研究、339 名患者、中位五年追蹤，緩解率中位數為 65%，死亡率中位數 8%；TRM 從 2004 年首份 EBMT 調查的 12%，降至 2017–2019 年近期報告多數 <5%（Burt 等，2021）。反應者通常無臨床症狀，甚至 ANA 轉陰，這在傳統治療少見。早期 HCT 也可能減少器官衰竭與毒性負擔，改善生活品質（Burt 等，2018）。未處理移植物或不含 serotherapy 的前處理，復發較高（Alchi 等，2013）。現有證據與共識將 HCT 列為 clinical option：適用於長期免疫抑制、可合併 B 細胞標靶治療後，仍有 BILAG A 類活動性疾病者（Illei 等，2011；Snowden 等，2012、2022）。
〔92.6 Crohn disease（CD）的 HCT〕雖然 steroids、thiopurines／MTX 等免疫抑制及 anti-TNFα、anti-α4β7 integrin、anti-IL-12／IL-23 等 DMT 已使治療大幅進步，仍有患者對所有療法無效。手術可行，但可能造成短腸或永久造口，病人未必能接受。因此，對所有可用療法難治、組織持續受損且壽命可能縮短的部分患者，auto-HCT 成為有希望的選項。
多項研究顯示令人鼓舞、部分持久的反應，但長期追蹤也確認復發持續累積（Burt 等，2010；Lopez-Garcia 等，2017）。
此外，患者即使移植前對 anti-TNF 無效，移植後仍可能重新恢復對此藥物類別的反應。
EBMT 的 ASTIC 試驗，因移植後少數人符合「三個月臨床緩解」的嚴格複合主要終點，看似陰性（Hawkey 等，2015）。但不能把這項小型試驗視為 CD 移植效益的最終答案，後續長期追蹤已有鼓舞結果（Lindsay 等，2017）。另一 EBMT 回顧分析涵蓋未參與 ASTIC 的 82 名難治患者，約四分之一不需進一步藥物即維持緩解；多數復發者重新使用救援治療後，仍能長期控制疾病。一名患者發生 TRM（Brierley 等，2018）。
EBMT ADWP 與 ECCO 的共同立場建議，理想上在多中心試驗中採 auto-HCT；但對免疫抑制及生物製劑無效的活動性 CD，或手術風險不可接受者，可個別考慮（Snowden 等，2018）。建議以前處理 CY／ATG 為主，這也是多數 CD 移植的方案，在此困難族群有可接受且可預測的安全與療效平衡。須留意，較近期一項 FLU、CY、ATG 方案的隨機試驗，因意外嚴重毒性、包括 TMA 而提早終止（Lindsay，2021）。
後續重點是降低感染併發症。不含 CY 的動員似乎安全有效（Giordano 等，2022）；其他調整也將影響 auto-HCT 能否進一步普及於現代 DMT 難治的嚴重 CD。
〔92.7 自體免疫疾病的異體 HCT〕AD 曾以相合親屬、非親屬及臍帶血進行 allo-HCT。
過去 25 年 EBMT 累積 286 例。由於程序風險較高及晚期效應可能長期影響生活品質，使用多限制於兒科危及生命的 AD，最常見為免疫性血球低下，其次關節炎。Greco 等（2019）分析 1997–2014 年 128 人，中位年齡 12.7 歲（0.2–62.2）；100天 II–IV 級 aGVHD 20.8%，五年 cGVHD 累積發生率 27.8%，100天 NRM 12.7%，五年 OS／PFS 為 70.2%／59.4%。多變項分析顯示，<18歲、男性及較近期移植與較佳 PFS 相關；較低前處理強度與較低 NRM 相關。資料較完整的 64 人中，一年完全臨床反應為 67%。
Allo-HCT 亦可能用於新辨識的 VEXAS（Vacuoles、E1 enzyme、X-linked、Autoinflammatory、Somatic）疾病（Bruno 等，2023）。
整體而言經驗有限，但長期資料支持自體與異體 HCT 在 AD 治癒能力上存在基本生物學差異。
因 NRM 風險，allo-HCT 在 AD 仍屬有限且發展中的應用。隨時間其安全性改善，兒科尤其持續使用；改善病人選擇、減毒前處理及 PT-CY 等 GVHD 預防也在研究，促成擴展至非惡性疾病的興趣。對部分具有特定遺傳成分的 AD，allo-HCT 可能是唯一實際可達長期控制的策略，因此與自體發炎／免疫缺陷重疊者，尤其兒科，重新受到重視（Achini-Gutzwiller 等，2022）。
〔92.8 其他適應症〕其他 AD 見表92.2。免疫性血球低下曾以自體或異體 HCT 治療；第一型糖尿病早期「蜜月期」試驗顯示，可能避免或降低胰島素需求。其餘罕見神經、風濕及腸胃道適應症，需要登錄庫建立證據。
ADWP 指引（Snowden 等，2012；Greco 等，2021）及更新的 EBMT 細胞治療適應症建議（Snowden 等，2022），對這些罕見疾病提供審慎建議。
〔92.9 結論與未來方向〕隨證據累積、結果改善，也因現代生物性及其他治療並非人人有效，AD 成為 HCT 成長最快的適應症（Alexander 與 Greco，2022；Passweg 等，2021）。HCT 從預後差患者的救援，逐漸前移為治療選項；這建立於大型第二期、隨機第三期試驗，以及 SSc、MS、CD 的病人選擇與移植技術更新指引（Farge 等，2017b；Sharrack 等，2020；Snowden 等，2012）。
2023 年 AD 的主要 HCT 適應症為 MS、SSc 與 CD，因其中相當部分患者對傳統及標靶生物治療仍反應不佳（Alexander 與 Greco，2022）。
未來需促進 HCT 進入常規照護。建議在有經驗、JACIE 認證中心，以跨專科模式治療。前處理應依疾病優化，在維持療效的同時，平衡強度以降低毒性與 TRM。CAR-T 近期亦有正面初步經驗，為 AD 創新細胞治療開路（第93章）。
完整資料回報、生物資料庫基礎建設的協調與運用（Alexander 等，2015）、中心及網絡教育（包括 ADWP 活動；Burt 等，2021）、醫療經濟評估及實證建議，將共同確立 HCT 在各類自體免疫及發炎疾病流程中的未來定位。
【致謝】感謝 EBMT Paris Office 的 Manuela Badoglio、Myriam Labopin 提供登錄資料，感謝各 EBMT 中心對登錄庫的貢獻，以及參與 ADWP 的同仁。
【章末重點】① 隨隨機試驗等證據累積，AD 成為 auto-HCT 成長最快的適應症之一。② 主要包括 MS 與 SSc，auto-HCT 已進入治療流程。③ AD 以自體移植為主，但對合併自體發炎／免疫缺陷者，allo-HCT 的興趣再度增加。④ 建議於有經驗、JACIE 認證中心，以密切跨專科合作治療並回報 EBMT。⑤ 免疫重建研究正釐清移植後 immune reset 及 AD 病程機轉。

CART Cells and Other Cell 
Therapies (ie MSC, Tregs) 
in Autoimmune Diseases
Raffaella Greco and Dominique Farge
93.1	
Introduction
Auto-immune diseases (AD) are heterogeneous 
conditions, characterized by polyclonal activa­
tion of the immune system with a defect of B or 
T lymphocyte selection and altered lymphocytic 
reactions to auto-antigens components (Burnet 
1959a, b), although it is rare to identify a single 
antigenic epitope. The native immune system and 
its tissue environment play an important role to 
determine if exposure to a given antigen will 
induce an immune response or tolerance or 
anergy. The role of the genes coding for the major 
histocompatibility system molecules, but also of 
many other genes, is important in the regulation 
of the immune response, although this does not 
explain all the observed phenomena during loss 
of tolerance (Matzinger 1994; Rioux and Abbas 
2005).
R. Greco (*) 
Unit of Hematology and Bone Marrow 
Transplantation, IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital, 
Vita-Salute San Raffaele University, Milan, Italy
e-mail: greco.raffaella@hsr.it 
D. Farge 
Unité de Médecine Interne (UF 04): CRMR 
MATHEC, Maladies auto-immunes et thérapie 
cellulaire, Centre de Référence des Maladies 
auto-immunes systémiques Rares d’Ile-de-France 
FAI2R, EBMT CIC 0461, Hôpital St-Louis, AP-HP, 
Paris, France 
Université de Paris-Cité, IRSL, URP 3518, Eq 3: 
MATHEC-EUROCORD, Paris, France
e-mail: dominique.farge-bancel@sls.ap-hop-paris.fr
93
Over the years, a better understanding of the 
genetic background of ADs led to revise the tra­
ditional pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases. 
The presence of self-directed tissue inflammation 
as a component of each type of AD occurs inde­
pendently of T or B cells abnormalities. Most of 
the classical AD are polygenic diseases which 
result from a combination of auto-inflammatory 
and autoimmune mechanisms (Rioux and Abbas 
2005; McGonagle and McDermott 2006) with a 
predominant autoimmune component back­
ground [systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), 
Type 1 diabetes (T1D), autoimmune thyroiditis], 
whereas other polygenic AD have a predominant 
auto-inflammatory component [Crohn’s disease 
(CD) for instance]. More exceptionally, ADs are 
set by mutations associated with monogenic 
autoimmune 
diseases 
[Immunodysregulation 
polyendocrinopathy enteropathy X-linked syn­
drome (IPEX) with FOXP3 mutation] or on the 
other hand of the spectrum appear as monogenic 
auto-inflammatory 
diseases 
[Familial 
Mediterranean Fever with MEFV/pyrin, or TNF 
receptor-associated periodic fever syndrome 
(TRAPS) 
with 
TNFRSFIA/TNFR1]. 
Autoimmunity is used to cause by impairment of 
adaptive immunity, whereas autoinflammatory 
was originally defined as a consequence of 
unregulated innate immunity. Despite the con­
trast in the system primarily tangled, they share a 
lot of similarities, both in pathogenesis and clini­
cal presentations. Therefore, the optimal treat­
ment of an AD should be discussed considering 
837

this specific pathological continuum between 
autoimmunity and auto-inflammation, which 
variably interacts in the ultimate phenotypic 
expression (Alexander and Greco 2022).
In this context, restoration of the immune tol­
erance with consequent resolution of the inflam­
matory response against self-antigens is one of 
the 
treatment 
goals 
to 
provide 
durable 
remissions.
Different types of cellular therapies, which 
include mesenchymal stem cells (MSC), regula­
tory T cells (Tregs) and chimeric antigen recep­
tors (CAR) T cell therapies, have been developed 
to restore immunologic self-tolerance or foster 
tissue regeneration in AD patients.
93.2	
Mesenchymal Stem Cells 
(MSC)
MSC-based therapies (Burt et al. 2021) theoreti­
cally appear as ideal tools to target the respective 
auto-inflammatory and autoimmune components 
of AD.
MSC were first identified in the bone 

marrow (MSC- bone marrow [BM])-stem cell 
niche 45 years ago (Friedenstein 1976) and since 
extensively characterized as main support of hae­
matopoiesis. These multipotent progenitor cells 
can be harvested and cultured in vitro from many 
other sources, mostly from adipose tissue-
MSC(AT)-, umbilical cord (MSC- umbilical cord 
[UC]) or Wharton’s jelly MSC (WJ) for thera­
peutic applications. In vitro expanded MSC were 
defined a minima in 2006 by the International 
Society of Cellular Therapy (ISCT) MSC com­
mittee as: (1) a plastic-adherent polyclonal popu­
lation with fibroblast-like morphology, (2) 
positive for CD73, CD90 and CD105 markers (in 
>95% MSC), (3) negative for haematopoietic and 
endothelial markers and (4) able to differentiate 
in vitro into osteoblasts, adipocytes and chondro­
blasts (Dominici et al. 2006). MSC have in vitro 
and in  vivo immune-modulatory and immuno­
suppressive effects on both the innate and adap­
tive immunity and also pro-angiogenic and 
anti-fibrotic properties, all supporting their thera­
peutic use in several AD.
While MSC from various tissue sources share 
many biological features, they differ in terms of 
proliferation potential, multilineage capacities, 
overall transcriptional profile and functionality. 
Importantly, numerous other parameters modu­
late MSC functional properties, including autolo­
gous or allogeneic donor sources, each step of 
production processes (culture conditions, prim­
ing, scale of expansion, cryopreservation) and the 
recipients characteristics and inflammatory envi­
ronment, which account for high heterogeneity 
amongst the various MSC products used for clin­
ical application (Barrett et al. 2019; Fernandez-­
Santos et al. 2022; Menard and Tarte 2013).
MSC have long been considered as immuno-­
privileged, due to low level of MHC class I mol­
ecules and lack of MHC class II and several 
co-stimulatory molecules expression at basal 
state on their cell surface. However, MSC expo­
sure to inflammatory environment increases the 
MHC class I and induces MHC class II molecules 
expression. The use of unmatched allogeneic 
MSC infusion may induce anti-HLA class I anti­
bodies, with potential clinical consequences 
which are still under study (Farge et  al. 2021, 
2022; Menard and Tarte 2013).

Proinflammatory microenvironment in autoimmune dis­
ease patients shift MSC towards an immunomodulatory 
state, able to target multiple cells from the innate (inhibi­
tion of dendritic [DC] and natural killer [NK] cells, and 
polarization of M1–M2 macrophages) and acquired (inhi­
trigger transcriptomic, metabolic, and functional 
reprogramming and favour Treg differentiation 
and (b) efferocytosis, the process by which 
­apoptotic cells are engulfed, leading macro­
phages towards IDO expression and MSC 
towards PGE2 and IL-10 upregulation, which 
also accounts for their immunosuppressive activ­
ity (Galipeau and Sensebe 2018; Galleu et  al. 
2017; Pang et al. 2021; Zhang et al. 2019). MSC 
also produce extracellular vesicles (EVs), namely 
exosomes, microvesicles and apoptotic bodies, 
which are small membrane vesicles (44–100 nm 
diameter), with evident immunosuppressive and 
immunomodulatory activity in vitro and in ani­
bition of B, T-CD4+ and T-CD8+ cells, and activation of 
regulatory T [Treg] cells) immune responses, notably 
through the production of metabolic enzymes (e.g.: 
Indeolemine 2,3 dioxygenase [IDO]) and cytokines (e.g.: 
transforming growth factor [TGF]-β, interleukins [IL]-6 
and IL-10, prostaglandin E2 [PGE-2])
mal models, for which clinical applications are 
currently under study in several AD.
The importance to assess MSC functional 
properties has been underlined since 2016 
(Galipeau et al. 2016). The use of standardized 
functional markers of MSC potency and release 
potency assays, which must be defined to con­
duct advanced clinical studies, is of utmost 
importance and required to seek potential regis­
tration of the product. The preferred matrix 
assays to evaluate MSC immunosuppressive and 
immune-modulatory capacities include the use 
of: (a) quantitative RNA analysis of selected gene 
product, (b) flow cytometry analysis of function­

ally relevant surface markers, and (c) protein-­
based 
assay 
of 
secretome. 
In 
addition, 
multiparametric immune-monitoring tools have 
to be set up to characterize the patient immuno­
logical status and the various immune cell ­subsets 
before and after MSC treatment, to identify 
responders and thereby optimize clinical trials 
design.
93.2.1	 MSC Clinical Applications 
for AD
MSCs 
produced 
from 
various 
sources 
[MSC(BM), MSC(UC)- and MSC(AT)] have 
been studied in around 1700 clinical trials world­
wide for many conditions and their safety repeat­
edly demonstrated and summarized in a 2020 
meta-analysis of 55 clinical trials in 12 countries 
using MSCs in 2700 recipients with various dis­
eases (Thompson et al. 2020).
Initially tested in the pre-clinical model of 
multiple sclerosis (MS), the rationale for using 
MSCs in AD was subsequently obtained in many 
preclinical models and provide effective experi­
mental support for their clinical application in 
patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), SLE and 
CD, which are characterized by a predominant 
auto-inflammatory component, but also in other 
AD, such as Sjogren disease, systemic sclerosis 
(SSc), type I and II diabetes or autism.
Numerous phase I–II trials and few completed 
or still ongoing phase III trials worldwide were 
developed first in China and Asia, then in US and 
Europe, to analyse the safety and efficacy of 
either autologous or allogeneic MSCs, from vari­
ous tissue sources (UC, B, AT) using single or 
repeated iv, sc or local injections in neurological, 
rheumatological or gastrointestinal AD.
After 20 years of clinical research, since the 
first report (Le Blanc et al. 2004) on clinical effi­
cacy of MSC(M) in a child with refractory 
aGvHD and more than 1360 clinical trials for 
MSC registered on Clinicaltrails.gov as of April 
2023, in the field of AD per se only one MSC 
product allogeneic MSC(AT) for the treatment of 
Crohn’s fistula (Alofisel/Takeda) has been 
approved since 2018  in Europe, Japan and 
Canada. 
The 
first 
successful 
autologous 
MSC(AT) injection for CD rectovaginal fistula 
was performed in 2003. Several phase I and II 
studies for the treatment of anoperineal fistulas in 
CD reported 46–90%, efficacy until the ADMIRE 
phase III randomized, double-blind, international 
multicentre trial (RCT) demonstrated the superi­
ority of MSC(AT) over placebo in 212 patients 
with CD and one or more complex anoperineal 
fistulas (Garcia-Olmo et al. 2022). For the other 
auto-immune diseases, several phase I–II studies 
reported safety results and promising efficacy 
signals in progressive MS, RA, SLE, SSc still 
require large RCT to demonstrate MSC efficacy 
(Burt et al. 2021; Farge et al. 2022; Loisel et al. 
2023; Petrou et  al. 2020; Wen et  al. 2019). 
Progress in the field has been hampered by large 
heterogeneity when considering each AD type 
and patient selection, MSC type, origin and pro­
duction process, route of delivery and number of 
injections, clinical trial design and national 
regulations.
Although the number of clinical trials regis­
tered on www.clinicaltrials.gov using MSC-EVs 
for therapeutic purposes increases in the last 10 
years, few results are available (Burt et al. 2021).
93.3	
Regulatory T Cells (Tregs)
Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are a specialized sub­
set of CD4+ T lymphocytes endowed with 
immune-suppressive functions. Tregs are posi­
tively selected in the thymus and emigrate to the 
periphery. They represent a very heterogeneous 
population, distributed in secondary lymphoid 
organs and tissues. Tregs contribute to maintain 
the immune tolerance and to prevent autoimmu­
nity. Tregs constitutionally express high levels of 
the interleukin-2 receptor alpha (CD25) and are 
highly enriched in the fraction of CD4+CD25bright 
cells. In addition, they are classically identified as

CD127low and Forkhead-box-P3 (FoxP3)+ cells. 
The FoxP3 transcription factor has been identi­
fied as the master regulator, which is essential for 
Treg development (Ikegawa and Matsuoka 2021). 
Aberrant Treg plasticity, quantitative and func­
tional deficiencies of Treg impair immune 
homeostasis and importantly contribute to AD 
(Selck and Dominguez-Villar 2021).

The first approach relies on the induction of 
Tregs directly in vivo, by enhancing their activity 
and/or persistence. Several drugs employed for 
the treatment of autoimmune diseases act directly 
or indirectly on Treg numbers and/or functional­
ity. In this context, the role of rapamycin/siroli­
mus in increasing the number of Tregs through 
the inhibition of the mTOR pathway is well 
established (Greco et al. 2021; Peng et al. 2020). 
Moreover, an indirect boost of Treg expansion 
may be induced by CY, as used after allogeneic 
haematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) for the 
prevention of GvHD (Cieri et al. 2015; Fletcher 
et al. 2023).
Other interventions that increase the number 
of polyclonal endogenous Treg cells in  vivo 
involve low-dose interleukin-2 (IL-2), mutant 
IL-2, IL2/Anti-IL-2 Ab complexes. In contrast, 
applications of antigen-based treatments could 
lead to the enhancement of antigen-specific Treg 
subsets (Ikegawa and Matsuoka 2021).
Moreover, after autologous HCT, the reset of 
Treg compartment is essential to obtain long-­
term remission in ADs (Baraut et  al. 2014; 
Cencioni et al. 2022; Doglio et al. 2022).
A second approach relies on adoptive Treg 
cell therapies, through the optimal isolation and 
in vitro expansion of Treg cells.
Data have shown the feasibility and safety of 
adoptive polyclonal Treg transfer, with variable 
efficacy, explained by the low level of Treg per­
sistence in  vivo and a limited number of 
Ag-specific cells in the final cell product (Doglio 
et al. 2022; Eggenhuizen et al. 2020). Challenges 
in in vitro Treg expansion and long-term persis­
tence, as well as difficulties in the identification 
of specific antigens, have significantly slowed 
their clinical application (Xue et al. 2022).
However, antigen-specific Tregs can be gener­
ated in  vitro by genetic insertion of synthetic 
receptors, including engineered T cell receptors 
(TCR), B cell antibody receptors (BAR) or CAR 
(Scott 2021; Selck and Dominguez-Villar 2021). 
In the context of autoimmunity, CARs may be 
effective in redirecting the antigen specificity of 
Tregs, boosting their suppressive capacities.

93.4	
Chimeric Antigen Receptor T 
Cells (CART)
Chimeric antigen receptors (CAR) are chimeric 
molecules capable of redirecting the specificity 
of engineered cells against target antigens, while 
simultaneously boosting their activation (Freitag 
et al. 2020).
CARs are composed of three major compo­
nents: an extracellular domain, a linker peptide 
and an intracellular part. The extracellular 
domain accounts for the recognition of the anti­
gen. The intracellular portion mediates the 
transduction of the signal upon antigen binding. 
The most frequently used intracellular portions 
are represented by the zeta-chain of CD3 
(CD3z) and the intracellular portion of CD28, 
4-1BB and OX-40, each molecule being 
involved in the co-­stimulation and activation of 
T lymphocytes (Doglio et al. 2022). According 
to the composition of the intracellular part, dif­
ferent generations of CARs can be distin­
guished: (a) the first generation composed only 
by the CD3z, (b) the second generation with 
two different domains with CD28-CD3z and 
4-1BB-CD3z, which represent the two most 
frequent combinations in use and (c) a third 
generation with three domains, generally 
obtained by adding OX-40 to a second genera­
tion CAR (Sadelain et al. 2017).
Conventional T cells (Tconvs) expressing 
CARs revealed impressive clinical results in 
patients affected by haematological malignan­
cies, since their cytotoxic action could be specifi­
cally redirected against transformed cells (Sterner 
and Sterner 2021).
Additionally, CAR-T cells (CART) may be 
employed in the field of autoimmunity, thanks to 
their 
ability 
of 
conferring 
new 
antigen-­
specificities and to simultaneously boost cell 
activation (Alexander and Greco 2022).
B cells and their effectors such as antibodies 
and cytokines impact the pathophysiology of 
ADs (Lee et al. 2021), thus attracting innovative 
B cell depletion therapies. Compared to mono­
clonal antibodies, CART have the advantage of a 
broader depletion of autoreactive B cells, (Doglio 
et  al. 2022), especially those maintained in 
inflamed tissues and access to lymphoid organ 
(i.e. lymph node and spleen).

93.5	
Conclusions and Future 
Directions
New insights are emerging in the complexity and 
power of innovative cellular therapies. MSC, a 
heterogeneous population of stromal cells with 
high regenerative capacity that can be isolated, 
cultured, and expanded ex vivo represent a prom­
ising source for cellular therapy approaches in 
AD due to their immunosuppressive, angiogenic 
and anti-fibrotic properties. MSCs plasticity and 
their regenerative and immunomodulatory prop­
erties are known to be driven by microenviron­
mental factors. MSC of different tissue origin 
have been investigated for treating several indica­
tions. Progresses in the field have been hampered 
by large heterogeneity of MSC products and 
sources. Promising results have been obtained in 
SSc, SLE and access to the market in CD.
Tregs, a specialized subset of T lymphocytes 
with immune suppressive capacities and dys­
functional in AD constitute the ideal candidate 
for adoptive cell therapy in AD.  Despite safe, 
polyclonal Tregs mediated suboptimal/controver­
sial responses in clinical trials, mainly due to low 
amount of disease relevant antigen-specific cells. 
CARs can redirect the T cell antigen specificity, 
aiming at restoring the immune tolerance.
CAR-Tregs were proven very effective in con­
trolling inflammatory conditions in AD pre-­
clinical studies Current available clinical data 
reveal that CD19 conventional CART effectively 
deplete B cells in patients with SLE, leading to 
impressive drug-free remission in patients refrac­
tory to standard therapies. The clinical effect of 
CART appears to be associated with abrogation 
of autoimmunity and persists even after B cell 
reconstitution. Longer follow-up is warranted 
after these preliminary promising experiences 
with various CART approaches in a variety of 
AD (antisynthetase syndrome, SSc, NMOSD). 
These findings show that the generation and 
administration of CART in AD is feasible and 
safe.
Future studies are warranted to further eluci­
date the mechanism of action of these cellular-­
based therapies, while shedding light on the 
underlying pathogenesis of AD.
Key Points
•	 AD are heterogeneous conditions char­
acterized by aberrant activation of the 
immune system with failure of the 
immune regulation to maintain adapted 
tolerance.
•	 The optimal treatment of AD should be 
discussed, in light of this pathological 
continuum between autoimmunity and 
auto-inflammation, 
which 
variably 
interacts in each AD phenotypic 
expression.
•	 MSC based therapies appear as ideal 
tools to target the respective auto-­
inflammatory and autoimmune compo­
nents of AD. Progresses in the field have 
been hampered by large heterogeneity.
•	 Tregs constitute the ideal candidate for 
adoptive cell therapy in AD, aiming at 
restoring the immune tolerance. Despite 
safe, polyclonal Tregs mediated contro­
versial results in clinical trials. CAR-­
Tregs 
proved 
very 
effective 
in 
controlling inflammatory conditions in 
pre-clinical studies.
•	 CART approach is feasible, tolerable 
and highly effective in severe/refractory 
SLE and other AD (antisynthetase syn­
drome, SSc, NMOSD) in preliminary 
clinical reports. Longer follow-up is 
warranted.

zh: 自體免疫疾病的 CAR-T、MSC 與 Tregs
points: 自體免疫與自體發炎在不同疾病中比例不同，選擇細胞治療需對應機轉。
MSC 具有免疫調節潛力，但產品異質性與研究差異限制結論。
Tregs／CAR-Tregs 目標是恢復耐受，不能與清除 B cells 的 CAR-T 當成同一作用。
本章 CAR-T 在嚴重／難治 SLE 等疾病的資料多為早期報告，反應可佳但仍需長期追蹤。
需評估感染、低免疫球蛋白、血球低下及其他細胞治療毒性。
question: SLE 的早期 CAR-T 報告療效佳，是否代表已證實適用所有自體免疫病？
answer: 不是。疾病、產品、樣本數與追蹤仍有限，應保留證據層級與長期安全的不確定性。
trap: 早期可行性、療效訊號與標準治療地位不同。
fullTranslationText:
【第93章：自體免疫疾病的 CAR-T 與其他細胞治療（MSC、Tregs）】作者：Raffaella Greco、Dominique Farge。〔93.1 導論〕AD 是異質疾病，以免疫系統多克隆活化、B／T 淋巴球選擇缺陷，以及對自體抗原成分的反應改變為特徵（Burnet，1959a、b），但很少能找出單一抗原表位。先天免疫系統與組織環境，會影響抗原暴露究竟引發免疫反應、耐受或無反應。MHC 分子及許多其他基因，對免疫調節很重要，但無法解釋耐受喪失時的所有現象（Matzinger，1994；Rioux 與 Abbas，2005）。
近年對 AD 遺傳背景更深入的了解，使傳統的自體免疫病生理概念受到修正。
每一類 AD 都可能有對自身組織的發炎，並不完全依賴 T／B 細胞異常。多數典型 AD 是自體發炎與自體免疫機轉共同作用的多基因疾病（Rioux 與 Abbas，2005；McGonagle 與 McDermott，2006）。SLE、第一型糖尿病、自體免疫甲狀腺炎等，以自體免疫成分為主；Crohn disease 等則較偏自體發炎。較少見者是單基因自體免疫疾病，例如 FOXP3 變異造成的 IPEX；光譜另一端則是單基因自體發炎疾病，例如 MEFV／pyrin 相關家族性地中海熱，或 TNFRSF1A／TNFR1 相關 TRAPS。
傳統上，自體免疫被歸於適應性免疫失衡，自體發炎則歸於先天免疫失控。雖然最初涉及的系統不同，兩者在病生理及臨床表現上有許多相似處。因此，最佳治療應考慮自體免疫與自體發炎的連續光譜，以及兩者如何共同決定最終表型（Alexander 與 Greco，2022）。作者機構：R. Greco，IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital／Vita-Salute San Raffaele University，Milan；greco.raffaella@hsr.it。D. Farge，CRMR MATHEC、Hôpital St-Louis AP-HP、Université de Paris-Cité／IRSL URP3518 MATHEC-EUROCORD，Paris；dominique.farge-bancel@sls.ap-hop-paris.fr。
在此背景下，恢復免疫耐受、讓對自體抗原的發炎反應消退，是獲得持久緩解的治療目標之一。
MSC、regulatory T cells（Tregs）與 CAR-T 等不同細胞療法，已被開發用來恢復自我免疫耐受，或促進 AD 患者組織再生。
〔93.2 間質幹／基質細胞（MSC）〕理論上，MSC 療法可同時針對 AD 的自體發炎與自體免疫成分，因而是理想工具（Burt 等，2021）。
MSC 約在 45 年前，首次於骨髓幹細胞 niche 中被辨識（Friedenstein，1976），此後被廣泛研究為造血的主要支持細胞。這些多潛能祖細胞也可從其他組織取得並體外培養，主要包括脂肪、臍帶及 Wharton’s jelly。ISCT MSC 委員會於 2006 年提出體外擴增 MSC 的最低定義：① 黏附塑膠、具纖維母細胞樣形態的多克隆群體；② >95% 表現 CD73、CD90、CD105；③ 不表現造血及內皮標記；④ 體外能分化為成骨、脂肪及軟骨細胞（Dominici 等，2006）。MSC 在體外及體內可調控、抑制先天與適應性免疫，也有促血管新生與抗纖維化特性，支持其 AD 治療潛力。
不同組織來源 MSC 雖有許多共同生物特性，增殖潛力、多系分化能力、整體轉錄輪廓與功能仍不同。
其他影響功能的因素包括自體／異體來源、製造各階段（培養、priming、擴增規模、冷凍），以及受者特徵與發炎環境，造成臨床 MSC 產品高度異質（Barrett 等，2019；Fernandez-Santos 等，2022；Menard 與 Tarte，2013）。
MSC 在基礎狀態的 MHC-I 表現低，且缺乏 MHC-II 與多種共刺激分子，因此長期被認為具有 immune privilege。但發炎暴露會提高 MHC-I 並誘導 MHC-II；輸注未配對異體 MSC 可能誘發 anti-HLA class I 抗體，臨床後果仍在研究（Farge 等，2021、2022；Menard 與 Tarte，2013）。
MSC 可調控體液與細胞免疫，包括抑制 B、T、NK、樹突細胞，減少促發炎細胞激素，以及阻止嗜中性球募集（圖93.1）。它們可透過細胞接觸作用，但主要為旁分泌，釋放代謝酵素（Han 等，2022），核心為 IDO／iNOS，及 VEGF、PDGF、ANG-1、IL-11、PGE2、TSG-6、SDF-1、HGF、IGF-1 等因子。這些並非固定持續表現，而由 IFN-γ±TNF-α、IL-1α／β 等發炎刺激誘導，可在體外 priming 或局部組織發生，並共同促進修復。
體內模型還發現：a）MSC 將粒線體轉移給 T 細胞，可重整轉錄、代謝及功能，促進 Treg 分化；b）efferocytosis，即吞噬凋亡細胞的過程，促進巨噬細胞 IDO 表現，以及 MSC 的 PGE2、IL-10 上調，也參與免疫抑制作用（Galipeau 與 Sensebe，2018；Galleu 等，2017；Pang 等，2021；Zhang 等，2019）。MSC 亦產生 extracellular vesicles（EVs），包括 exosomes、microvesicles、apoptotic bodies；原文描述其為直徑 44–100 nm 的膜性囊泡，於體外及動物模型有明顯免疫調控／抑制活性，數種 AD 的臨床應用正在研究。
【圖93.1：MSC 在 AD 的免疫調控】病人的促發炎微環境，會使 MSC 轉向免疫調節狀態，同時影響先天免疫（抑制 DC、NK，促進巨噬細胞由 M1 向 M2 極化）與後天免疫（抑制 B、CD4+、CD8+ T 細胞，活化 Tregs）。主要媒介包括 IDO 等代謝酵素，以及 TGF-β、IL-6、IL-10、PGE2 等訊號分子。
自 2016 年起，MSC 功能評估的重要性受到強調（Galipeau 等，2016）。進階試驗及產品註冊，需定義標準化 potency 功能標記與產品放行試驗。建議矩陣式評估包括：a）特定基因產物的定量 RNA 分析；b）功能相關表面標記的流式分析；c）secretome 的蛋白質分析。此外，需建立多參數免疫監測，在治療前後描繪患者免疫狀態及各細胞亞群，辨認反應者並優化試驗設計。
〔93.2.1 MSC 的 AD 臨床應用〕BM、UC、AT 等來源 MSC 已用於全球約 1,700 項、涵蓋多疾病的試驗；安全性反覆被證實。2020 年統合分析彙整 12 國 55 項試驗、2,700 名受者（Thompson 等，2020）。
MSC 的 AD 應用最初由 MS 前臨床模型支持，之後多種模型也提供證據，用於 RA、SLE、CD 等具顯著自體發炎成分的疾病，以及 Sjögren disease、SSc、第一／二型糖尿病或 autism 等其他情境。
世界各地有許多第一至二期，以及少數完成或進行中的第三期研究，先始於中國與亞洲，再擴至歐美。這些研究評估不同來源、自體或異體 MSC，以單次或重複靜脈、皮下或局部注射，治療神經、風濕及腸胃道 AD 的安全性與療效。
自 Le Blanc 等（2004）首次報告 MSC 用於兒童難治 aGVHD 的臨床療效後，已有約二十年研究；截至 2023 年4月，ClinicalTrials.gov 登錄逾 1,360 項 MSC 試驗。但就 AD 本身，依原書時點，僅治療 Crohn fistula 的異體脂肪 MSC 產品 Alofisel／Takeda，自 2018 年起陸續在歐洲、日本、加拿大獲准。首例成功自體脂肪 MSC 注射治療 CD 直腸陰道瘻管是在 2003 年。多項第一、二期肛周瘻管研究的有效率為 46–90%；之後 ADMIRE 第三期國際多中心隨機雙盲試驗，在 212 名有複雜肛周瘻管的 CD 患者，證實脂肪 MSC 優於安慰劑（Garcia-Olmo 等，2022）。其他 AD 如進行型 MS、RA、SLE、SSc，有安全性及初步療效訊號，仍需大型 RCT 確認（Burt 等，2021；Farge 等，2022；Loisel 等，2023；Petrou 等，2020；Wen 等，2019）。
進展受到高度異質性限制，包括 AD 類型、病人選擇、MSC 種類／來源／製程、給藥途徑與次數、試驗設計及各國法規。
過去十年，MSC-EVs 的治療試驗登錄增加，但可用結果仍少（Burt 等，2021）。
〔93.3 調節性 T 細胞（Tregs）〕Tregs 是具免疫抑制功能的 CD4+ T 細胞亞群，經胸腺正向選擇後移至周邊，分布於次級淋巴器官及組織，異質性很高。它們維持免疫耐受並預防自體免疫，持續高表現 IL-2 receptor α（CD25），富集於 CD4+CD25bright 群體，典型表型另包括 CD127low、FoxP3+。
FoxP3 轉錄因子是 Treg 發育所必需的主調控因子（Ikegawa 與 Matsuoka，2021）。
Treg 可塑性異常、數量或功能不足，會破壞免疫恆定，促成 AD（Selck 與 Dominguez-Villar，2021）。
基於這些特性，Tregs 是 AD 免疫治療的理想候選。已有多種增強 Treg 反應的策略（圖93.2；Doglio 等，2022；Xue 等，2022）。
第一種策略是在體內直接誘導 Tregs，提高活性或持續性。數種 AD 藥物可直接或間接影響 Treg 數量／功能；rapamycin／sirolimus 經 mTOR 抑制增加 Tregs 的作用已充分建立（Greco 等，2021；Peng 等，2020）。
CY 也可能間接促進 Treg 擴增，例如移植後用於 GVHD 預防時（Cieri 等，2015；Fletcher 等，2023）。
其他在體內增加多克隆內生 Tregs 的方法，包括低劑量 IL-2、突變型 IL-2、IL-2／anti-IL-2 antibody complexes。相對地，抗原導向療法可增強抗原特異性 Treg 亞群（Ikegawa 與 Matsuoka，2021）。
Auto-HCT 後 Treg 群體的重置，也是 AD 達成長期緩解的關鍵（Baraut 等，2014；Cencioni 等，2022；Doglio 等，2022）。
第二種策略是過繼性 Treg 治療，透過最佳化分離及體外擴增取得細胞。
多克隆 Treg 過繼輸注已證實可行且安全，但療效不一，可能因體內持續性低、最終產品的抗原特異性細胞比例有限（Doglio 等，2022；Eggenhuizen 等，2020）。體外擴增、長期存續與疾病特異抗原辨識的困難，都延緩臨床應用（Xue 等，2022）。
但可經基因導入合成受體，在體外製造抗原特異性 Tregs；受體包括工程化 TCR、B-cell antibody receptor（BAR）或 CAR（Scott，2021；Selck 與 Dominguez-Villar，2021）。
在自體免疫情境，CAR 可重新導向 Treg 的抗原特異性，增強其抑制能力。
CAR-Tregs 在前臨床研究，已非常有效地控制發炎狀態（Doglio 等，2022）。
【圖93.2：Treg 為基礎的 AD 治療】主要有體內增強 Treg 與過繼輸注體外擴增 Treg 兩大策略，均可為多克隆或抗原特異性。a）增加體內多克隆 Treg：sirolimus 等藥物、低劑量 IL-2、突變型 IL-2、IL-2／anti-IL-2 複合物，以及 anti-CD3 選擇性去除 effector T（Teff）細胞。b）抗原療法增強抗原特異性亞群。c）最佳化分離與擴增後，回輸多克隆 Tregs。d）體外製造抗原特異性 Tregs：導入工程化 TCR、CAR、BAR，或將抗原特異性 Teff 轉為 induced Tregs（iTregs）。轉換方法包括 TGF-β＋IL-2 刺激、轉基因 FOXP3 過度表現、阻斷 CDK8／CDK19，或合併 CTLA-4 過度表現、IL-2 去除及抗原刺激。Ag＝抗原；DCs＝樹突細胞；APL＝改變的 peptide ligands；pMHC＝peptide–MHC 複合體。改編自 Doglio 等（2022）、Selck 與 Dominguez-Villar（2021）。
〔93.4 CAR-T〕CAR 是嵌合分子，能把工程化細胞的特異性重新導向目標抗原，同時增強細胞活化（Freitag 等，2020）。
其三個主要部分為胞外區、連接 peptide、胞內區；胞外區負責辨識抗原，胞內區在結合抗原後傳遞訊號。
最常見胞內構造包括 CD3ζ，以及 CD28、4-1BB、OX-40 的胞內區，參與 T 細胞共刺激與活化（Doglio 等，2022）。依組成可區分：第一代僅 CD3ζ；第二代含兩個區域，最常見為 CD28–CD3ζ 或 4-1BB–CD3ζ；第三代有三個區域，通常在第二代上再加 OX-40（Sadelain 等，2017）。
表現 CAR 的 conventional T cells（Tconvs），能將細胞毒性導向轉化細胞，在血液惡性疾病取得顯著結果（Sterner 與 Sterner，2021）。
因為 CAR 能同時賦予新抗原特異性並增強活化，也可應用於自體免疫（Alexander 與 Greco，2022）。
B 細胞及其抗體、細胞激素等效應產物參與 AD 病理，因此引發新 B 細胞去除療法的興趣（Lee 等，2021）。相較單株抗體，CAR-T 可更廣泛清除自體反應性 B 細胞，尤其是發炎組織中殘留者，並能進入淋巴結、脾臟（Doglio 等，2022）。
早期臨床經驗（表93.1）顯示，CD19-CAR Tconvs 對 SLE 有效，五名患者的腎炎及其他症狀消退（Mackensen 等，2022；Mougiakakos 等，2021）。此效果伴隨深度 B 細胞去除，之後在輸注後中位約 110 天觀察到 B 細胞重新出現。
三個月後，循環中仍可檢出 CAR-T。所有人均接受自體 CD19 CAR-T，沒有重大毒性，僅輕度 CRS；anti-dsDNA 抗體與補體數值皆恢復正常。
CD19 CAR-T 另有難治 antisynthetase syndrome 一例（Müller 等，2023）及嚴重 SSc 一例的初步經驗（Bergmann 等，2023）。
BCMA CAR-T 已在 12 名 R/R neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder（NMOSD）患者研究（Qin 等，2023）。
只報告輕度 CRS；中位追蹤 5.5 個月時，11 名患者未復發，並伴隨自體抗體下降。
【表93.1：AD 的 CAR-T 臨床應用】Mougiakakos 等（2021）：活動性 lupus nephritis，一人；CD19 CAR、4-1BB 共刺激。Lymphodepletion：FLU 25 mg/m²/day IV，第 −5、−4、−3 天，CY 1,000 mg/m² IV，第 −3 天。無 CRS、ICANS 或其他毒性；蛋白尿／SLEDAI 臨床緩解，dsDNA／C3、C4 血清學緩解；追蹤44天。Mackensen 等（2022）：多器官 SLE 五人，全有腎炎；相同 CD19／4-1BB 及 FLU／CY 劑量。3／5 有一級 CRS，無 ICANS、無感染；5／5 腎炎、其他症狀及血清學緩解；追蹤8個月。Müller 等（2023）：antisynthetase syndrome 一人；lentiviral CD19 CAR，相同 FLU／CY。一级 CRS，短暫 CK 增加及肌痛；Ig 下降。肌力與耐力改善、CK／myoglobin 下降、血清學緩解，MRI 肌炎消退；追蹤200天。
【表93.1續】Bergmann 等（2023）：瀰漫皮膚 SSc，合併廣泛心肌及肺纖維化、肺高壓；lentiviral CD19 CAR。因腎功能不佳減半劑量：FLU 12.5 mg/m²，第 −5、−4、−3 天；CY 500 mg/m²，第 −3 天。一級 CRS、無 ICANS 或其他毒性；心臟、關節、皮膚改善，血清學緩解，肺纖維化穩定；追蹤6個月。Qin 等（2023）：NMOSD 十二人；BCMA CAR。FLU 30 mg/m²/day IV＋CY 500 mg/m²/day IV，第 −4、−3、−2 天。12／12 為一至二級 CRS，無 ICANS 或其他神經毒性；常見血液毒性，58% 感染（無第四級），25% CMV。11／12 達無藥物及血清學緩解，12／12 失能改善；追蹤5.5個月。縮寫：Ab＝自體抗體、CRS＝細胞激素釋放症候群、ICANS＝免疫效應細胞相關神經毒性症候群、Ig＝免疫球蛋白；其餘縮寫依原表疾病與藥物名稱。
整體初步經驗顯示 AD 對 CAR-T 可迅速反應，但需延長追蹤確定長期療效。
〔93.5 結論與未來方向〕創新細胞治療的複雜性與潛力，正逐漸被了解。MSC 是可分離、培養與體外擴增、具高再生能力的異質 stromal cells，免疫抑制、促血管新生及抗纖維化特性，使其成為 AD 有希望的細胞來源。其可塑性、再生與免疫調節能力受微環境驅動，不同組織來源已用於多種疾病，但產品與來源異質性阻礙進展。SSc、SLE 有鼓舞結果，CD 已有產品上市。
Tregs 具有免疫抑制能力，AD 中常功能失調，是過繼治療理想候選。多克隆 Treg 雖安全，臨床反應仍不理想或有爭議，主因可能是疾病相關抗原特異性細胞太少。
CAR 可重新導向 T 細胞抗原特異性，以恢復免疫耐受為目標。
CAR-Tregs 在 AD 前臨床研究有效控制發炎。現有早期臨床資料顯示，CD19 conventional CAR-T 能有效清除 SLE 的 B 細胞，讓標準治療難治者出現顯著無藥物緩解；效果似與自體免疫消退相關，即使 B 細胞恢復後仍持續。Antisynthetase syndrome、SSc、NMOSD 的不同 CAR-T 初步經驗，仍需更長追蹤。
這些發現顯示，在 AD 製造及給予 CAR-T 是可行且初步安全的。
未來研究需進一步闡明細胞療法機轉，也藉此了解 AD 本身的病理。
【致謝】感謝 EBMT Paris Office 的 Manuela Badoglio、Myriam Labopin 提供登錄資料、各中心對資料庫的貢獻，以及 ADWP 參與者。
【章末重點】① AD 是免疫異常活化、調控無法維持耐受的異質疾病。
② 最佳治療應考慮自體免疫與自體發炎的連續光譜，以及兩者對各疾病表型的不同影響。
③ MSC 理論上可同時針對兩種病理成分，但高度異質性阻礙進展。
④ Tregs 可望恢復耐受；多克隆產品雖安全，試驗療效有爭議。CAR-Tregs 前臨床抑制發炎效果良好。
⑤ 初步報告中，CAR-T 對嚴重／難治 SLE，以及 antisynthetase syndrome、SSc、NMOSD 可行、耐受且有效，仍需長期追蹤。

94.2	
Solid Tumours in Children 
and Adolescents
Ruth Ladenstein
Regarding the respective solid tumour entities 
relevant in the paediatric and adolescent age 
groups this year’s report informs on recent 
advances in the literature. In brief, to date the evi­
dence for high-dose-therapy (HDT)/HCT from 
prospective randomized trials is still limited to 
high-risk neuroblastoma hrNBL and Ewing sar­
coma (Matthay et al. 2009; Whelan et al. 2018).
94.2.1	 Recall on General Lessons 
Based on EBMT Data
Transplant-related mortality. TRM markedly 
decreased over time and is related with the HDT 
regimen (i.e., elimination of TBI) and most 
importantly use of peripheral stem cells. TRM 
rates associated to auto-HCT dropped to under 
5% after 1992 and is since 2012 only 1%.
Total body irradiation. TBI showed no advan­
tage in any of the solid tumour indications and 
should thus be avoided in children with solid 
tumours in view of late effects.
Remission status. First-line high-risk patients 
perform significantly better than after relapse. 
Response to induction treatments prior to HDT/
HCT is critical in all indications. In brief, good 
response to first-line treatment (CR/VGPR/PR) 
in high-risk patients in and sensitive relapse 
(SR) are good indications, while patients with 
stable disease or minor response (<50%) (SD/
MR) should only be considered for well-defined 
phase I/phase II trials. Patients with no response 
(NR) or tumour progression or refractory dis­
ease (RR) have a very short life expectancy even 
after HDT/HCT and thus should not be 
considered.
Age plays a crucial role as outcome predictor. 
Adolescent age is generally associated with infe­
rior outcome. While age <10 years is a favourable 
factor in sarcomas (Ewing sarcoma and rhabdo­
myosarcoma), NBL has an earlier cut-off at 
5 years. Patients with NBL ≤18 months at diag­
nosis need biological profiling and are only eli­
gible with high-risk biological features, in 
particular MYCN amplification (Canete et  al. 
2009; Ladenstein et al. 2023).
Double HCT approaches. The EBMT data on 
tandem or repetitive HDT/HCT approaches show 
no advantage over single HDT/HCT.  However, 
the elective selection of particularly poor-­
prognosis patients in phase II settings is a likely 
bias. A randomized trial in NBL emerged with 
superiority for the tandem strategy for hrNBL in 
front-line patients (Park et al. 2016).
Busulfan–melphalan. This HDT combination 
is the only one in the EBMT database resulting in 
significantly improved survival rates in NBL and 
Ewing tumours.
Allo-HCT. No advantage for allo-HCT can be 
detected in the EBMT data for any paediatric 
solid tumour indication. The potential bias of 
negative selection of particular poor-prognosis 
patients’ needs to be considered.
The EBMT data showed a benefit from sal­
vage HDT/HCT in responding patients relapsing 
after 12  months from diagnosis and without a 
previous HDT.
94.2.2	 Neuroblastoma (NBL)
High-risk neuroblastoma (hrNBL) is defined in 
the front-line setting by widespread disease 
>18 months, but includes any stage and age in the 
presence of MYCN oncogene amplification 
(Cohn et  al. 2009; Moroz et  al. 2011; Canete 
et al. 2009; Ladenstein et al. 2023). In addition, 
genetic alterations of ALK (clonal mutations and 
amplifications) are independent predictors of 
poorer survival in hrNBL (Bellini et  al. 2021; 
Goldsmith et  al. 2023) ALK inhibitors are 
increasingly integrated in upfront treatments, 
mostly the third-generation ALK inhibitor lorlati­
nib, and contribute to improved response rates 
prior to HCT.  Standard treatment approaches

include multicycle, intense induction where 
recently combinations with immunotherapy are 
evaluated in randomised trails, local control via 
mostly extensive surgery to the primary tumour 
site enhanced by radiotherapy including local 
and, in some collaborative groups, also meta­
static 
sites 
delivered 
after 
HDT/auto-­
HCT.  Immunotherapy for maintenance with 
respective ch14.18 antibodies is meanwhile con­
sidered standard (Park et al. 2016; Yu et al. 2010; 
Ladenstein et al. 2017, 2018).
94.2.2.1	
Autologous HCT in NBL
Although three randomized trials and a meta-­
analysis have demonstrated that HDT with aHCT 
improves EFS in high-risk NBL (Pritchard et al. 
2005; Berthold et al. 2005; Matthay et al. 2009; 
Yalçin et al. 2013), there is no consensus which 
HDT regimen is superior. Whilst EBMT data and 
the HR-NBl1/SIOPEN trial support Busulphan 
and Melphalan as HDT regimen (Ladenstein 
et al. 2008, 2017), the randomized results of the 
ANBL0532 COG found superiority for double 
HDT/HCT [first HDT, CY and TT; second HDT, 
CBP, VP and MEL (with reduced doses of single 
HDT CEM) vs. single HDT (CEM)/auto-HCT 
(Park et al. 2019) with Anti-GD2 antibody-based 
immunotherapy being beneficial for both arms 
(Yu et al. 2010)]. The value of a tandem approach 
including Busulphan and Melphalan is currently 
explored within the randomized HRNBL2/
SIOPEN trial.
A recent analysis (Ladenstein et al. 2023) on 
MYCN amplified NBL in infants and toddlers 
found markedly improved outcomes within the 
HR-NBl1/SIOPEN trial for infants and toddlers.
Targeted therapies, in particular iodine-­131-­
metaiodobenzylguanidine (mIBG) therapy with 
and without chemotherapy or radiosensitisers 
like vorinostat and/or HDT followed by HCT, 
have generated increasing interest (Lee et  al. 
2017; Johnson et  al. 2011; Ferry et  al. 2018; 
Kraal et  al. 2017, 2019; DuBois et  al. 2021). 
Further HDT tandem approaches with or without 
mIBG are currently explored by the COG and 
SIOPEN in randomized and by other groups in 
non-randomized trials (Lee et al. 2017).
94.2.2.2	
Allogeneic HCT in NBL
The role of allo-HCT remains controversial. 
Allo-HCT as immunotherapy received special 
attention after introduction of RIC and NMA 
transplants. Some reports highlight a graft-­
versus-­tumour (GvT) effect with adopted allo-­
HCT approaches, while early EBMT data showed 
no benefit with classical allo-HCT (Ladenstein 
et  al. 1994). The CIBMTR conducted a retro­
spective review showing some benefit for allo-­
HCT in patients without prior auto HCT (Hale 
et al. 2013). The Japan Children’s Cancer Group 
(JCCG) (Hara et  al. 2022) reported recently 
improved outcomes with allo-HCT.
Haplo-HCT in very high-risk refractory/
relapsed (R(/R) patients is capable to induce 
long-term remission (Illhardt et al. 2018). Graft-­
versus-­NBL effects can be elicited by transplan­
tation of haploidentical hematopoietic cells 
(haplo-HCT) exploiting cytotoxic functions of 
natural killer cells and their activation by the anti-
­GD2 antibody dinutuximab beta (DB) (Flaadt 
et al. 2023). Immunotherapy after haplo-HCT is 
feasible, with low risk of inducing GvHD and 
resulted in markedly improved long-term sur­
vival likely attributable to increased anti-NBL 
activity by donor-derived effector cells.
94.2.2.3	
Cell Therapy in NBL
The success of anti-GD2 therapy has proven that 
immunotherapy can be effective in NBL. Adoptive 
transfer of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T 
cells has the potential to build on this success. In 
early phase clinical trials, CART for NBL has 
proven to be safe and feasible, but significant bar­
riers to efficacy remain. One such approach is 
adoptive transfer of CART cells, which combine 
the specificity of an antibody with the cytolytic 
capacity of T cells in an MHC independent man­
ner. Persisting hurdles to date include lack of T 
cell persistence and potency, difficulty in target 
identification, and an immunosuppressive tumour 
microenvironment. Outcomes so far have been 
encouraging but modest, with only a fraction of 
patients achieving measurable responses and 
very few patients demonstrating long-term per­
sistence of CART cells (Yang et al. 2017; Yeku

et al. 2017; Pinto et al. 2018; Richards et al. 2018; 
Heczey et al. 2017). Immunotherapy with CAR T 
cells that target the disialoganglioside GD2 
expressed on tumour cells, i.e., third-generation 
GD2-CART cells expressing the inducible cas­
pase 9 suicide gene (GD2-CART01) may be a 
new therapeutic opportunity in R/R advanced 
high-risk neuroblastoma (Del Bufalo et al. 2023).
94.2.2.4	
Recommended Indications 
NBL–HCT
Standard indications include first-line hrNBL 
>18 months at diagnosis with widespread meta­
static disease or those of any age with MYCN 
amplified tumours with INSS stages 2–4. Any 
responding 
metastatic 
relapse 
in 
patients 
>18  months and any MYCN amplified tumour 
without prior HDT/HCT are suitable indications. 
Any other indication is reserved for well-designed 
experimental phase I/phase II trials. Children 
<18 months need to be evaluated for a high-risk 
biological risk profile prior to being considered 
for HDT/auto-HCT (Canete et  al. 2009; 
Ladenstein et al. 2023; Moroz et al. 2011; Cohn 
et al. 2009). Immunotherapy-related approaches 
including recent haploidentical HCT and third 
generations CART cell approaches hold promise 
for patients advanced relapsed and refractory 
disease.
94.2.3	 Ewing Sarcomas (EWS)
Ewing sarcomas (EWS) are solid tumours of the 
bone and soft tissue that usually affect children, 
adolescents and young adults. An incidence rate 
of 4.5 per million a year is reported, with a peak 
incidence of 11 per million at the age of 12 years. 
Metastatic disease is detected in about 20–30% 
and is typically found in the lungs, bone, bone 
marrow or a combination of these. Presence of 
metastatic disease at diagnosis (primary meta­
static disease) is the most important adverse 
prognostic factor and is associated with a 5-year 
survival lower than 30%. The hypothesis is that 
HDC regimens may overcome the resistance to 
standard multidrug chemotherapy and improve 
survival rates. Despite more intensive chemother­
apy, 30–40% of young people with Ewing sar­
coma will have recurrence of the disease. Less 
than 30% of young people with a recurrence of 
EWS are alive at 24 months, and less than 10% 
are alive at 48 months (Haveman et al. 2021).
94.2.3.1	
Autologous HCT in EWS
For primary disseminated multifocal EWS 
(Ladenstein et  al. 2010) receiving BU/MEL 
HDT/auto-HCT after VIDE induction (Euro-­
EWING 99 study group), an increased risk at 
diagnosis was observed for patients ≥14  years 
(HR  =  1.6), with a primary tumour volume 
>200 mL (HR = 1.8), more than one bone meta­
static site (HR = 2.0), BM metastases (HR = 1.6) 
and additional lung metastases (HR = 1.5), carry. 
A score based on these factors identified patients 
with an EFS rate of 50% for scores ≤3 (82 
patients), 25% for a score >3 and ≤5 (102 
patients) and 10% for score ≥5 (70 patients; 
p < 0.0001). In Ewing2008R3, the effect of treo­
sulfan and melphalan (TreoMel) HDT/HCT was 
investigated in patients with disseminated EWS 
with metastases to bone and/or other sites, 
excluding patients with only pulmonary metasta­
ses (Koch et  al. 2022). Additionally, TreoMel-­
HDT was of no benefit for the entire cohort of 
patients, whereas TreoMel-HDT may be of ben­
efit for children age <14 years.
When using standard methodological proce­
dures as expected by Cochrane no evidence from 
RCTs or CCTs to determine the efficacy of HDC 
with AHCT compared to conventional chemo­
therapy was found for patients with primary 
metastases to locations other than the lungs 
(Haveman et al. 2021).
In EWS patients with poor histologic response 
(≥10% viable cells) after VIDE induction (6 
courses) or large tumour volume at diagnosis 
(≥200  mL), the risk of event was significantly 
decreased by BU/MEL compared to VAI with 
better EFS and OS.  For this group of patients, 
BU/MEL is now a standard of care (Euro-­
EWING 99 study group (Whelan et al. 2018).
In contrast, the R2Pulm trial of the Euro-­
EWING 99 study group and EWING 2008 ran­
domised 
busulfan–melphalan 
HDT/HCT 
(BuMel) in comparison with standard chemo­

therapy with whole lung irradiation (WLI) in 
EWS presenting with pulmonary and/or pleural 
metastases (Dirksen et  al. 2019). There was a 
clear benefit from BuMel compared with conven­
tional VAI plus WLI which in addition was asso­
ciated with less toxicity.
A retrospective study addressed the important 
question of compatibility of BU/MEL and whole 
lung irradiation (WLI) and found WLI at recom­
mended doses and time interval after BU/MEL 
feasible (Abate et al. 2021).
A recent analysis on R/R EWS patients under­
pinned a role of HDT/HCT in 196 patients with 
64 patients receiving HDT, 98 standard non-HDT 
chemotherapy and 34 no systemic therapy 
(Windsor et al. 2022).
However, a survey on patients with a first 
recurrence of EWS in children, adolescents, and 
young adults found no informative data from ran­
domized controlled trials (RCTs) or (historical) 
controlled clinical trials (CCTs), so no conclu­
sions may be drawn (Haveman et al. 2021).
94.2.3.2	
Allogeneic HCT in EWS
Tandem HDT and allo-HCT were part of the 
EICESS92 and Meta-EICESS protocols yielding 
long-term DFS in patients with advanced EWS 
(Burdach and Jürgens 2002).
Patients suffering a relapse generally have a 
poor prognosis with conventional chemotherapy. 
The role of HDT/auto-HCT still awaits 
­clarification in randomized controlled studies 
(Tenneti et al. 2018; Ferrari et al. 2015). A GvT 
or improved survival following allo-HCT effect 
was highlighted in some reports, but a retrospec­
tive review (Thiel et al. 2011) could not identify 
benefits with either RIC or MAC or with either 
HLA-­matched 
or 
HLA-mismatched 
grafts. 
Haplo-HCT for consolidation after conventional 
therapy seems to be of interest for some, but not 
for most patients with high-risk paediatric sarco­
mas (Eichholz et al. 2023; Sano et al. 2022).
94.2.3.3	
Recommended Indications 
in EWS
BU/MEL HDT for patients with a poor histologi­
cal response after induction and/or a tumour vol­
ume ≥200 mL is now standard of care. Patients 
with primary metastatic disease at sites other 
than the lungs and a low-risk score may be con­
sidered good candidates in the absence of a con­
trolled trial. Any metastatic relapse without prior 
HDT may be considered for controlled phase II 
HDT protocols. Adoptive immunotherapy is an 
evolving field and subject to experimental early 
trials.
94.2.4	 Soft Tissue Sarcoma (STS)
Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is the most common 
soft tissue sarcoma (STS) in childhood. Whereas 
more than 90% of patients with localized low-­
risk RMS can be cured, metastatic RMS have a 
dismal outcome, with survival rates of less than 
30%.
94.2.4.1	
Recommended Indications
Currently there is no evidence-based standard 
indication for HDT/HCT in STS.
94.2.5	 Osteosarcoma (OS)
Even in responding high-risk patients treated 
with HDT/HCT in first or second remission, the 
length of remission is short, and relapse occurs 
early after HDT. High-risk features include poor 
histological response or non-response of the pri­
mary tumour at the time of definitive surgery, 
inoperable, axial tumours (large volume), pri­
mary dissemination or relapse other than iso­
lated, late lung metastases.
94.2.5.1	
Recommended Indications 
in OS
There is no standard indication for HCT based on 
published results or EBMT data.
94.2.6	 Retinoblastoma (RB)
Retinoblastoma (RB) is the most frequent intra­
ocular malignancy in children, with the incidence 
rate of 1 per 17,000–24,000 live births. Delayed 
time to diagnosis may lead to the development of

locally advanced or metastatic disease associated 
with poor survival, especially when CNS metas­
tasis is present. Chemotherapy drugs that may be 
useful for these patients include platinum-­
containing agents (carboplatin and cisplatin), 
etoposide, vincristine, cisplatin, cyclophospha­
mide and anthracyclines.
94.2.6.1	
Recommended Indications 
in RB
Advocated HDT/auto-HCT approaches are 
CARBOPEC (CBP, VP, CY) (Jaradat et al. 2012), 
but for CNS-positive patients, TT or BU was 
introduced (Dunkel et  al. 2010). Other groups 
used combinations including MEL and CBDCA 
and/or VP for metastatic RB and reported prom­
ising survival results for patients without CNS 
involvement. Future trials should take the follow­
ing high-risk factors into consideration: involve­
ment of the cut end or subarachnoidal space of 
the optic nerve after enucleation, orbital involve­
ment and distant metastatic disease and CNS 
disease.
94.2.7	 Wilms’ Tumour (WT)
Wilms tumour (WT) treatment regimens are 
curative for more than 80% of patients, but those 
with relapsed or refractory disease continue to 
have poor outcomes. HDT-autologous aHCT 
­rescue is often utilized although outcomes remain 
variable. So far attempts to conduct a randomized 
trial comparing maintenance chemotherapy with 
consolidation versus HDT/auto-HCT have failed 
in this indication.
94.2.7.1	
Recommended Indications 
in WT
Experience of the SIOP, GPOH, NWTS, MRC 
and respective national groups over the last 
20 years found the probability of cure of 30% at 
best in the presence of adverse prognostic fac­
tors. High-risk factors are unfavourable histology 
and metastatic disease (Presson et  al. 2010; 
Delafoy et al. 2022; Groenendijk et al. 2022) and 
are after relapse again unfavourable histology 
and one of the following criteria: extra-­pulmonary 
relapse or abdominal relapse after radiation, 
stage IV, more than two drugs in the first-line 
regimen or relapse within 1 year. HDT is indi­
cated if a response to second-line treatment is 
achieved.
94.2.8	 Recommended Indications 
in Brain Tumours
Patients with high-risk medulloblastoma (pri­
mary metastases/relapse) of any age older than 
3 years are eligible for HDT/HCT in combination 
with radiation, while in infants HDT/HCT is used 
with the aim of reducing (volumes and doses) or 
avoiding radiation.
Metastatic PNETs at diagnosis or with addi­
tional high-risk features such as incomplete 
resection or young age (younger than 3 or 5 years) 
as well as infants and young children (<4 years) 
with malignant brain tumours are further 
indications.
Very controversial indications include high-­
grade glioma. Currently, there is little or no indi­
cation for HDT/HCT in ependymoma, brain stem 
glioma or pineoblastoma. More investigations 
are required to define the optimal HDT for each 
tumour type. Most groups use similar HDT regi­
mens, i.e. BU/TT (SFOP, Spain), VP/TT/CBDCA 
(US/CCG, Germany, Spain) or a tandem approach 
Vp16/CBDCA—TTP/L-PAM (Italy).
94.2.9	 Extra and Intracranial Germ 
Cell Tumours
CNS germ cell tumours (GCTs) can be divided 
into major groups including germinomas (having 
a superior prognosis) and non-germinomatous 
GCTs (NGGCTs), with teratomas often consid­
ered a separate category- and represent approxi­
mately 3% of primary paediatric brain tumours.
94.2.9.1	
Recommended Indications 
in in Germ Cell Tumours
As paediatric patients with extracranial GCTs 
may expect an excellent outcome with conven­
tional chemotherapy approaches, there is no stan­

dard indication for HDT/AHCT.  Based on 
previously published reports on adults, or the few 
reports for children, treatment with HDT com­
bined with aHCT has a beneficial effect on R/R 
GCTs. However, the strategy of HDCT used as a 
frontline treatment has no demonstrated benefit 
for children in the poor-risk group and requires 
further research.
High-risk patients with extracranial GCTs are 
initial non-responders or poor responders (no 
local control achieved) and patients after relapse 
failing to achieve second CR.
In high-risk CNS GCT patients <18 years, the 
following criteria for HDT may be adopted: 
recurrent CNS GCT when biological remission is 
achieved prior to HDC and insufficient response 
to primary chemotherapy.
Since carboplatin and etoposide have been 
included in the front-line chemotherapy of paedi­
atric GCTs, other drug combinations should be 
considered for conditioning regimens, such as 
melphalan, thiotepa, or paclitaxel. The treatment 
of paediatric poor-risk GCTs is still a challenge 
for paediatric oncologists. HDCT combined with 
AHCT in this group of patients requires further 
study.
Key Points for Solid Tumours in Children and 
Adolescents
•	 In neuroblastoma and Ewing sarcoma, 
there is clear evidence for the advantage 
of HDT/auto-HCT with an increasing 
interest in tandem transplants.
•	 In other paediatric solid tumour, indica­
tion still lacks randomized trials, and 
indications are based on observational 
studies, case reports and EBMT data­
base only.
94.3	
Solid Tumours in Adults
Paolo Pedrazzoli, Giovanni Rosti.
94.3.1	 Auto-HCT in Adults
­
­
­
­
94.1
2015
2022
94.3.1.1	
Breast Cancer (BC)
The role of intensified chemotherapy with auto-­
HCT for primary BC at high risk of recurrence 
(at least four involved axillary lymph nodes) has 
been assessed by several randomized trials, eval­
uated by a meta-analysis of individual patient 
data (Berry et al. 2011a; Pedrazzoli et al. 2015). 
Overall, it was shown that auto-HCT prolonged 
DFS when used as adjuvant therapy and showed 
a benefit on BC-specific survival and OS in 
selected cohorts of patients (Nitz et  al. 2005; 
Pedrazzoli et al. 2015). Whether auto-HCT has 
benefits in the context of contemporary targeted 
therapies is largely unknown.
In the metastatic setting, seven phase III stud­
ies have been published in peer-reviewed jour­
nals. Most of these trials showed improved PFS 
in the auto-HCT arm, but only one OS advantage. 
Six randomized trials, including 866 metastatic 
breast cancer (MBC) patients, have been ana­
lyzed in the parallel meta-analysis of individual 
patient data (Berry et al. 2011b) showing a sig­
nificant improvement in PFS, but no improve­
ment in OS.

Overall, based on the randomized studies so 
far, meta-analyses and retrospective studies, 
auto-HCT may still represent a therapeutic option 
for younger patients harbouring HER2-negative 
tumours and having gross involvement of axillary 
nodes (adjuvant setting) or highly chemo sensi­
tive disease (advanced setting) (Martino et  al. 
2016, 2022).
A recent update (20 years) of the Dutch trial 
(Steenbruggen 2020) on 885 patients below 
56 years of age did provide improved statistically 
significant overall survival in very high-risk 
patients (i.e. with ≥10 involved axillary lymph 
nodes) compared to standard adjuvant therapy. 
High-dose chemotherapy did not affect the long-­
term risk of a second malignant neoplasm or 
major cardiovascular events.
94.3.1.2	
Germ Cell Tumours (GCTs)
Auto-HCT is not recommended as first-line ther­
apy in GCT.
In relapsed GCT, high-dose chemotherapy 
(HDCT) is considered a therapeutic option, espe­
cially when poor prognostic factors are present 
(Lorch et al. 2011; Necchi et al. 2015; De Giorgi 
et al. 2017a, b). In this setting, a randomized trial 
(Tiger study) comparing conventional-dose ther­
apy with high-dose therapy has recently (2023) 
completed its accrual of over 400 patients world­
wide, but results are not available yet. Auto-HCT 
is a standard of care for patients that are (primar­
ily) refractory to platinum-based chemotherapy 
or for those with a second or further relapse 
(Necchi et al. 2015). Multiple intensified cycles 
with carboplatin and etoposide are recommended 
as the standard conditioning regimen for GCT 
also due to concerns that using a three-drug regi­
men would require dose reductions of the two 
most active drugs in this disease (Einhorn et al. 
2007; Feldman et al. 2010).
Furthermore, auto-HCT can be safely admin­
istered in high-risk patients older than 45 years. 
However, since the prognosis is poorer for older 
patients with non-seminoma histology, a compre­
hensive risk–benefit evaluation should include 
co-morbidities and the patient’s risk category.
The assessment of a large series of EBMT 
centers, including 46 cases with pure seminoma, 
seems to support the notion that auto-HCT may 
represent a valuable therapeutic option after fail­
ure of standard-dose chemotherapy in this patient 
category (Necchi et al. 2017).
Both HDCT with peripheral blood stem cell 
transplant and conventional-dose chemotherapy 
(CDCT) are recommended treatment options for 
relapsed GCTs. Consistently reported cure rates 
from phase II and large retrospective studies sup­
port the use of HDCT in the hands of an experi­
enced team of oncologists (Adra et  al. 2017; 
Chovanec 2023).
The role of auto-HCT in the mediastinal non-­
seminoma (MnS) GCT disease category is under 
evaluation due to the rarity of the disease. Data 
from the EBMT confirmed that the MnS was 
characterized by the poorest outcome with 5-year 
OS ranging from 40 to 45% (Rosti et al. 2019). 
The use of auto-HCT as both early intensification 
and at disease recurrence proved to be effective, 
given upfront and may produce a 15–20% abso­
lute improvement in survival compared with 
standard-dose CT (Bokemeyer et al. 2002, 2003; 
De Giorgi et al. 2005). The EBMT is currently 
conducting a registry-based retrospective inter­
national study on primary mediastinal GCTs.
94.3.1.3	
Soft Tissue Sarcoma (STS)
STS accounts for about 1% of adult cancers. 
Based on the observation of a dose–response cor­
relation for some drugs used in STS, e.g., DOX 
and IFO, HDT with auto-HCT has been investi­
gated in some, mostly non-randomized phase II 
trials. Most of these trials found few patients to 
possibly benefit from auto-HCT but, owing to the 
small patient numbers of each of the included 
histologic subgroups, they could not establish 
robust markers for identifying these patients.
A recent large retrospective analysis from the 
EBMT Registry (Heilig et al. 2020) found no evi­
dence for a clear benefit of auto-HCT in STS but, 
again, did not sufficiently report on outcomes in 
the different histologic subgroups. However, con­
sidering that the current WHO classification dif­
ferentiates more than 50 histological subtypes of 
STS, it might be hypothesized that clinical 
response to auto-HCT may vary significantly 
depending on the histological differentiation.

94.3.1.4	
Other Solid Tumours
Data from randomized phase III studies compar­
ing HDCT vs. CDC for first-line treatment of 
advanced ovarian cancer and limited or extensive 
small-cell lung cancer have shown no statistically 
significant difference in PFS or OS (Pedrazzoli 
et al. 2006). Limitations due to study design, dif­
ficulty in recruitment and toxicity may have 
accounted for the lack of favourable results that 
were expected based on previous phase II and ret­
rospective analyses of such highly chemo-­
sensitive diseases.
In other chemo-sensitive histologies, includ­
ing Ewing/PNET and certain CNS tumours, data 
regarding auto-HCT in adult patients are limited, 
again based on clinical trials without randomiza­
tion and retrospective analyses. For this reason, 
auto-HCT cannot be recommended as a standard 
of care. High-dose therapy can be regarded as a 
potential clinical option in selected adult and 
AYA (adult young adolescents) patients harbour­
ing paediatric tumours including Ewing’s sar­
coma and medulloblastoma (Haveman et  al. 
2021; Spreafico et al. 2005).
94.3.2	 Allo-HCT in Adults
Immune therapy for cancer is being pursued with 
extraordinary interest by researchers all over the 
world, given the recent scientific acquisitions on 
immune mechanisms that control cancer and the 
introduction in the marketplace of checkpoint 
inhibitor molecules, such as nivolumab/pembro­
lizumab (PD-1/PDL-1 inhibitors) and ipilim­
umab (anti-CTLA4). The paradigm for immune 
therapy of cancer is allo-HCT, whose therapeutic 
effect is carried out by immunocompetent T cells 
of the donor, an effect known graft-versus-tumour 
effect (GvT). Several studies of allo-HCT in 
selected solid tumours, namely, renal cell cancer 
(RCC), ovarian cancer, BC, colorectal cancer and 
others, with some evidence of GvT and occur­
rence of transplant-related toxicities, mostly 
GvHD have been reported. In RCC, a long-term 
survival effect in a fraction (20%) of patients was 
documented. Since 2004, when molecularly tar­
geted drugs were introduced into the clinic for 
renal cell cancer, patient referral for transplants 
dropped precipitously, and transplant rate evalua­
tion for solid tumours from 2009 was limited to a 
few patients in Europe.
A survey provided a picture of the status of 
allo-HCT for solid tumours in EBMT centres 
(Bregni et al. 2016). In contrast to our expecta­
tions, allo-HCT for solid tumour indications has 
been nearly abandoned in adults and can be pro­
posed only within clinical trials.
94.3.3	 Cell Therapy in Solid Tumours 
in Adults
Despite the encouraging success of industry-­
manufactured chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T 
cell therapy in haematology, clinical trials with 
advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMP) 
face unique challenges in solid tumours because 
of the immunosuppressive tumour microenviron­
ment, the hurdle of T-cell trafficking and infiltra­
tion into scarcely accessible tumour sites and 
difficulties in identifying targetable antigens with 
optimal expression and a good toxicity profile 
(Comoli et al. 2019; Maher and Davies 2023). In 
addition, due to the variety of programs and 
infrastructures involved in ATMP manufacturing 
and delivery, the availability of information on 
ongoing studies in ST is limited (Comoli et al. 
2023).
Currently, while waiting for breakthrough cel­
lular products to treat ST, cellular therapy pro­
grams in solid tumours in adults can be offered 
only within clinical trials.
Key Points
•	 The benefit of auto-HCT in solid 
tumours of the adults, with the possible 
exception of selected high risk (more 
than 10 positive axillary nodes) and 
metastatic breast cancer patients and 
germ cell tumours in second or subse­
quent lines, is still unsettled.
•	 Despite the great potential, cell therapy 
programs, including allogeneic trans­

plant for cancer control still have a mar­
ginal, if any, role in the management of 
patients with solid tumours. This issue 
should be regarded as a priority for 
medical oncology and cell therapy/
transplantation societies also in view of 
the recent development of immune 
checkpoint inhibitors that represent a 
major breakthrough in cancer treatment 
and may well be incorporated into cell 
therapy programs.
•	 The story of HCT in solid tumours dem­
onstrates the importance of adopting an 
internationally coordinated approach to 
the investigation of this treatment 
modality. There needs to be an increased 
emphasis on prospective trials that are 
statistically robust and have well-­
defined criteria for patient selection. 
Only these will be able to demonstrate 
whether HCT, alone or incorporated 
into programs with novel therapeutic 
modalities, is worthwhile in patients for 
whom conventional treatments have 
often limited impact on survival.

zh: 實體腫瘤的 HCT 與細胞治療
points: 兒童高風險 neuroblastoma 有 HDT／auto-HCT 的重要證據；其他腫瘤需分病種與治療情境。
Ewing sarcoma 的高劑量治療效益受風險群與方案影響，不能把所有病期視為同等適應症。
成人 germ-cell tumors 的 auto-HCT 主要在復發／難治的高劑量化療救援，不是所有初診一律使用。
成人乳癌與其他實體腫瘤的移植角色較受限，需按證據、風險與試驗情境判斷。
CAR-T 在實體腫瘤面臨抗原異質性、微環境與 trafficking 等限制。
question: 為何實體腫瘤的 auto-HCT 常稱為 stem-cell rescue？
answer: 主要作用是讓病人承受高劑量化療後恢復造血，不能把效益解釋為異體移植的 GVL。
trap: 兒童／成人、腫瘤種類與初治／救援需分開比較。
fullTranslationText:
【第94章：實體腫瘤】作者：Ruth Ladenstein、Paolo Pedrazzoli、Giovanni Rosti。〔94.1 導論〕缺少前瞻性隨機試驗時，EBMT 登錄庫是評估實體腫瘤自體／異體 HCT 適應症、結果與臨床風險的重要資料來源。截至 2022 年底，共 47,221 名實體腫瘤患者接受 65,586 次 HCT，成人略多於兒童（58%／42%）；97% 為自體、3% 異體，約三分之一接受多次移植。表94.1及圖94.1、94.2比較成人與兒童的活動與適應症。
【作者任職機構】R. Ladenstein：St. Anna Children’s Hospital、Children’s Cancer Research Institute（CCRI）／Medical University of Vienna，Vienna；ruth.ladenstein@ccri.at。P. Pedrazzoli：IRCCS Fondazione Policlinico San Matteo，Department of Oncology，以及 University of Pavia，Department of Internal Medicine and Medical Therapy，Pavia；p.pedrazzoli@smatteo.pv.it。G. Rosti：IRCCS Fondazione Policlinico San Matteo，Department of Oncology，Pavia；g.rosti@smatteo.pv.it。【表94.1；2023年2月資料】患者47,221；成人／兒童58%／42%；男／女48%／52%；自體／異體97%／3%。自體 n=63,592、異體 n=1,981：首次45,997／1,221；第二次12,124／577；第三次4,470／134；第四次746／34；第五次以上210／1。2020年前病例中位追蹤，自體3.49年（<1–39），異體2.98年（<1–37）。原表總移植數印為「65,0586」，前文為65,586；數字依原位置保留，未自行重算或修訂。
【圖94.1】EBMT 2012–2022 年實體腫瘤自體 HCT 登錄，共17,850次；比較成人與兒童，資料截至2023年2月。圖例 <18／≥18 為年齡組，縱軸為自體移植次數；腫瘤類別為 germ-cell tumour、neuroblastoma、medulloblastoma、Ewing、breast、sarcoma、ovarian 及其他。各柱狀數值以原圖為準。
【圖94.2】EBMT 1990–2022 年成人與兒童實體腫瘤自體 HCT 次數；2022年僅部分資料。橫軸為年份，縱軸為自體移植次數，圖例分為 <18 及 ≥18 歲。
〔94.2 兒童與青少年實體腫瘤；Ruth Ladenstein〕以下回顧該年文獻的新發展。至今，高劑量治療（HDT）／HCT 的前瞻性隨機證據，仍主要限於高風險 neuroblastoma 與 Ewing sarcoma（Matthay 等，2009；Whelan 等，2018）。
〔94.2.1 EBMT 資料的一般啟示〕【TRM】隨時間明顯下降，與 HDT 方案改變，例如淘汰 TBI，及尤其是周邊血幹細胞使用有關。自體移植 TRM 在1992年後低於5%，2012年以來約1%。
【TBI】在任何兒童實體腫瘤適應症均未顯示優勢，考慮晚期效應應避免使用。
【緩解狀態】第一線高風險患者的結果，顯著優於復發後才接受治療者。
所有適應症的 HDT／HCT 前誘導反應都極重要。高風險但對第一線反應良好（CR／VGPR／PR），或化學敏感復發者，是較合適情境；僅穩定或輕微反應（<50%，SD／MR）者，只應納入定義明確的第一／二期試驗。無反應、腫瘤進展或難治者，即使 HDT／HCT 後預期存活仍很短，因此不應考慮。
年齡是重要預後因素。
青少年通常結果較差。Ewing 與 rhabdomyosarcoma 的有利界線為 <10歲，NBL 則較早，為5歲。診斷時 ≤18個月的 NBL，須做生物風險分析，僅有高風險特徵、特別是 MYCN amplification 才符合資格（Canete 等，2009；Ladenstein 等，2023）。
【雙次移植】EBMT 的 tandem／重複 HDT 資料未顯示優於單次，但第二期研究常選入預後特差者，可能有偏差。相反，NBL 的隨機試驗顯示，第一線高風險患者 tandem 策略較佳（Park 等，2016）。
【BU／MEL】在 EBMT 資料庫中，這是唯一與 NBL 及 Ewing 腫瘤存活顯著改善相關的 HDT 組合。
【異體 HCT】EBMT 未發現任何兒童實體腫瘤適應症的 allo-HCT 優勢，但必須考慮特別差預後者被選入的負向選擇偏差。
EBMT 資料顯示，診斷超過12個月才復發、先前未做 HDT，且對救援治療有反應者，可從 HDT／HCT 獲益。
〔94.2.2 神經母細胞瘤（NBL）〕第一線高風險 NBL 包括 >18個月、廣泛疾病者；若 MYCN amplification，則任何年齡及分期亦可屬高風險（Cohn 等，2009；Moroz 等，2011；Canete 等，2009；Ladenstein 等，2023）。ALK 克隆性變異及擴增，亦為較差存活的獨立預測因子（Bellini 等，2021；Goldsmith 等，2023）。ALK inhibitors，尤其第三代 lorlatinib，越來越常整合到第一線，提高移植前反應。
標準治療包括多療程密集誘導；近期隨機試驗評估結合免疫治療。局部控制主要為原發病灶廣泛手術，加上 HDT／auto-HCT 後放療；部分合作團隊亦照射轉移部位。使用 ch14.18 類抗體的免疫維持，已被視為標準（Park 等，2016；Yu 等，2010；Ladenstein 等，2017、2018）。
〔94.2.2.1 NBL 自體 HCT〕三項隨機試驗及一項統合分析，顯示 HDT／自體移植改善高風險 NBL 的 EFS（Pritchard 等，2005；Berthold 等，2005；Matthay 等，2009；Yalçin 等，2013），但最佳 HDT 方案仍無共識。EBMT 與 HR-NBL1／SIOPEN 支持 BU／MEL（Ladenstein 等，2008、2017）；COG ANBL0532 則顯示雙次移植優於單次 CEM：第一次 CY／TT，第二次 CBP／VP／MEL（較單次 CEM 減量）。兩組均可受益於 anti-GD2 免疫治療（Park 等，2019；Yu 等，2010）。包含 BU／MEL 的 tandem 價值，正在 HR-NBL2／SIOPEN 隨機試驗評估。
MYCN-amplified NBL 的嬰幼兒近期分析，顯示 HR-NBL1／SIOPEN 中結果明顯改善（Ladenstein 等，2023）。
標靶放射療法，尤其 ¹³¹I-mIBG，可單用或合併化療、vorinostat 等放射增敏劑，及／或 HDT 後 HCT，受到越來越多關注（Lee 等，2017；Johnson 等，2011；Ferry 等，2018；Kraal 等，2017、2019；DuBois 等，2021）。
COG、SIOPEN 的隨機研究及其他團隊非隨機試驗，正探索有／無 mIBG 的其他 tandem HDT 策略（Lee 等，2017）。
〔94.2.2.2 NBL 異體 HCT〕其角色仍有爭議。
RIC／NMA 發展後，allo-HCT 作為免疫治療再次受重視。部分報告提示 GVT，但早期 EBMT 傳統異體移植未見益處（Ladenstein 等，1994）。CIBMTR 回顧顯示，未曾 auto-HCT 者可能獲益（Hale 等，2013）；日本 JCCG 也報告較佳結果（Hara 等，2022）。
極高風險 R/R 患者的 haplo-HCT 可誘發長期緩解（Illhardt 等，2018）。Haplo 移植可利用 NK 細胞毒性，以及 anti-GD2 dinutuximab beta（DB）活化，產生抗 NBL 效應（Flaadt 等，2023）。Haplo 後免疫治療可行，GVHD 風險低，長期存活明顯改善，可能源自供者效應細胞增強的抗腫瘤活性。
〔94.2.2.3 NBL 細胞治療〕Anti-GD2 成功證實免疫治療可對 NBL 有效。CAR-T 有望進一步提升效果；早期試驗證明安全可行，但療效仍有障礙。CAR 結合抗體特異性與 T 細胞殺傷力，不依賴 MHC；困難包括 T 細胞持續性／效力不足、靶點難找，以及免疫抑制微環境。結果雖鼓舞但仍有限：只有部分患者有可量測反應，極少數能長期維持 CAR-T（Yang 等，2017；Yeku 等，2017；Pinto 等，2018；Richards 等，2018；Heczey 等，2017）。
針對腫瘤 GD2 的第三代 GD2-CART01，另表現 inducible caspase-9 suicide gene，可能成為 R/R 晚期高風險 NBL 新機會（Del Bufalo 等，2023）。
〔94.2.2.4 NBL–HCT 建議適應症〕標準包括診斷時 >18個月、廣泛轉移的第一線高風險 NBL，或任何年齡、INSS 2–4期、MYCN-amplified 腫瘤。>18個月患者對治療有反應的轉移復發，以及未曾 HDT／HCT 的 MYCN-amplified 腫瘤，也可為合適適應症。
其他情境限於設計良好的第一／二期試驗。<18個月者須先評估是否有高風險生物特徵，再考慮 HDT／auto-HCT（Canete 等，2009；Ladenstein 等，2023；Moroz 等，2011；Cohn 等，2009）。近期 haplo 與第三代 CAR-T 等免疫策略，對晚期復發難治病人有希望。
〔94.2.3 Ewing sarcoma（EWS）〕EWS 是骨或軟組織腫瘤，多見於兒童、青少年、年輕成人。年發生率約每百萬4.5例，12歲最高約每百萬11例。
約20–30% 有轉移，常在肺、骨、骨髓或其組合。初診轉移是最重要不良預後因子，五年存活 <30%。HDC 的假說是克服標準多藥化療抗性、改善存活。即使更密集治療，30–40% 仍復發；復發後24個月存活 <30%，48個月 <10%（Haveman 等，2021）。
〔94.2.3.1 EWS 自體 HCT〕Euro-EWING99 的初診播散多灶 EWS，接受 VIDE 後 BU／MEL HDT／移植。初診不利因子包括 ≥14歲（HR1.6）、原發腫瘤 >200 mL（HR1.8）、多於一處骨轉移（HR2.0）、骨髓轉移（HR1.6）及合併肺轉移（HR1.5）（Ladenstein 等，2010）。
依這些因素評分：≤3分的82人，EFS50%；>3且≤5分的102人，25%；≥5分的70人，10%（p<0.0001；區間依原文保留）。Ewing2008R3 評估 TREO／MEL 於骨及／或其他部位轉移、但排除僅肺轉移者；整體未獲益，但 <14歲可能受益（Koch 等，2022）。
以 Cochrane 標準方法回顧，對初診肺外轉移者，沒有足以比較 HDC＋自體移植與傳統化療療效的 RCT／CCT 證據（Haveman 等，2021）。
六療程 VIDE 後病理反應差（仍 ≥10% 活細胞），或初診腫瘤 ≥200 mL 的 EWS，BU／MEL 相較 VAI 降低事件風險、改善 EFS 與 OS，因此在該群成為標準（Whelan 等，2018）。
相對地，Euro-EWING99／EWING2008 的 R2Pulm，對肺及／或肋膜轉移者，隨機比較 BU／MEL HDT／HCT 與標準 VAI＋全肺照射（WLI）（Dirksen 等，2019）。書中接著寫道：「相較傳統 VAI＋WLI，BuMel 有明確效益；後者另與較低毒性相關。」此處原書敘述與所引試驗結論有出入，請務必閱讀下方獨立譯註。
回顧研究探討 BU／MEL 與 WLI 的相容性，認為在建議劑量與時間間隔下，BU／MEL 後 WLI 可行（Abate 等，2021）。
近期 R/R EWS 分析涵蓋196人：64人 HDT、98人標準非 HDT 化療、34人無全身治療，支持進一步探討 HDT／HCT 的角色（Windsor 等，2022）。
但對兒童、青少年及年輕成人第一次復發的系統調查，沒有具資訊價值的隨機或歷史對照試驗，因此不能下定論（Haveman 等，2021）。
〔94.2.3.2 EWS 異體 HCT〕EICESS92、Meta-EICESS 包含 tandem HDT 與 allo-HCT，使部分晚期 EWS 達長期 DFS（Burdach 與 Jürgens，2002）。
復發者接受傳統化療，通常預後不佳。
HDT／auto-HCT 的角色仍需隨機試驗釐清（Tenneti 等，2018；Ferrari 等，2015）。部分報告提示 allo-HCT 的 GVT 或存活改善，但 Thiel 等（2011）回顧無法確認 RIC／MAC、相合／不相合供者的效益。
傳統治療後以 haplo-HCT 鞏固，可能適用少數、而非多數高風險兒童肉瘤（Eichholz 等，2023；Sano 等，2022）。
〔94.2.3.3 EWS 建議適應症〕誘導後病理反應差及／或腫瘤 ≥200 mL，BU／MEL HDT 已屬標準。初診肺外轉移、風險分數較低者，在缺乏對照試驗時可視為較佳候選。未曾 HDT 的轉移性復發，可考慮有對照的第二期方案；過繼免疫治療仍在早期實驗試驗階段。
〔94.2.4 軟組織肉瘤（STS）〕Rhabdomyosarcoma（RMS）是兒童最常見 STS。局限低風險 RMS 的治癒率 >90%，轉移型存活則 <30%。
〔94.2.4.1 建議適應症〕目前 STS 沒有實證支持的 HDT／HCT 標準適應症。
〔94.2.5 骨肉瘤（OS）〕高風險患者即使在第一或第二次緩解、且已有反應時做 HDT／HCT，緩解仍短且早復發。高風險包括最終手術時病理反應差或無反應、無法切除或大型中軸腫瘤、初診播散，或不是孤立晚發肺轉移的復發。
〔94.2.5.1 建議適應症〕依已發表資料與 EBMT，沒有標準 HCT 適應症。
〔94.2.6 視網膜母細胞瘤（RB）〕RB 是兒童最常見眼內惡性腫瘤，發生率每17,000–24,000名活產一例。延遲診斷可能導致局部晚期或轉移，預後差，尤其 CNS 轉移。可用藥包括 carboplatin／cisplatin、etoposide、vincristine、cyclophosphamide 及 anthracyclines。
〔94.2.6.1 RB 建議適應症〕HDT／auto-HCT 策略包括 CARBOPEC（CBP／VP／CY；Jaradat 等，2012）；CNS 陽性者加入 TT 或 BU（Dunkel 等，2010）。其他 MEL、CBDCA 及／或 VP 組合，對無 CNS 受累的轉移性 RB 有鼓舞存活。未來試驗需考慮：眼球摘除後視神經切緣或蛛網膜下腔受累、眼眶受累、遠處轉移及 CNS 疾病。
〔94.2.7 Wilms tumour（WT）〕現有治療可治癒 >80%，但 R/R 仍預後差。HDT＋自體幹細胞救援常使用，結果不一；此適應症比較維持／鞏固化療與 HDT／auto-HCT 的隨機試驗，迄今未能成功完成。
〔94.2.7.1 WT 建議適應症〕SIOP、GPOH、NWTS、MRC 等團隊過去二十年發現，有不良因素時治癒機率最多約30%。因素包括不利組織型與轉移（Presson 等，2010；Delafoy 等，2022；Groenendijk 等，2022）；復發後則是不利組織型，另合併肺外或照射後腹部復發、第四期、第一線用超過兩種藥、或一年內復發任一條件。若對第二線有反應，可考慮 HDT。
〔94.2.8 腦腫瘤建議適應症〕>3歲高風險 medulloblastoma（初診轉移／復發），可用 HDT／HCT 合併放療；嬰兒則以減少照射體積／劑量或避免放療為目的。
其他情境包括初診轉移 PNET，或不完全切除、<3或5歲等高風險條件，以及 <4歲嬰幼兒惡性腦腫瘤。
High-grade glioma 的適應症極具爭議；ependymoma、brainstem glioma、pineoblastoma 則很少或沒有 HDT／HCT 適應症。需更多研究確定各病型最佳方案。常用 BU／TT（SFOP、西班牙）、VP／TT／CBDCA（美國CCG、德國、西班牙），或 tandem VP16／CBDCA → TT／L-PAM（義大利）。
〔94.2.9 顱內及顱外生殖細胞腫瘤〕CNS GCT 約占兒童原發腦腫瘤3%，主要為預後較佳的 germinoma 與 non-germinomatous GCT（NGGCT），teratoma 常另列一類。
〔94.2.9.1 建議適應症〕兒童顱外 GCT 傳統化療結果很好，沒有標準 HDT／auto-HCT 適應症。依成人及少數兒童報告，HDT＋auto-HCT 可能對 R/R 有益；但對 poor-risk 兒童，第一線即使用 HDCT 尚未證實有益，需更多研究。
顱外 GCT 高風險者，包括初治無反應或反應差、無法局部控制，以及復發後無法達 CR2 者。
<18歲高風險 CNS GCT，可考慮 HDT 的條件包括：復發後在 HDC 前先達生物學緩解，以及對初始化療反應不足。
因兒童 GCT 第一線已含 carboplatin、etoposide，前處理應考慮 MEL、TT 或 paclitaxel 等其他組合。Poor-risk 兒童 GCT 仍很困難，此族群 HDCT＋auto-HCT 需進一步研究。
〔94.3 成人實體腫瘤〕Paolo Pedrazzoli、Giovanni Rosti。
〔94.3.1 成人自體 HCT〕1990年代，基於實驗室理論及早期第二期研究看似令人信服的結果，auto-HCT 未經充分批判便被採納為實體腫瘤潛在治癒策略，使隨機比較高劑量與傳統治療難以進行。因此用於證明或否定效益的研究數量與規模不足，且常未完成。經三十年、數千人研究，除 GCT 及可能的部分乳癌外，其效益仍未定（圖94.1；Sureda 等，2015；Snowden 等，2022）。
〔94.3.1.1 乳癌（BC）〕多項隨機研究評估至少四顆腋下淋巴結受累等高復發風險原發乳癌的強化化療／auto-HCT，並有個別病人資料統合分析（Berry 等，2011a；Pedrazzoli 等，2015）。
整體顯示輔助 auto-HCT 可延長 DFS，特定族群有乳癌特異存活及 OS 益處（Nitz 等，2005；Pedrazzoli 等，2015）；但在現代標靶療法背景下的效益大多未知。
轉移乳癌已有七項同儕審查第三期研究，多數移植組 PFS 改善，但僅一項有 OS 優勢。
六項隨機研究共866名轉移乳癌的個別資料統合分析，顯示 PFS 顯著改善，但 OS 未改善（Berry 等，2011b）。
【兒童與青少年實體腫瘤章末重點】NBL 與 Ewing 有 HDT／auto-HCT 效益的明確證據，對 tandem 策略的興趣增加。
其他兒童實體腫瘤仍缺隨機試驗，適應症主要來自觀察研究、病例與 EBMT 登錄。
綜合現有隨機、統合及回顧資料，auto-HCT 對較年輕、HER2 陰性且腋下淋巴結廣泛受累的輔助治療情境，或高度化學敏感的晚期疾病，仍可能是選項（Martino 等，2016、2022）。
荷蘭試驗885名 <56歲患者的二十年更新，顯示 ≥10顆腋下淋巴結受累的極高風險者，較標準輔助治療有統計顯著 OS 改善（Steenbruggen，2020）。
高劑量化療未改變第二惡性腫瘤或重大心血管事件的長期風險。
〔94.3.1.2 生殖細胞腫瘤（GCT）〕不建議 auto-HCT 作為第一線。
復發 GCT 可考慮 HDCT，尤其有不良預後因素（Lorch 等，2011；Necchi 等，2015；De Giorgi 等，2017a、b）。本書時點，TIGER 隨機比較傳統與高劑量治療，2023年已完成全球逾400人收案，但結果尚未公布。對原發 platinum 難治，或第二次及之後復發，auto-HCT 為標準選項（Necchi 等，2015）。建議多次強化 carboplatin／etoposide 作為 GCT 標準前處理；三藥方案可能迫使這兩種最有效藥減量（Einhorn 等，2007；Feldman 等，2010）。
高風險 >45歲患者，也可安全接受 auto-HCT。
但較年長、non-seminoma 組織型者預後較差，需將共病及風險分類納入完整風險效益評估。
EBMT 多中心含46名 pure seminoma 的資料，支持標準劑量化療失敗後，auto-HCT 可能有價值（Necchi 等，2017）。
復發 GCT 的治療選項同時包括 HDCT＋PBSC 移植及傳統劑量化療。第二期及大型回顧研究一致報告治癒機會，支持由有經驗的腫瘤團隊執行 HDCT（Adra 等，2017；Chovanec，2023）。
縱膈 non-seminoma GCT（MnS）罕見，auto-HCT 角色仍在評估；EBMT 資料中此類預後最差，五年 OS 約40–45%（Rosti 等，2019）。
早期強化或復發時的 auto-HCT 顯示療效；若第一線強化使用，相較標準化療可能增加絕對存活15–20%（Bokemeyer 等，2002、2003；De Giorgi 等，2005）。本書時點 EBMT 正進行原發縱膈 GCT 的國際登錄回顧研究。
〔94.3.1.3 軟組織肉瘤（STS）〕約占成人癌症1%。
DOX、IFO 等藥有劑量反應關係，促成多為非隨機第二期的 HDT／auto-HCT 試驗。部分病人可能獲益，但各組織亞型人數太少，無法建立可靠選人標記。
近期 EBMT 大型回顧也未找到明確效益，且未充分報告各亞型結果（Heilig 等，2020）。WHO 區分超過50種 STS 組織亞型，因此反應可能隨分化類型而大幅不同。
〔94.3.1.4 其他實體腫瘤〕第三期研究比較 HDCT 與傳統化療用於晚期卵巢癌，以及局限或廣泛小細胞肺癌第一線，PFS、OS 均無顯著差異（Pedrazzoli 等，2006）。設計、收案困難與毒性，可能解釋為何未重現先前第二期／回顧研究對這些化學敏感疾病的期待。
成人 Ewing／PNET 及部分 CNS 等化學敏感腫瘤，資料仍少，主要非隨機與回顧，不能推薦 auto-HCT 為標準。選定成人及 AYA 的兒童型腫瘤，如 Ewing、medulloblastoma，可把 HDT 視為潛在 clinical option（Haveman 等，2021；Spreafico 等，2005）。
〔94.3.2 成人異體 HCT〕癌症免疫機轉的進步，以及 nivolumab／pembrolizumab、ipilimumab 等 checkpoint inhibitors 上市，使免疫治療受到極大關注。Allo-HCT 是一種典型免疫治療：供者具免疫能力 T 細胞發揮 GVT。腎細胞癌、卵巢、乳癌、大腸直腸癌等研究，顯示部分 GVT，但也有移植毒性，尤其 GVHD。RCC 約20%患者有長期存活效應。2004年分子標靶藥開始用於 RCC 後，移植轉介驟減；2009年後歐洲實體腫瘤移植評估僅少數患者。
EBMT 中心調查顯示，與原先期待相反，成人實體腫瘤的 allo-HCT 幾乎已被放棄，只應在臨床試驗提出（Bregni 等，2016）。
〔94.3.3 成人實體腫瘤細胞治療〕商業 CAR-T 在血液科雖成功，ATMP 用於實體腫瘤仍面臨獨特困難：抑制性微環境、T 細胞移行與浸潤難以接近的部位，以及難找兼具理想表現與安全性的抗原（Comoli 等，2019；Maher 與 Davies，2023）。製造與提供 ATMP 的計畫及基礎設施多樣，也使實體腫瘤進行中研究資訊有限（Comoli 等，2023）。
在等待突破性細胞產品期間，成人實體腫瘤細胞治療目前僅應在臨床試驗中提供。
【成人章末重點】除部分高風險（>10顆陽性腋下淋巴結）或轉移乳癌，以及第二線以後 GCT 可能例外，成人實體腫瘤 auto-HCT 效益仍未確立。
包括異體移植的細胞療法雖有潛力，在實體腫瘤控制上仍只有邊緣性、甚至沒有角色。腫瘤與移植／細胞治療學會應優先研究此議題，尤其 checkpoint inhibitors 的重大進展，也可能整合進細胞治療。實體腫瘤 HCT 的歷史顯示，必須國際協調研究，增加統計嚴謹、選人標準清楚的前瞻試驗；只有這樣，才能證明 HCT 單用或整合新療法，是否值得用於傳統治療對存活幫助有限的患者。
